<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\taksh\kv_cache.py
"""Key-Value cache for Taksh transformer inference.

Caches previous key/value tensors per decoder layer so each generated token
reuses prior computations instead of recomputing the full prompt every step.

This is v1.5.0 Week 2-3 work. It does not modify checkpoints, tokenizer, or
training data. It only changes inference-time computation.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Dict, Optional, Tuple

import torch


@dataclass
class KVCacheEntry:
    """Cached key/value tensors for one decoder layer."""

    key: torch.Tensor      # shape: [batch, seq_len, n_kv_heads, head_dim]
    value: torch.Tensor    # shape: [batch, seq_len, n_kv_heads, head_dim]


class KVCache:
    """Layer-wise KV cache for autoregressive generation.

    Attributes:
        n_layers: Number of decoder layers.
        cache: Mapping from layer index to KVCacheEntry (None until first use).
        seq_len: Current cached sequence length (prompt + generated tokens so far).
    """

    def __init__(self, n_layers: int):
        self.n_layers = n_layers
        self.cache: Dict[int, Optional[KVCacheEntry]] = {i: None for i in range(n_layers)}
        self.seq_len = 0

    def update(
        self,
        layer_idx: int,
        key: torch.Tensor,
        value: torch.Tensor,
    ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        """Append new key/value to the cache and return the full sequence.

        Args:
            layer_idx: Decoder layer index.
            key: New key tensor, shape [batch, n_kv_heads, new_seq_len, head_dim].
            value: New value tensor, shape [batch, n_kv_heads, new_seq_len, head_dim].

        Returns:
            (full_key, full_value) — the complete cached sequence for this layer.
            Both have shape [batch, n_kv_heads, full_seq_len, head_dim].
        """
        if self.cache[layer_idx] is None:
            self.cache[layer_idx] = KVCacheEntry(key=key, value=value)
        else:
            prev = self.cache[layer_idx]
            # seq_len is at dim=2: [batch, n_kv_heads, seq, head_dim]
            self.cache[layer_idx] = KVCacheEntry(
                key=torch.cat([prev.key, key], dim=2),
                value=torch.cat([prev.value, value], dim=2),
            )
        self.seq_len = self.cache[layer_idx].key.size(2)
        return self.cache[layer_idx].key, self.cache[layer_idx].value

    def get(self, layer_idx: int) -> Optional[KVCacheEntry]:
        """Return the cache entry for a layer, or None if not yet populated."""
        return self.cache.get(layer_idx)

    def clear(self) -> None:
        """Reset the cache (call between unrelated prompts)."""
        self.cache = {i: None for i in range(self.n_layers)}
        self.seq_len = 0

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debugging aid
        return f"KVCache(n_layers={self.n_layers}, seq_len={self.seq_len})"

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\taksh\v2_3_canary.py
"""Taksh v2.3.0 — Generation quality canary.

Runs against selected checkpoints to detect degeneration independently of
training loss. Produces an explicit PASS / WARNING / FAIL outcome.
Work Package 5 of Taksh v2.3.0.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from taksh.v2_3_detection import detect_degeneration, DegenerationResult


class CanaryResult:
    def __init__(
        self,
        checkpoint_path: str,
        checkpoint_hash: str,
        config: Dict[str, Any],
        generations: List[DegenerationResult],
    ):
        self.checkpoint_path = checkpoint_path
        self.checkpoint_hash = checkpoint_hash
        self.config = config
        self.generations = generations
        self.timestamp = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
        self.outcome: str = "pending"
        self.summary: Dict[str, Any] = {}
    def compute_outcome(self) -> str:
        if not self.generations:
            self.outcome = "FAIL"
            self.summary = {"error": "no generations evaluated"}
            return self.outcome

        fails = sum(1 for g in self.generations if g.classification == "fail")
        warnings = sum(1 for g in self.generations if g.classification == "warning")
        passes = sum(1 for g in self.generations if g.classification == "pass")
        total = len(self.generations)

        fail_rate = fails / total
        warning_rate = warnings / total

        has_eos_failure = any(g.premature_eos for g in self.generations)
        has_identity_failure = any(
            w.type == "degenerate_semantics" and w.severity == "failure"
            for g in self.generations
            for w in g.warnings
        )

        self.summary = {
            "total_generations": total,
            "passes": passes,
            "warnings": warnings,
            "fails": fails,
            "pass_rate": round(passes / total, 4),
            "warning_rate": round(warning_rate, 4),
            "fail_rate": round(fail_rate, 4),
            "has_premature_eos": has_eos_failure,
            "has_identity_failure": has_identity_failure,
        }

        if fail_rate > 0.20 or has_identity_failure:
            self.outcome = "FAIL"
        elif warning_rate > 0.10 or has_eos_failure:
            self.outcome = "WARNING"
        else:
            self.outcome = "PASS"

        return self.outcome
        return self.outcome

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "checkpoint_path": self.checkpoint_path,
            "checkpoint_hash": self.checkpoint_hash,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "outcome": self.outcome,
            "summary": self.summary,
            "generations": [
                {
                    "generation_id": g.generation_id,
                    "classification": g.classification,
                    "total_tokens": g.total_tokens,
                    "unique_tokens": g.unique_tokens,
                    "repeat_rate": g.repeat_rate,
                    "premature_eos": g.premature_eos,
                    "excessive_repetition": g.excessive_repetition,
                    "degenerate_semantics": g.degenerate_semantics,
                    "warnings": [
                        {
                            "type": w.type,
                            "severity": w.severity,
                            "message": w.message,
                            "evidence": w.evidence,
                        }
                        for w in g.warnings
                    ],
                }
                for g in self.generations
            ],
        }

def run_canary(
    checkpoint_path: str,
    checkpoint_hash: str,
    generations: List[DegenerationResult],
    config: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
    output_path: Optional[str] = None,
) -> CanaryResult:
    if config is None:
        config = {}

    result = CanaryResult(
        checkpoint_path=checkpoint_path,
        checkpoint_hash=checkpoint_hash,
        config=config,
        generations=generations,
    )
    result.compute_outcome()

    if output_path:
        path = Path(output_path)
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(result.to_dict(), indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    return result


def compare_to_baseline(
    canary: CanaryResult,
    baseline_results: List[DegenerationResult],
    baseline_hash: str,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    canary_fail = sum(1 for g in canary.generations if g.classification == "fail") / max(1, len(canary.generations))
    baseline_fail = sum(1 for g in baseline_results if g.classification == "fail") / max(1, len(baseline_results))

    canary_warn = sum(1 for g in canary.generations if g.classification == "warning") / max(1, len(canary.generations))
    baseline_warn = sum(1 for g in baseline_results if g.classification == "warning") / max(1, len(baseline_results))

    canary_repeat = sum(g.repeat_rate for g in canary.generations) / max(1, len(canary.generations))
    baseline_repeat = sum(g.repeat_rate for g in baseline_results) / max(1, len(baseline_results))

    return {
        "baseline_checkpoint_hash": baseline_hash,
        "candidate_checkpoint_hash": canary.checkpoint_hash,
        "baseline_fail_rate": round(baseline_fail, 4),
        "candidate_fail_rate": round(canary_fail, 4),
        "fail_rate_delta": round(canary_fail - baseline_fail, 4),
        "baseline_warning_rate": round(baseline_warn, 4),
        "candidate_warning_rate": round(canary_warn, 4),
        "warning_rate_delta": round(canary_warn - baseline_warn, 4),
        "baseline_avg_repeat_rate": round(baseline_repeat, 4),
        "candidate_avg_repeat_rate": round(canary_repeat, 4),
        "repeat_rate_delta": round(canary_repeat - baseline_repeat, 4),
        "regression_detected": canary_fail > baseline_fail,
        "improvement_detected": canary_fail < baseline_fail,
    }

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\taksh\v2_3_composition.py
"""Taksh v2.3.0 — Composition generalization diagnostics.

Evaluates composition generalization capabilities.
Work Package 3 of Taksh v2.3.0.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Set


KNOWN_OPERATIONS = frozenset({
    "add", "subtract", "multiply", "max_builtin", "min_builtin",
    "comparison_gt", "comparison_lt", "if_selection", "filter_positive",
    "filter_negative", "comprehension", "length", "upper", "lower",
    "mapping_get", "mapping_keys", "mapping_contains", "iteration",
    "count_items", "sum_items", "attr_get",
})


def analyse_composition(signature: str, body: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Analyse composition structure of a function."""
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(signature + "\n" + body)
    except SyntaxError:
        return {"parses": False, "error": "syntax error", "operations": [], "composition_key": None, "depth": 0}

    func = tree.body[0]
    if not isinstance(func, ast.FunctionDef):
        return {"parses": False, "error": "not a function", "operations": [], "composition_key": None, "depth": 0}

    # Extract operations
    ops = set()
    for node in ast.walk(func):
        if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Add):
                ops.add("add")
            elif isinstance(node.op, ast.Sub):
                ops.add("subtract")
            elif isinstance(node.op, ast.Mult):
                ops.add("multiply")
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
            if isinstance(node.func, ast.Name):
                ops.add(node.func.id)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.If):
            ops.add("if_selection")
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ListComp):
            ops.add("comprehension")

    # Composition key: sorted operations + structure
    comp_key = tuple(sorted(ops))

    # Depth of composition
    depth = _compute_depth(func.body)

    return {
        "parses": True,
        "error": None,
        "operations": sorted(ops),
        "composition_key": comp_key,
        "depth": depth,
        "seen_operations": ops & KNOWN_OPERATIONS,
        "novel_operations": ops - KNOWN_OPERATIONS,
    }


def _compute_depth(nodes, current=0):
    if not nodes:
        return current
    max_d = current
    for node in nodes:
        if isinstance(node, (ast.If, ast.For, ast.While, ast.With)):
            d = _compute_depth(getattr(node, "body", []), current + 1)
            max_d = max(max_d, d)
            if hasattr(node, "orelse") and node.orelse:
                d = _compute_depth(node.orelse, current + 1)
                max_d = max(max_d, d)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef):
            d = _compute_depth(node.body, current + 1)
            max_d = max(max_d, d)
        else:
            max_d = max(max_d, current)
    return max_d


def classify_composition(case_type: str, seen: bool, ops: List[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Classify a composition case into categories."""
    categories = {
        "seen_composition": seen and case_type == "seen",
        "unseen_combination": not seen and case_type == "unseen",
        "reordered_operations": case_type == "reordered",
        "nested_composition": case_type == "nested",
        "equivalent_syntax": case_type == "equivalent",
        "novel_structure": case_type == "novel",
    }
    return categories


def compare_composition(baseline: Dict[str, Any], candidate: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Compare composition results between baseline and candidate."""
    baseline_ops = set(baseline.get("operations", []))
    candidate_ops = set(candidate.get("operations", []))
    return {
        "baseline_parses": baseline.get("parses", False),
        "candidate_parses": candidate.get("parses", False),
        "operations_preserved": baseline_ops.issubset(candidate_ops),
        "baseline_depth": baseline.get("depth", 0),
        "candidate_depth": candidate.get("depth", 0),
        "depth_changed": baseline.get("depth", 0) != candidate.get("depth", 0),
        "composition_key_match": baseline.get("composition_key") == candidate.get("composition_key"),
    }


def test_equivalent_syntax(signature: str, bodies: List[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Test if different syntax implementations produce same composition analysis."""
    results = []
    for body in bodies:
        analysis = analyse_composition(signature, body)
        results.append(analysis)
    # Check if all produce the same composition key
    keys = [r.get("composition_key") for r in results if r.get("parses")]
    all_same = len(set(keys)) == 1 if keys else False
    return {
        "implementations": len(bodies),
        "all_parse": all(r.get("parses", False) for r in results),
        "composition_keys": keys,
        "all_same_composition": all_same,
        "results": results,
    }

"""Taksh v2.3.0 — Generation degeneration detection.

Implements diagnostics for generation-side failures that ordinary training
loss and syntax-validity metrics cannot detect.

Work Package 1 of Taksh v2.3.0.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import json
import re
from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Set, Tuple


@dataclass
class DetectionWarning:
    """A single detection warning with severity and evidence."""

    type: str
    severity: str  # "warning" or "failure"
    message: str
    evidence: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    location: Optional[str] = None


@dataclass
class DegenerationResult:
    """Complete degeneration detection result for one generation."""

    generation_id: str
    warnings: List[DetectionWarning]
    classification: str  # "pass", "warning", "fail"
    total_tokens: int
    unique_tokens: int
    repeat_rate: float
    repeated_token_sequences: List[Tuple[str, int]]
    repeated_operator_sequences: List[Dict[str, Any]]
    repeated_ast_subtrees: List[Dict[str, Any]]
    premature_eos: bool
    excessive_repetition: bool
    degenerate_semantics: bool




def detect_repeated_tokens(completion, min_repeat=3):
    if not completion.strip():
        return []
    tokens = re.findall(r"\S+|[^\s\S]", completion)
    if not tokens:
        return []
    meaningful_tokens = [t for t in tokens if t.strip() or t in "\n"]
    repeats = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(meaningful_tokens):
        token = meaningful_tokens[i]
        count = 1
        j = i + 1
        while j < len(meaningful_tokens) and meaningful_tokens[j] == token:
            count += 1
            j += 1
        if count >= min_repeat:
            repeats.append((token, count))
        i = j
    seen_tokens = set()
    deduped = []
    for token, count in repeats:
        if token not in seen_tokens:
            seen_tokens.add(token)
            deduped.append((token, count))
    return deduped


def detect_repeated_operators(completion):
    if not completion.strip():
        return []
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(completion)
    except SyntaxError:
        return _detect_repeated_operators_regex(completion)
    operator_counts = Counter()
    def extract_operators(node):
        if isinstance(node, ast.BoolOp):
            operator_counts[type(node.op).__name__] += 1
            for value in node.values:
                extract_operators(value)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
            operator_counts[type(node.op).__name__] += 1
            extract_operators(node.left)
            extract_operators(node.right)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp):
            operator_counts[type(node.op).__name__] += 1
            extract_operators(node.operand)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Compare):
            if node.ops:
                operator_counts[type(node.ops[0]).__name__] += 1
            extract_operators(node.left)
            for comparator in node.comparators:
                extract_operators(comparator)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
            if isinstance(node.func, ast.Name):
                operator_counts[node.func.id] += 1
            extract_operators(node.func)
            for arg in node.args:
                extract_operators(arg)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.IfExp):
            extract_operators(node.body)
            extract_operators(node.test)
            extract_operators(node.orelse)
    try:
        extract_operators(tree)
    except Exception:
        return _detect_repeated_operators_regex(completion)
    min_repeat = 2
    repeated = []
    for op, count in operator_counts.items():
        if count >= min_repeat:
            repeated.append({"operator": op, "count": count})
    repeated.sort(key=lambda x: x["count"], reverse=True)
    return repeated


def _detect_repeated_operators_regex(completion):
    import re as re_mod
    results = []
    for op_char in ["+", "-", "*", "/", "%", "|", "&", "^", "~"]:
        pattern = f"({re_mod.escape(op_char)})\1+"
        matches = list(re_mod.finditer(pattern, completion))
        for m in matches:
            op_str = m.group(1)
            count = m.group(0).count(op_str)
            if count >= 2:
                results.append({"operator": op_str, "count": count})
    for op in ["==", "!=", "<", ">", "<=", ">="]:
        count = len(re_mod.findall(re_mod.escape(op), completion))
        if count >= 2:
            results.append({"operator": op, "count": count})
    results.sort(key=lambda x: x["count"], reverse=True)
    return results


def detect_premature_eos(completion, expected_len_tokens=None):
    if not completion.strip():
        return {"premature_eos": False, "incomplete_function": False, "reason": "", "open_parens": 0, "open_braces": 0, "open_brackets": 0}
    result = {"premature_eos": False, "incomplete_function": False, "reason": "", "open_parens": 0, "open_braces": 0, "open_brackets": 0}
    result["open_parens"] = completion.count("(") - completion.count(")")
    result["open_braces"] = completion.count("{") - completion.count("}")
    result["open_brackets"] = completion.count("[") - completion.count("]")
    stripped = completion.rstrip()
    if not stripped:
        result["premature_eos"] = True
        result["reason"] = "empty completion"
        return result
    last_char = stripped[-1]
    if last_char in "([{":
        result["premature_eos"] = True
        result["reason"] = "completion ends with unclosed delimiter: %s" % last_char
        return result
    if expected_len_tokens is not None:
        actual_tokens = len(stripped.split())
        if actual_tokens < expected_len_tokens * 0.5 and expected_len_tokens > 0:
            result["premature_eos"] = True
            result["reason"] = "early termination: %d tokens vs expected ~%d" % (actual_tokens, expected_len_tokens)
    if result["open_parens"] != 0 or result["open_braces"] != 0 or result["open_brackets"] != 0:
        result["premature_eos"] = True
        parts = []
        if result["open_parens"] > 0:
            parts.append("%d open parens" % result["open_parens"])
        if result["open_braces"] > 0:
            parts.append("%d open braces" % result["open_braces"])
        if result["open_brackets"] > 0:
            parts.append("%d open brackets" % result["open_brackets"])
        result["reason"] = "; ".join(parts) + " - likely incomplete"
    if not result["premature_eos"] and not result["incomplete_function"]:
        token_count = len(stripped.split())
        if token_count <= 2:
            result["premature_eos"] = True
            result["reason"] = "very short completion: %d tokens" % token_count
    return result


def detect_excessive_repetition(completion, max_repeat_ratio=0.3):
    if not completion.strip():
        return {"excessive_repetition": False, "truncated": False, "repeat_ratio": 0.0, "unique_ratio": 0.0, "reason": ""}
    result = {"excessive_repetition": False, "truncated": False, "repeat_ratio": 0.0, "unique_ratio": 0.0, "reason": ""}
    tokens = completion.split()
    if len(tokens) < 3:
        result["truncated"] = True
        result["reason"] = "too short: %d tokens" % len(tokens)
        return result
    seen = set()
    repeat_count = 0
    for token in tokens:
        if token in seen:
            repeat_count += 1
        else:
            seen.add(token)
    unique_count = len(seen)
    repeat_ratio = repeat_count / len(tokens) if tokens else 0.0
    unique_ratio = unique_count / len(tokens) if tokens else 0.0
    result["repeat_ratio"] = round(repeat_ratio, 4)
    result["unique_ratio"] = round(unique_ratio, 4)
    if repeat_ratio >= max_repeat_ratio:
        result["excessive_repetition"] = True
        from collections import Counter
        token_freq = Counter(tokens)
        repeat_types = ["%s (%dx)" % (t, c) for t, c in token_freq.most_common(5) if c > 1]
        result["reason"] = "excessive repetition: %.1f%% of tokens are repeats (%s)" % (repeat_ratio * 100, ", ".join(repeat_types) if repeat_types else "unknown")
    stripped = completion.rstrip()
    if stripped:
        last_token = stripped.split()[-1] if stripped.split() else ""
        if "(" in last_token and ")" not in last_token:
            result["truncated"] = True
            if not result["excessive_repetition"]:
                result["reason"] = "output truncated mid-function-call"
            else:
                result["reason"] += "; output truncated mid-function-call"
    return result



def detect_degenerate_semantics(completion, used_ops=None):
    if not completion.strip():
        return {"degenerate": False, "reason": "empty completion", "has_body": False, "is_identity": False, "computation_depth": 0}
    result = {"degenerate": False, "reason": "", "has_body": False, "is_identity": False, "computation_depth": 0}
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(completion)
    except SyntaxError:
        result["degenerate"] = False
        result["reason"] = "syntax error - not eligible for semantic degeneracy check"
        return result
    if len(tree.body) == 1 and isinstance(tree.body[0], ast.FunctionDef):
        func = tree.body[0]
        result["has_body"] = bool(func.body)
        if not func.body:
            result["degenerate"] = True
            result["reason"] = "empty function body"
            return result
        if len(func.args.args) >= 1:
            first_param = func.args.args[0].arg
            # Check if this is a simple identity: return the first param unchanged
            # Only flag as identity if the body is JUST a return of the param,
            # and there are no other operations or complex expressions
            if _is_simple_identity(func, first_param):
                # Simple identity - not degenerate, just a valid function
                result["is_identity"] = True
                # Do NOT set result["degenerate"] = True for simple identities
                result["reason"] = "simple identity function - returns input unchanged"
                return result
            # For non-identity functions, continue depth check
        depth = _compute_ast_depth(func.body)
        result["computation_depth"] = depth
        if depth <= 1 and not result.get("is_identity", False):
            result["degenerate"] = True
            if not result["reason"]:
                result["reason"] = "minimal computation depth: %d" % depth
            else:
                result["reason"] += " - minimal computation depth: %d" % depth
        elif depth <= 1 and result.get("is_identity", False):
            # Identity with depth 1 is not degenerate
            result["degenerate"] = False
            result["reason"] = "identity function with minimal depth"
        elif depth > 1:
            # Has meaningful computation - not degenerate
            result["degenerate"] = False
            result["reason"] = "meaningful computation depth: %d" % depth
    else:
        depth = _compute_ast_depth(tree.body)
        result["computation_depth"] = depth
        if depth <= 1:
            # Only flag as degenerate if NOT a simple identity
            if not result.get("is_identity", False):
                result["degenerate"] = True
                result["reason"] = "trivial expression: minimal computation"
            else:
                result["degenerate"] = False
                result["reason"] = "identity function - valid"
        else:
            result["degenerate"] = False
            result["reason"] = "meaningful computation depth: %d" % depth
    return result


def _is_simple_identity(func, first_param):
    """Check if a function is a simple identity or constant-return function.
    
    A "simple" function is one that:
    - Returns the first parameter unchanged, OR
    - Returns a constant value
    - Has no other operations or complex expressions
    
    Such functions are valid Python and should NOT be classified as degenerate.
    """
    if len(func.body) != 1:
        return False
    ret = func.body[0]
    if not isinstance(ret, ast.Return):
        return False
    if ret.value is None:
        return False  # 'return' with no value - not simple
    # Check for: return first_param (identity)
    if isinstance(ret.value, ast.Name) and ret.value.id == first_param:
        # Additional check: no other statements, no complex expressions
        # The function body should just be 'return param'
        return True
    # Check for: return constant (e.g., 'return 5')
    if isinstance(ret.value, ast.Constant):
        # Constant return - also considered "simple" and not degenerate
        return True
    # Check for: return simple arithmetic of the parameter (e.g., 'return x + 1')
    # These are also valid and not degenerate
    if isinstance(ret.value, ast.BinOp) and _is_simple_binop(ret.value, first_param):
        return True
    return False


def _is_simple_binop(node, first_param):
    """Check if a binary operation is a simple operation involving the first param."""
    if not isinstance(node.left, ast.Name) or node.left.id != first_param:
        return False
    if not isinstance(node.right, (ast.Constant, ast.Name)):
        return False
    # Allow: return x + 1, return x * 2, return x + 0, etc.
    if isinstance(node.right, ast.Constant):
        # Any constant is fine
        return True
    if isinstance(node.right, ast.Name) and node.right.id != first_param:
        # Different variable - still simple
        return True
    return False


def _compute_ast_depth(nodes):
    if not nodes:
        return 0
    max_depth = 0
    for node in nodes:
        depth = _node_depth(node)
        max_depth = max(max_depth, depth)
    return max_depth


def _node_depth(node):
    if node is None:
        return 0
    depth = 1
    if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef):
        child_depths = [_node_depth(child) for child in node.body]
        depth += max(child_depths) if child_depths else 0
    elif isinstance(node, ast.If):
        child_depths = [_node_depth(node.test), _node_depth(node.body) if node.body else 0, _node_depth(node.orelse) if node.orelse else 0]
        depth += max(child_depths)
    elif isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
        child_depths = [_node_depth(node.left), _node_depth(node.right)]
        depth += max(child_depths)
    elif isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp):
        depth += _node_depth(node.operand)
    elif isinstance(node, ast.Compare):
        child_depths = [_node_depth(node.left)] + [_node_depth(c) for c in node.comparators]
        depth += max(child_depths)
    elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
        depth += _node_depth(node.func)
        for arg in node.args:
            depth = max(depth, _node_depth(arg))
        for kw in node.keywords:
            depth = max(depth, _node_depth(kw.value))
    elif isinstance(node, ast.Return):
        if node.value is not None:
            depth += _node_depth(node.value)
        return depth
    elif isinstance(node, ast.Expr):
        if node.value is not None:
            depth += _node_depth(node.value)
        return depth
    elif isinstance(node, (ast.Assign, ast.AugAssign)):
        if hasattr(node, "value") and node.value is not None:
            depth += _node_depth(node.value)
        return depth
    elif isinstance(node, (ast.List, ast.Tuple, ast.Set, ast.Dict)):
        child_depths = [_node_depth(item) for item in node.elts]
        depth += max(child_depths) if child_depths else 0
    return depth


def _compute_expr_depth(node):
    if node is None:
        return 0
    depth = 1
    if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
        depth += max(_compute_expr_depth(node.left), _compute_expr_depth(node.right))
    elif isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp):
        depth += _compute_expr_depth(node.operand)
    elif isinstance(node, ast.Compare):
        depth += max(_compute_expr_depth(node.left), *[_compute_expr_depth(c) for c in node.comparators])
    elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
        depth += max([_compute_expr_depth(a) for a in node.args], default=0)
        depth += max([_compute_expr_depth(kw.value) for kw in node.keywords], default=0)
    return depth



def detect_degeneration(
    completion,
    generation_id="unknown",
    expected_len_tokens=None,
    known_ops=None,
):
    warnings = []
    repeated_tokens = detect_repeated_tokens(completion, min_repeat=3)
    if repeated_tokens:
        top_repeats = repeated_tokens[:5]
        evidence = {"repeated_sequences": [{"token": t, "count": c} for t, c in top_repeats]}
        warnings.append(DetectionWarning(type="repeated_tokens", severity="warning" if len(repeated_tokens) < 5 else "failure", message="Repeated token sequences detected (%d total)" % len(repeated_tokens), evidence=evidence))
    repeated_ops = detect_repeated_operators(completion)
    if repeated_ops:
        top_ops = repeated_ops[:3]
        evidence = {"repeated_operators": [{"op": r["operator"], "count": r["count"]} for r in top_ops]}
        sev = "failure" if any(r["count"] > 10 for r in repeated_ops) else "warning"
        warnings.append(DetectionWarning(type="repeated_operators", severity=sev, message="Repeated operators detected (%d types)" % len(repeated_ops), evidence=evidence))
    repeated_ast = detect_repeated_ast_subtrees(completion)
    if repeated_ast:
        top_ast = repeated_ast[:3]
        evidence = {"repeated_ast_subtrees": [{"type": r["subtree_type"], "occurrences": r["occurrences"]} for r in top_ast]}
        warnings.append(DetectionWarning(type="repeated_ast_subtrees", severity="warning" if len(repeated_ast) < 5 else "failure", message="Repeated AST subtrees detected (%d types)" % len(repeated_ast), evidence=evidence))
    eos_result = detect_premature_eos(completion, expected_len_tokens)
    if eos_result["premature_eos"]:
        sev = "failure" if eos_result.get("reason", "").startswith("completion ends") else "warning"
        warnings.append(DetectionWarning(type="premature_eos", severity=sev, message=eos_result.get("reason", "premature EOS detected"), evidence={"open_parens": eos_result["open_parens"], "open_braces": eos_result["open_braces"], "open_brackets": eos_result["open_brackets"], "reason": eos_result["reason"]}))
    repeat_result = detect_excessive_repetition(completion)
    if repeat_result["excessive_repetition"]:
        warnings.append(DetectionWarning(type="excessive_repetition", severity="failure", message="Excessive repetition: %s" % repeat_result["reason"], evidence={"repeat_ratio": repeat_result["repeat_ratio"], "unique_ratio": repeat_result["unique_ratio"]}))
    deg_result = detect_degenerate_semantics(completion, known_ops)
    if deg_result.get("degenerate", False):
        sev = "failure" if deg_result.get("is_identity", False) else "warning"
        warnings.append(DetectionWarning(type="degenerate_semantics", severity=sev, message=deg_result.get("reason", "degenerate semantics detected"), evidence={"is_identity": deg_result.get("is_identity", False), "computation_depth": deg_result.get("computation_depth", 0), "has_body": deg_result.get("has_body", False)}))
    failure_types = {"premature_eos", "excessive_repetition", "degenerate_semantics"}
    warning_types = {"repeated_tokens", "repeated_operators", "repeated_ast_subtrees"}
    has_failure = any(w.type in failure_types for w in warnings)
    has_warning = any(w.type in warning_types for w in warnings) and not has_failure
    if has_failure:
        classification = "fail"
    elif has_warning:
        classification = "warning"
    else:
        classification = "pass"
    total_tokens = len(completion.split()) if completion.strip() else 0
    unique_tokens = len(set(completion.split())) if completion.strip() else 0
    repeat_rate = (total_tokens - unique_tokens) / total_tokens if total_tokens > 0 else 0.0
    premature_eos = any(w.type == "premature_eos" for w in warnings)
    excessive_repetition = any(w.type == "excessive_repetition" for w in warnings)
    degenerate_semantics = any(w.type == "degenerate_semantics" for w in warnings)
    return DegenerationResult(
        generation_id=generation_id, warnings=warnings, classification=classification,
        total_tokens=total_tokens, unique_tokens=unique_tokens, repeat_rate=round(repeat_rate, 4),
        repeated_token_sequences=repeated_tokens,
        repeated_operator_sequences=repeated_ops,
        repeated_ast_subtrees=repeated_ast,
        premature_eos=premature_eos,
        excessive_repetition=excessive_repetition,
        degenerate_semantics=degenerate_semantics,
    )


def classify_warning(result):
    categories = {"repetition": "warning", "structure": "warning", "syntax": "warning", "semantics": "warning"}
    for w in result.warnings:
        if w.type == "repeated_tokens":
            categories["repetition"] = w.severity
        elif w.type == "repeated_operators":
            categories["structure"] = w.severity
        elif w.type == "repeated_ast_subtrees":
            categories["structure"] = w.severity
        elif w.type == "premature_eos":
            categories["syntax"] = w.severity
        elif w.type == "excessive_repetition":
            categories["repetition"] = w.severity
        elif w.type == "degenerate_semantics":
            categories["semantics"] = w.severity
    return categories


def detect_repeated_ast_subtrees(completion, min_occurrences=2):
    if not completion.strip():
        return []
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(completion)
    except SyntaxError:
        return []
    subtree_serializations = Counter()
    visited = set()
    def serialize_subtree(node):
        if node is None:
            return "None"
        node_id = id(node)
        if node_id in visited:
            return None
        visited.add(node_id)
        type_name = type(node).__name__
        fields = []
        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef):
            fields = [node.name, node.args.args, node.returns, node.body, node.decorator_list]
        elif isinstance(node, ast.If):
            fields = [node.test, node.body, node.orelse]
        elif isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
            fields = [type(node.op).__name__, node.left, node.right]
        elif isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp):
            fields = [type(node.op).__name__, node.operand]
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Compare):
            fields = [node.left, type(node.ops[0]).__name__ if node.ops else None, node.comparators]
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
            fields = [node.func.id if isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) else type(node.func).__name__, node.args]
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Name):
            fields = [node.id]
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Constant):
            fields = [repr(node.value)]
        serialization = (type_name, str(fields))
        subtree_serializations[serialization] += 1
        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef):
            for child in node.args.args:
                serialize_subtree(child)
            for child in node.body:
                serialize_subtree(child)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.If):
            serialize_subtree(node.test)
            for child in node.body:
                serialize_subtree(child)
            for child in node.orelse:
                serialize_subtree(child)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
            serialize_subtree(node.left)
            serialize_subtree(node.right)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.UnaryOp):
            serialize_subtree(node.operand)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Compare):
            serialize_subtree(node.left)
            for comp in node.comparators:
                serialize_subtree(comp)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
            if isinstance(node.func, ast.Name):
                serialize_subtree(node.func)
            for child in node.args:
                serialize_subtree(child)
            for child in node.keywords:
                serialize_subtree(child)
        else:
            for field_key in ["left", "right", "test", "body", "orelse", "args"]:
                if hasattr(node, field_key):
                    child = getattr(node, field_key)
                    if isinstance(child, list):
                        for c in child:
                            if isinstance(c, ast.AST):
                                serialize_subtree(c)
                    elif isinstance(child, ast.AST):
                        serialize_subtree(child)
        return serialization
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        serialize_subtree(node)
    # Only report non-trivial subtrees (skip leaf nodes and simple expressions)
    # Filter out subtrees that are just a single node type or too small
    trivial_types = {"Name", "Constant", "Num", "Str", "Load", "Store", "Del"}
    filtered_repeated = []
    for serialization, count in subtree_serializations.items():
        type_name, fields = serialization
        if type_name in trivial_types:
            continue
        # Also skip if the serialized fields are too short (trivial subtree)
        if len(fields) < 5:
            continue
        if count >= min_occurrences:
            type_name, fields = serialization
            filtered_repeated.append({"subtree_type": type_name, "occurrences": count})
    filtered_repeated.sort(key=lambda x: x["occurrences"], reverse=True)
    return filtered_repeated

"""Taksh v2.3.0 — Held-out task mapping diagnostics.

Measures whether the model can map unfamiliar instructions to code structures.
Work Package 4 of Taksh v2.3.0.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Set


def fingerprint_instruction(instruction: str) -> str:
    """Create a content fingerprint for an instruction to detect contamination."""
    return hashlib.sha256(instruction.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]


def build_mapping_case(
    case_id: str,
    instruction: str,
    expected_structure: Dict[str, Any],
    is_negative: bool = False,
    paraphrase_of: str = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Build a held-out mapping case.

    Args:
        case_id: unique identifier
        instruction: the instruction text
        expected_structure: expected code structure signature
        is_negative: if True, this is a negative control
        paraphrase_of: case_id this paraphrases (for contamination tracking)
    """
    return {
        "case_id": case_id,
        "instruction": instruction,
        "instruction_fingerprint": fingerprint_instruction(instruction),
        "expected_structure": expected_structure,
        "is_negative": is_negative,
        "paraphrase_of": paraphrase_of,
    }


def evaluate_mapping_case(case: Dict[str, Any], completion: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Evaluate a single mapping case against a completion."""
    import ast

    expected = case.get("expected_structure", {})
    result: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "case_id": case["case_id"],
        "instruction": case["instruction"],
        "is_negative": case.get("is_negative", False),
        "paraphrase_of": case.get("paraphrase_of"),
        "parses": False,
        "structure_match": False,
        "expected_ops": expected.get("operations", []),
        "found_ops": [],
        "expected_params": expected.get("params", []),
        "found_params": [],
    }

    try:
        tree = ast.parse(completion)
    except SyntaxError:
        result["parse_error"] = "syntax error"
        return result

    result["parses"] = True

    # Find function definitions
    funcs = [n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef)]
    if not funcs:
        result["error"] = "no function definition found"
        return result

    func = funcs[0]
    result["found_params"] = [arg.arg for arg in func.args.args]

    # Extract operations
    found_ops = set()
    for node in ast.walk(func):
        if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
            if isinstance(node.op, ast.Add):
                found_ops.add("add")
            elif isinstance(node.op, ast.Sub):
                found_ops.add("subtract")
            elif isinstance(node.op, ast.Mult):
                found_ops.add("multiply")
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
            if isinstance(node.func, ast.Name):
                found_ops.add(node.func.id)
    result["found_ops"] = sorted(found_ops)

    # Check structure match
    expected_ops = set(expected.get("operations", []))
    expected_params = set(expected.get("params", []))

    ops_match = expected_ops.issubset(found_ops)
    params_match = expected_params.issubset(set(result["found_params"]))
    result["structure_match"] = ops_match and params_match

    return result


def summarize_mapping(results: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Summarize mapping evaluation results."""
    total = len(results)
    if total == 0:
        return {"total": 0, "error": "no results"}

    parse_rate = sum(1 for r in results if r.get("parses")) / total
    match_rate = sum(1 for r in results if r.get("structure_match")) / total

    negatives = [r for r in results if r.get("is_negative")]
    positive = [r for r in results if not r.get("is_negative")]

    neg_match_rate = (
        sum(1 for r in negatives if r.get("structure_match")) / len(negatives)
        if negatives else 0.0
    )

    return {
        "total": total,
        "parse_rate": round(parse_rate, 4),
        "structure_match_rate": round(match_rate, 4),
        "negative_control_match_rate": round(neg_match_rate, 4),
        "negative_control_count": len(negatives),
        "positive_count": len(positive),
        "recommendation": "PASS" if match_rate >= 0.7 and neg_match_rate <= 0.3 else "REVIEW",
    }

﻿"""Taksh v2.3.0 — Parameter-binding diagnostics.

Extends existing evaluation to test parameter binding robustness.
Work Package 2 of Taksh v2.3.0.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Set


def analyse_parameter_binding(signature: str, body: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Analyse parameter binding in a function using static analysis."""
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(signature + "\n" + body)
    except SyntaxError:
        return {"parses": False, "error": "syntax error", "params": [], "params_used": [], "undefined_names": [], "consistent_references": False}

    func = tree.body[0]
    if not isinstance(func, ast.FunctionDef):
        return {"parses": False, "error": "not a function definition", "params": [], "params_used": [], "undefined_names": [], "consistent_references": False}

    param_names = [arg.arg for arg in func.args.args]
    param_set = set(param_names)

    used_names = set()
    for node in ast.walk(func):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and isinstance(node.ctx, ast.Load):
            used_names.add(node.id)

    assigned_names = set()
    for node in ast.walk(func):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
            for target in node.targets:
                if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
                    assigned_names.add(target.id)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.AugAssign):
            if isinstance(node.target, ast.Name):
                assigned_names.add(node.target.id)

    builtins = {"len", "max", "min", "sum", "abs", "sorted", "range", "list",
                "dict", "set", "tuple", "str", "int", "float", "bool", "print",
                "True", "False", "None"}
    undefined = sorted(used_names - param_set - assigned_names - builtins)
    params_used = sorted(param_set & used_names)
    consistent = len(undefined) == 0

    return {
        "parses": True,
        "error": None,
        "params": param_names,
        "params_used": params_used,
        "undefined_names": undefined,
        "consistent_references": consistent,
        "all_params_used": len(params_used) == len(param_names),
    }

def check_renamed_params(signature, body, new_param_names):
    original = analyse_parameter_binding(signature, body)
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(signature + "\n" + body)
    except SyntaxError:
        return {"error": "syntax error", "binding_preserved": False}
    func = tree.body[0]
    if not isinstance(func, ast.FunctionDef):
        return {"error": "not a function", "binding_preserved": False}
    original_params = [arg.arg for arg in func.args.args]
    if len(new_param_names) != len(original_params):
        return {"error": "param count mismatch", "binding_preserved": False}
    import re
    renamed_sig = signature
    renamed_body = body
    for old, new in zip(original_params, new_param_names):
        renamed_sig = re.sub(r"\b" + old + r"\b", new, renamed_sig)
        renamed_body = re.sub(r"\b" + old + r"\b", new, renamed_body)
    renamed = analyse_parameter_binding(renamed_sig, renamed_body)
    return {
        "original_params": original_params,
        "new_params": new_param_names,
        "original_binding": original,
        "renamed_binding": renamed,
        "binding_preserved": (
            renamed.get("parses", False)
            and renamed.get("consistent_references", False)
            and len(renamed.get("undefined_names", [])) == 0
        ),
    }


def check_reordered_params(signature, body, new_order):
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(signature + "\n" + body)
    except SyntaxError:
        return {"error": "syntax error", "binding_preserved": False}
    func = tree.body[0]
    if not isinstance(func, ast.FunctionDef):
        return {"error": "not a function", "binding_preserved": False}
    original_params = [arg.arg for arg in func.args.args]
    if sorted(new_order) != list(range(len(original_params))):
        return {"error": "invalid reorder", "binding_preserved": False}
    reordered_params = [original_params[i] for i in new_order]
    return {
        "original_params": original_params,
        "reordered_params": reordered_params,
        "new_order": new_order,
        "binding_preserved": True,
    }


def check_unseen_variable_names(signature, body, unseen_names):
    results = {}
    for name in unseen_names:
        test_body = body + "\n    _ = " + name
        analysis = analyse_parameter_binding(signature, test_body)
        results[name] = {
            "defined": name not in analysis.get("undefined_names", []),
            "analysis": analysis,
        }
    return {
        "unseen_names": unseen_names,
        "results": results,
        "all_undefined": all(
            name in r["analysis"].get("undefined_names", [])
            for name, r in results.items()
        ),
    }


def compare_binding(baseline, candidate):
    return {
        "baseline_consistent": baseline.get("consistent_references", False),
        "candidate_consistent": candidate.get("consistent_references", False),
        "baseline_undefined": baseline.get("undefined_names", []),
        "candidate_undefined": candidate.get("undefined_names", []),
        "improved": (
            candidate.get("consistent_references", False)
            and not baseline.get("consistent_references", False)
        ),
        "regressed": (
            baseline.get("consistent_references", False)
            and not candidate.get("consistent_references", False)
        ),
    }

"""Experimental Taksh provider profile for coding-agent integration (v1.4.0).

The profile is a *declaration* of what a local Taksh deployment actually
offers, written so an external coding agent (QuantsMind-Agent, OpenCode,
Cline) can be configured against it without being told something the server
does not do.

Two rules shape it:

* **Nothing unsupported is advertised.** The OpenAI-compatible server in
  ``serving/openai_server.py`` exposes ``GET /v1/models``, ``GET /health``
  and ``POST /v1/chat/completions``. It has no plain-completion endpoint, it
  returns non-streaming responses, and it *rejects* tool, function, n,
  logprobs and response_format requests with an explicit error. The profile
  says exactly that.
* **Tool calling is reported as unsupported**, not as "maybe". A profile that
  implied tool support would cause an agent to send tool requests and then
  fail at runtime.

The integration status is ``EXTERNAL_AGENT_INTEGRATION_PENDING``: the
contract tests in ``evaluation/agent_contract`` exercise the wire format
against the real application, but QuantsMind-Agent lives in another
repository, so real interoperability has not been demonstrated.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field

PROFILE_SCHEMA_VERSION = "quantsmind.agent_profile/1"
INTEGRATION_STATUS_PENDING = "EXTERNAL_AGENT_INTEGRATION_PENDING"


@dataclass
class AgentProviderProfile:
    """What a local Taksh deployment offers to a coding agent."""

    provider_id: str = "taksh-local"
    model_id: str = "qm-code-m3-9m"
    api_style: str = "openai_chat_completions"
    base_url: str = "http://127.0.0.1:8000"
    supported_endpoints: list = field(default_factory=lambda: [
        "GET /v1/models",
        "GET /health",
        "POST /v1/chat/completions",
    ])
    request_types: list = field(default_factory=lambda: ["chat_completion"])
    context_window: int = 512
    max_generation_tokens: int = 256
    max_generation_tokens_ceiling: int = 4096
    streaming_supported: bool = False
    streaming_status: str = "not_implemented: responses are always a single JSON object"
    tool_calling_supported: bool = False
    tool_calling_status: str = (
        "unsupported: the server rejects tools/functions/tool_choice with an "
        "explicit error rather than ignoring them"
    )
    structured_output_supported: bool = False
    structured_output_status: str = (
        "unsupported: response_format is rejected with an explicit error"
    )
    authentication: str = "optional bearer token via TAKSH_API_KEY; the middleware is always active"
    recommended_timeouts: dict = field(default_factory=lambda: {
        "connect_seconds": 5,
        "read_seconds": 120,
        "overall_seconds": 180,
    })
    known_limitations: list = field(default_factory=lambda: [
        "The model is a 9.36M-parameter base model; it is not instruction-tuned.",
        "No plain /v1/completions endpoint: use /v1/chat/completions.",
        "Responses are never streamed.",
        "No tool calling and no structured output.",
        "The base model is served as raw text; the chat template is not applied.",
        "No KV cache: generation re-runs a full forward pass per token, so long "
        "generations are slow on CPU.",
    ])
    integration_status: str = INTEGRATION_STATUS_PENDING
    notes: str = (
        "Experimental profile. The wire contract is exercised offline against "
        "the real application; interoperability with QuantsMind-Agent itself "
        "has not been demonstrated."
    )

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        payload = asdict(self)
        payload["schema"] = PROFILE_SCHEMA_VERSION
        return payload

    def summary(self) -> str:
        return (
            f"{self.provider_id}/{self.model_id} | endpoints: "
            f"{', '.join(self.supported_endpoints)} | streaming: "
            f"{self.streaming_supported} | tool calling: "
            f"{self.tool_calling_supported} | integration: "
            f"{self.integration_status}"
        )


def default_profile(model_id: str = "qm-code-m3-9m", **overrides) -> AgentProviderProfile:
    """The profile for a local Taksh deployment."""
    profile = AgentProviderProfile(model_id=model_id)
    for key, value in overrides.items():
        setattr(profile, key, value)
    return profile


def profile_to_json(profile: AgentProviderProfile) -> str:
    return json.dumps(profile.to_dict(), indent=2, sort_keys=True)

import os

import gradio as gr

from serving.llm_client import (
    LLMConfig,
    ResidencyError,
    append_disclaimer,
    build_messages,
    client_stream,
    demo_stream,
    enforce_residency,
)

TITLE = "Taksh — Financial Knowledge Assistant"
DESCRIPTION = (
    "Ask anything about markets, investing, and financial concepts. "
    "India-first answers. Educational only — not investment advice."
)


def respond(message: str, history):
    if not message.strip():
        yield ""
        return
    cfg = LLMConfig.from_env()
    if not cfg.configured():
        for chunk in demo_stream(message):
            yield chunk
        return
    messages = build_messages(history, message)
    try:
        enforce_residency(cfg.api_base)
    except ResidencyError as e:
        yield f"**Blocked by India data-residency policy**\n\n{e}"
        return
    full = []
    try:
        for delta in client_stream(cfg.api_base, cfg.api_key, cfg.model, messages):
            full.append(delta)
            yield "".join(full)
    except Exception as e:
        yield f"Backend error: {e}\n\nCheck `QM_API_BASE`, `QM_API_KEY`, `QM_MODEL`."
        return
    yield append_disclaimer("".join(full))


def build_ui():
    with gr.Blocks() as ui:
        gr.ChatInterface(
            fn=respond,
            title=TITLE,
            description=DESCRIPTION,
            examples=[
                "What is a P/E ratio and how do I interpret it?",
                "Explain CAGR with an example.",
                "What happens to my SIP if markets crash?",
            ],
        )
    return ui


def main():
    port = int(os.environ.get("QM_UI_PORT", "7860"))
    cfg = LLMConfig.from_env()
    mode = f"backend={cfg.model}" if cfg.configured() else "DEMO MODE (no backend configured)"
    print(f"Starting Taksh UI on http://localhost:{port} [{mode}]")
    build_ui().launch(server_name="0.0.0.0", server_port=port)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import gradio as gr
import torch

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from serving.local_inference import generate_ids, load_model
from training.chat_template import SYSTEM_PROMPT, render_for, render_prompt

#: One canonical preamble. There must not be a second "serving system prompt":
#: the M7 mismatch was exactly that. Callers may still pass their own system
#: message explicitly, but the default is the one training used.
CODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT = SYSTEM_PROMPT

LANGUAGE_INFO = {
    "python": {"extensions": [".py"], "prompt_prefix": "# Python code:\n"},
    "javascript": {"extensions": [".js", ".jsx", ".mjs"], "prompt_prefix": "// JavaScript code:\n"},
    "typescript": {"extensions": [".ts", ".tsx"], "prompt_prefix": "// TypeScript code:\n"},
}


@torch.no_grad()
def generate_code(model, tokenizer, prompt: str, max_new_tokens: int = 512, temperature: float = 0.2, device: str = "cpu") -> str:
    """Generate a completion. Delegates to the shared sampler in local_inference."""
    result = generate_ids(
        model,
        tokenizer,
        prompt,
        max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
        temperature=temperature,
        device=device,
    )
    return result["text"]


def format_prompt(message: str, language: str, context: str = "", tokenizer=None) -> str:
    """Render the inference prompt.

    C3: this used to hand-build "<|system|>...<|user|>...<|assistant|>", none of
    which exist in the tokenizer, so inference fed the model the same shredded
    byte fragments SFT trained on. It now renders through the shared template so
    training and inference cannot drift apart. With a tokenizer supplied, the
    contract is derived from that tokenizer instead of assumed.
    """
    if context:
        lang_label = language if language != "auto" else "unknown"
        user = f"Context ({lang_label}):\n```\n{context}\n```\n\nQuestion: {message}"
    else:
        user = message
    if tokenizer is None:
        return render_prompt(CODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, user)
    return render_for(tokenizer, CODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT, user)


def create_code_chat_ui(model, tokenizer, device: str):
    def respond(message, history, language, context):
        if not message.strip():
            yield ""
            return
        prompt = format_prompt(message, language, context)
        full = ""
        for chunk in generate_code(model, tokenizer, prompt, device=device):
            full += chunk
            yield full

    with gr.Blocks(title="Taksh Coder", theme=gr.themes.Soft()) as ui:
        gr.Markdown("# Taksh Coder — AI Programming Assistant")
        gr.Markdown("Python, JavaScript/TypeScript specialist, and experimental C# evaluation support. Code generation, debugging, review, and explanation.")

        with gr.Row():
            with gr.Column(scale=1):
                language = gr.Dropdown(
                    choices=["auto", "python", "javascript", "typescript", "csharp"],
                    value="auto",
                    label="Language",
                )
                context = gr.Textbox(
                    lines=5,
                    label="Code Context (optional)",
                    placeholder="Paste relevant code here for context...",
                )
            with gr.Column(scale=2):
                chat = gr.ChatInterface(
                    fn=respond,
                    additional_inputs=[language, context],
                    examples=[
                        ["Write a function to debounce a callback in JavaScript", "python", ""],
                        ["Explain how Python decorators give with an example", "python", ""],
                        ["Write a TypeScript generic for a key-value store", "typescript", ""],
                        ["Review this Python code for bugs", "python", "def divide(a, b):\n    return a / b"],
                    ],
                )
    return ui


def main():
    import argparse

    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Taksh Coder — Code Chat UI")
    p.add_argument("--ckpt", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--tokenizer", default="tokenizer/qm_code_bpe_v0.json")
    p.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=7860)
    args = p.parse_args()

    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    print(f"device={device}")

    model, model_cfg = load_model(args.ckpt, device)

    from tokenizers import Tokenizer
    tokenizer = Tokenizer.from_file(args.tokenizer)

    print(f"Starting Taksh Coder on http://localhost:{args.port}")
    ui = create_code_chat_ui(model, tokenizer, device)
    ui.launch(server_name="0.0.0.0", server_port=args.port)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\serving\completion_server.py
import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from serving.languages import is_supported_language
from serving.server_security import (
    add_standard_args,
    api_key_from_env,
    install_auth,
    load_trusted_state,
    resolve_device,
    serve,
)

app = FastAPI(title="Taksh Coder — Completion API")

_model = None
_tokenizer = None
_device = None

# There is deliberately no POST /load. The previous implementation accepted a
# `ckpt` query parameter and called torch.load(weights_only=False) on it with no
# authentication while binding 0.0.0.0 -- unauthenticated remote code execution.
# The checkpoint is now chosen once, on the command line, by the operator.


class CompletionRequest(BaseModel):
    prefix: str
    suffix: str = ""
    language: str = "python"
    max_tokens: int = 64
    temperature: float = 0.2
    top_k: int = 5


class CompletionResponse(BaseModel):
    completions: list[str]
    scores: list[float]
    model: str


def get_model():
    global _model, _tokenizer, _device
    if _model is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=503, detail="Model not loaded. Start the server with --ckpt.")
    return _model, _tokenizer, _device


@app.post("/complete", response_model=CompletionResponse)
async def complete(request: CompletionRequest):
    model, tokenizer, device = get_model()
    if not is_supported_language(request.language):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="unsupported language")

    if request.suffix:
        prompt = f"<|fim_prefix|>{request.prefix}<|fim_suffix|>{request.suffix}<|fim_middle|>"
    else:
        prompt = request.prefix

    ids = tokenizer.encode(prompt).ids
    x = torch.tensor([ids], dtype=torch.long, device=device)

    completions = []
    scores = []

    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(request.top_k):
            gen_ids = x.clone()
            log_prob_sum = 0.0
            for _ in range(request.max_tokens):
                idx_cond = gen_ids if gen_ids.size(1) <= model.cfg["max_seq_len"] else gen_ids[:, -model.cfg["max_seq_len"]:]
                logits, _ = model(idx_cond)
                logits = logits[:, -1, :] / request.temperature
                v, _ = torch.topk(logits, min(50, logits.size(-1)))
                logits[logits < v[:, [-1]]] = float("-inf")
                probs = F.softmax(logits, dim=-1)
                next_id = torch.multinomial(probs, num_samples=1)
                log_prob_sum += torch.log(probs[0, next_id.item()] + 1e-10).item()
                gen_ids = torch.cat([gen_ids, next_id], dim=1)
                if next_id.item() == tokenizer.token_to_id("<eos>"):
                    break

            generated = tokenizer.decode(gen_ids[0].tolist())
            completion = generated[len(prompt):] if generated.startswith(prompt) else generated
            completions.append(completion)
            scores.append(log_prob_sum / max(1, request.max_tokens))

    return CompletionResponse(
        completions=completions,
        scores=scores,
        model="quantsmind-coder",
    )


@app.get("/health")
async def health():
    return {"status": "ok", "model_loaded": _model is not None}


def main():
    global _model, _tokenizer, _device

    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Taksh Coder — Completion API")
    add_standard_args(p, default_port=8000)
    args = p.parse_args()

    _device = resolve_device()
    _model, _model_cfg, _tokenizer = load_trusted_state(args.ckpt, args.tokenizer, _device)
    print(f"loaded {_model_cfg.get('name')} context={_model_cfg.get('max_seq_len')} device={_device}")

    auth_on = install_auth(app, api_key_from_env())
    serve(app, p, args, "Completion API", auth_on)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Shared language identifiers for Taksh serving surfaces."""

from __future__ import annotations

SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES = frozenset({
    "auto",
    "python",
    "javascript",
    "typescript",
    "java",
    "csharp",
    "cpp",
    "c",
    "go",
    "rust",
    "ruby",
    "shell",
    "yaml",
    "toml",
    "dockerfile",
    "sql",
    "unknown",
})

_ALIASES = {
    "c#": "csharp",
    "cs": "csharp",
    "dotnet": "csharp",
    ".net": "csharp",
    "ts": "typescript",
    "js": "javascript",
    "c++": "cpp",
    "sh": "shell",
    "bash": "shell",
    "yml": "yaml",
}


def normalize_language(value: str | None) -> str:
    normalized = (value or "unknown").strip().lower()
    normalized = _ALIASES.get(normalized, normalized)
    return normalized if normalized in SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES else "unknown"


def is_supported_language(value: str | None) -> bool:
    normalized = (value or "").strip().lower()
    normalized = _ALIASES.get(normalized, normalized)
    return normalized in SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES


def prompt_language(value: str | None) -> str:
    normalized = normalize_language(value)
    return {
        "csharp": "C#",
        "cpp": "C++",
        "javascript": "JavaScript",
        "typescript": "TypeScript",
        "yaml": "YAML",
        "toml": "TOML",
        "sql": "SQL",
        "auto": "unknown",
    }.get(normalized, normalized)

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass
class LLMConfig:
    api_base: str
    api_key: str
    model: str

    @classmethod
    def from_env(cls) -> "LLMConfig":
        return cls(
            api_base=os.environ.get("QM_API_BASE", ""),
            api_key=os.environ.get("QM_API_KEY", ""),
            model=os.environ.get("QM_MODEL", ""),
        )

    def configured(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.api_base and self.api_key and self.model)


SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You are Taksh, an India-focused financial knowledge assistant.\n"
    "- Use Indian market conventions: Rupees (Rs.), lakh/crore, NSE/BSE, and SEBI/RBI regulatory context.\n"
    "- Prefer Indian instruments in examples (NSE/BSE stocks, mutual funds, PPF, ELSS, NPS, sovereign gold bonds).\n"
    "- Show formulas and worked numeric examples using Indian conventions.\n"
    "- You provide educational information only. You are NOT a SEBI-registered investment adviser; "
    "never give personalized buy/sell/hold recommendations or portfolio-specific advice. "
    "For personal decisions, direct users to a SEBI-registered investment adviser (SEBI RIA).\n"
    "- For non-Indian markets, answer generally and relate back to Indian context where useful."
)

DISCLAIMER = (
    "\n\n---\n"
    "*Educational information only — not investment advice. Taksh is not a "
    "SEBI-registered investment adviser (RIA); consult a SEBI-registered adviser for personal decisions.*"
)


class ResidencyError(Exception):
    pass


def is_private_endpoint(api_base: str) -> bool:
    from urllib.parse import urlparse

    host = (urlparse(api_base).hostname or "").lower()
    if not host:
        return False
    if host in ("localhost", "::1") or host.endswith((".local", ".intranet", ".internal")):
        return True
    parts = host.split(".")
    if len(parts) == 4 and all(p.isdigit() for p in parts):
        a, b = int(parts[0]), int(parts[1])
        if a == 10 or a == 127 or (a == 192 and b == 168):
            return True
        if a == 172 and 16 <= b <= 31:
            return True
    return False


def enforce_residency(api_base: str) -> None:
    strict = os.environ.get("QM_STRICT_RESIDENCY", "1") == "1"
    if strict and api_base and not is_private_endpoint(api_base):
        raise ResidencyError(
            f"QM_STRICT_RESIDENCY=1: refusing to send prompts outside your controlled "
            f"network (endpoint: {api_base}). India data-residency policy: prompts must stay "
            f"on localhost/private/India-hosted infrastructure. "
            f"To override consciously: set QM_STRICT_RESIDENCY=0."
        )


def append_disclaimer(text: str) -> str:
    if DISCLAIMER.strip() in text:
        return text
    return text + DISCLAIMER


def build_messages(history: list, message: str) -> list:
    msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}]
    for turn in history:
        if isinstance(turn, (list, tuple)) and len(turn) == 2:
            msgs.append({"role": "user", "content": str(turn[0])})
            msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": str(turn[1])})
    msgs.append({"role": "user", "content": message})
    return msgs


def client_stream(api_base: str, api_key: str, model: str, messages: list):
    from openai import OpenAI

    client = OpenAI(base_url=api_base, api_key=api_key)
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model=model,
        messages=messages,
        temperature=0.3,
        max_tokens=1024,
        stream=True,
    )
    for chunk in response:
        delta = chunk.choices[0].delta.content if chunk.choices else None
        if delta:
            yield delta


DEMO_ANSWERS = [
    (
        ("pe ", "pe?", "p/e", "price-to-earnings"),
        "**P/E Ratio (Price-to-Earnings)**\n\n"
        "P/E = Share Price / Earnings Per Share (EPS)\n\n"
        "Example: If a stock trades at Rs.500 and its EPS is Rs.25, "
        "P/E = 500 / 25 = **20x**. Investors pay Rs.20 for every Re.1 of annual earnings.\n\n"
        "Rules of thumb: high P/E implies growth expectations; compare within the same sector."),
    (
        ("cagr",),
        "**CAGR (Compound Annual Growth Rate)**\n\n"
        "CAGR = (End Value / Start Value)^(1/years) - 1\n\n"
        "Example: Rs.10,000 grows to Rs.16,000 in 3 years:\n"
        "CAGR = (16000/10000)^(1/3) - 1 = **~17%** per year."),
    (
        ("sip",),
        "**SIP (Systematic Investment Plan)**\n\n"
        "A fixed amount invested at regular intervals, averaging out purchase cost "
        "(rupee-cost averaging).\n\n"
        "Example: Rs.5,000/month at 12% p.a. for 10 years grows to roughly **Rs.11.6 lakh** "
        "(invested Rs.6 lakh)."),
]


def demo_stream(message: str):
    low = " " + message.lower() + " "
    body = None
    for keys, ans in DEMO_ANSWERS:
        if any(k in low for k in keys):
            body = ans
            break
    if body is None:
        body = (
            "**Taksh demo mode** — no LLM backend configured.\n\n"
            "Set these environment variables to connect any OpenAI-compatible model:\n"
            "`QM_API_BASE`, `QM_API_KEY`, `QM_MODEL`\n\n"
            "Try asking about: P/E ratio, CAGR, SIP."
        )
    for i in range(0, len(body), 24):
        yield body[: i + 24]
