<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\evaluation\eval_text.py
"""Text-task evaluation for the multimodal models (regression/forgetting check).

Reuses the pilot metrics from ``evaluation/evaluate_pilot.py`` (held-out
perplexity, seed-question set NLL by category) but is MM-aware: it extracts
the text component from a multimodal checkpoint (or uses a text-only
checkpoint directly), so the same metrics can be run on both an MM checkpoint
and the text-only reference it was warm-started from.  Reported deltas are
measurements, not decisions -- thresholds live in ``promotion.yaml``.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import torch

from evaluation.evaluate_pilot import heldout_ppl, summarize
from evaluation.load_eval import load_eval_set
from evaluation.mm_checkpoint import load_checkpoint


@torch.no_grad()
def score_items(model, items, tok_encode, device: str = "cpu") -> list[dict]:
    """Score seed items exactly like ``evaluate_pilot.score_seed``."""
    rows = []
    for item in items:
        ids = torch.tensor(
            [tok_encode(f"Q: {item['question']}\nA: {item['reference']}")],
            dtype=torch.long, device=device,
        )
        _, loss = model(ids, targets=ids)
        rows.append({
            "id": item["id"],
            "category": item["category"],
            "nll_per_token": round(float(loss.item()), 4),
        })
    return rows


def evaluate_text(
    model,
    tok_encode,
    seed_path: str | None,
    tokens_path: str | None,
    device: str = "cpu",
    seq_len: int = 2048,
    max_windows: int = 32,
) -> dict:
    """Run the text metrics for one text model.

    Returns a dict of metric sections.  Unavailable inputs produce ``None``
    markers rather than fabricated numbers.
    """
    rep = {}
    if tokens_path is not None and Path(tokens_path).is_file():
        nll, ppl = heldout_ppl(model, tokens_path, seq_len=seq_len,
                               max_windows=max_windows, device=device)
        rep["heldout_perplexity"] = ppl
        rep["heldout_tokens/ppl_windows"] = {"max_windows": max_windows, "nll": nll}
    else:
        rep["heldout_perplexity"] = None

    if seed_path is not None and Path(seed_path).is_file():
        items = load_eval_set(Path(seed_path))
        rows = score_items(model, items, tok_encode, device=device)
        rep["seed_summary"] = summarize(rows)
        rep["seed_items"] = rows
    else:
        rep["seed_summary"] = None

    return rep


def _deltas(a: dict, b: dict) -> dict:
    d = {}
    for key in ("heldout_perplexity",):
        if isinstance(a.get(key), (int, float)) and isinstance(b.get(key), (int, float)):
            d[key] = {"candidate": b[key], "reference": a[key], "delta": b[key] - a[key]}
    sa, sb = a.get("seed_summary"), b.get("seed_summary")
    if isinstance(sa, dict) and isinstance(sb, dict):
        d["seed_overall_nll_delta"] = {
            "candidate": sb.get("overall_mean_nll"),
            "reference": sa.get("overall_mean_nll"),
            "delta": (
                sb.get("overall_mean_nll") - sa.get("overall_mean_nll")
                if sa.get("overall_mean_nll") is not None
                and sb.get("overall_mean_nll") is not None else None
            ),
        }
    return d


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="python -m evaluation.eval_text",
        description="MM-aware text regression/forgetting evaluation (measurement only).",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--ckpt", required=True, help="MM or text-only checkpoint (.pt)")
    parser.add_argument("--ref", help="reference checkpoint to diff against (e.g. text-only M0)")
    parser.add_argument("--tokenizer", default="tokenizer/qm_bpe_v0.json")
    parser.add_argument("--tokens", help="uint16 memmap of eval tokens for heldout PPL")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", default="evaluation/india_finance/seed_v0.jsonl",
                        help="seed question set (JSONL, load_eval format)")
    parser.add_argument("--device", default="cpu")
    parser.add_argument("--seq-len", type=int, default=2048)
    parser.add_argument("--max-windows", type=int, default=32)
    parser.add_argument("--out", help="write JSON report here")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    from tokenizers import Tokenizer

    tok = Tokenizer.from_file(args.tokenizer)
    encode = lambda s: tok.encode(s).ids  # noqa: E731

    loaded = load_checkpoint(args.ckpt, device=args.device)
    rep = evaluate_text(
        loaded.text_model, encode, seed_path=args.seed, tokens_path=args.tokens,
        device=args.device, seq_len=args.seq_len, max_windows=args.max_windows,
    )
    rep["checkpoint"] = str(loaded.path)
    rep["checkpoint_is_mm"] = loaded.is_mm
    rep["note"] = "measurement only; no regression decision is made here"

    if args.ref is not None:
        ref = load_checkpoint(args.ref, device=args.device)
        ref_rep = evaluate_text(
            ref.text_model, encode, seed_path=args.seed, tokens_path=args.tokens,
            device=args.device, seq_len=args.seq_len, max_windows=args.max_windows,
        )
        rep["reference"] = {
            "checkpoint": str(ref.path),
            "checkpoint_is_mm": ref.is_mm,
            "deltas_vs_reference": _deltas(ref_rep, rep),
        }

    if args.out:
        Path(args.out).write_text(json.dumps(rep, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")

    hp = rep.get("heldout_perplexity")
    ss = rep.get("seed_summary") or {}
    print(f"heldout_ppl={hp} seed_overall_nll={ss.get('overall_mean_nll')} (measurement only)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\evaluation\eval_vqa.py
"""Minimal VQA smoke evaluation.

For each record ``{image, question, expected_answer}`` the model generates an
answer conditioned on the image and the question, and the result is compared
with the expected answer using an exact normalized match.  The pass/fail
outcomes are *reported only* (exit code is always 0); this is measurement
infrastructure and does not by itself promote or demote a checkpoint.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
from pathlib import Path

import torch

from evaluation.generate import decode_ids, generate_answer, image_tensor_file
from evaluation.mm_checkpoint import load_checkpoint


def normalize_answer(text: str) -> str:
    """Lowercase, strip surrounding whitespace, collapse internal whitespace."""
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(text or "").strip().lower())


def evaluate_records(model, tokenizer, records, max_new_tokens=16, image_size=112,
                     device="cpu"):
    """Evaluate a list of VQA records.

    Each record must contain ``image`` (path), ``question``, ``expected_answer``.
    ``image`` paths are resolved relative to the records file directory when
    they are relative.  Returns per-record results, a summary, and any
    per-record errors (bad/missing files, wrong types).
    """
    results = []
    errors = []
    for i, rec in enumerate(records):
        if not isinstance(rec, dict) or not {"image", "question", "expected_answer"} <= set(rec):
            errors.append({"index": i, "error": "record missing image/question/expected_answer"})
            continue
        img_path = rec["image"]
        if not Path(img_path).is_absolute():
            img_path = str(Path(".") / img_path)
        if not Path(img_path).is_file():
            errors.append({"index": i, "error": f"image file not found: {img_path}"})
            continue
        try:
            ids = tokenizer.encode(rec["question"]).ids
            image = image_tensor_file(img_path, size=image_size, device=device)
            gen_ids = generate_answer(model, image, ids, max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens)
            generated = decode_ids(tokenizer, gen_ids)
            expected = normalize_answer(rec["expected_answer"])
            got = normalize_answer(generated)
            results.append({
                "index": i,
                "question": rec["question"],
                "expected_answer": rec["expected_answer"],
                "generated_answer": generated,
                "pass": bool(got == expected),
            })
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - report per-record and continue
            errors.append({"index": i, "error": str(exc)})

    summary = {
        "records": len(records),
        "evaluated": len(results),
        "errors": len(errors),
        "passed": sum(1 for r in results if r["pass"]),
        "failed": sum(1 for r in results if not r["pass"]),
        "measurement_only": True,
    }
    return {"summary": summary, "results": results, "errors": errors}


def _iter_records(path: Path):
    """Yield records from a JSON array file, a single JSON object, or JSONL."""
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig").strip()
    if not text:
        return
    try:
        obj = json.loads(text)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        for line in text.splitlines():
            line = line.strip()
            if line:
                yield json.loads(line)
        return
    if isinstance(obj, list):
        yield from obj
    else:
        yield obj


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="python -m evaluation.eval_vqa",
        description="Minimal VQA smoke evaluation (measurement only).",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--ckpt", required=True, help="MM checkpoint (.pt)")
    parser.add_argument("--tokenizer", default="tokenizer/qm_bpe_v0.json")
    parser.add_argument("--device", default="cpu")
    parser.add_argument("--max-new-tokens", type=int, default=16)
    parser.add_argument("--image-size", type=int, default=112)
    parser.add_argument("--records", required=True,
                        help="JSON or JSONL list of {image, question, expected_answer}")
    parser.add_argument("--out", help="write JSON report here")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    from tokenizers import Tokenizer

    tokenizer = Tokenizer.from_file(args.tokenizer)
    loaded = load_checkpoint(args.ckpt, device=args.device)
    if not loaded.is_mm:
        raise SystemExit(f"error: {args.ckpt} is not a multimodal checkpoint")

    records = list(_iter_records(Path(args.records)))
    report = evaluate_records(
        loaded.model, tokenizer, records,
        max_new_tokens=args.max_new_tokens, image_size=args.image_size, device=args.device,
    )
    report["checkpoint"] = str(loaded.path)
    report["note"] = "measurement only; no promotion decision"

    if args.out:
        Path(args.out).write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")

    s = report["summary"]
    print(f"records={s['records']} evaluated={s['evaluated']} errors={s['errors']} "
          f"passed={s['passed']} failed={s['failed']} (measurement only)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\evaluation\evaluate_pilot.py
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

from evaluation.load_eval import load_eval_set


def format_item(item: dict) -> str:
    return f"Q: {item['question']}\nA: {item['reference']}"


def load_qm_checkpoint(path: str, device: str):
    from training.model import QMModel

    ckpt = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    raw_cfg = ckpt.get("cfg") or ckpt.get("config", {})
    if "model" in raw_cfg and isinstance(raw_cfg["model"], dict):
        model_cfg = raw_cfg["model"]
    elif "vocab_size" in raw_cfg:
        model_cfg = raw_cfg
    else:
        import yaml
        model_path = raw_cfg.get("run", {}).get("model_config", "configs/model/code_30m.yaml")
        with open(model_path) as f:
            model_cfg = yaml.safe_load(f)["model"]
    model_cfg = dict(model_cfg)
    model_cfg.setdefault("rope_theta", 10000.0)
    model_cfg.setdefault("norm_eps", 1e-5)
    model = QMModel(model_cfg)
    model.load_state_dict(ckpt["model"])
    return model.to(device).eval(), model_cfg


@torch.no_grad()
def heldout_ppl(
    model,
    tokens_path: str,
    seq_len: int = 2048,
    max_windows: int = 32,
    val_fraction: float = 0.01,
    device: str = "cpu",
):
    """Held-out NLL and perplexity; returns ``(None, None)`` when unmeasurable.

    Same false-pass guard as `evaluation.eval_code.compute_code_perplexity`: a
    held-out tail shorter than one window used to yield ``exp(0) == 1.0``.
    """
    data = np.memmap(tokens_path, dtype=np.uint16, mode="r")
    split = int(len(data) * (1.0 - val_fraction))
    val_tokens = len(data) - split
    if val_tokens < seq_len + 1:
        return None, None

    losses = []
    for i in range(max_windows):
        off = split + i * seq_len
        if off + seq_len + 1 > len(data):
            break
        x = torch.from_numpy(data[off : off + seq_len].astype(np.int64)).unsqueeze(0).to(device)
        y = torch.from_numpy(data[off + 1 : off + 1 + seq_len].astype(np.int64)).unsqueeze(0).to(device)
        _, loss = model(x, targets=y)
        losses.append(loss.item())

    if not losses:
        return None, None
    avg = sum(losses) / len(losses)
    return avg, math_exp(avg)


def math_exp(x: float) -> float:
    import math

    return math.exp(min(20.0, x))


@torch.no_grad()
def score_seed(model, tokenizer_encode, device: str) -> list[dict]:
    results = []
    for item in load_eval_set():
        ids = torch.tensor([tokenizer_encode(format_item(item))], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
        _, loss = model(ids, targets=ids)
        results.append({"id": item["id"], "category": item["category"], "nll_per_token": round(loss.item(), 4)})
    return results


@torch.no_grad()
def score_seed_hf(model_name: str, device: str) -> list[dict]:
    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device).eval()
    results = []
    for item in load_eval_set():
        ids = tok(format_item(item), return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to(device)
        out = model(ids, labels=ids)
        results.append({"id": item["id"], "category": item["category"], "nll_per_token": round(out.loss.item(), 4)})
    return results


def summarize(rows: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Aggregate per-item NLL into a category summary.

    An empty ``rows`` list returns ``overall_mean_nll: None`` and ``ok: False``
    instead of ``0.0``. Dividing by ``max(1, len(rows))`` used to report a *perfect*
    mean NLL of 0.0 for an unevaluated seed set, which would satisfy the
    ``no_regression`` gate in ``evaluation/promotion.yaml``. Same false-pass class
    as the empty held-out-token split guarded in ``heldout_ppl``.
    """
    by_cat = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_cat.setdefault(r["category"], []).append(r["nll_per_token"])
    if not rows:
        return {
            "overall_mean_nll": None,
            "by_category": {},
            "n_items": 0,
            "ok": False,
            "error": "no seed items were evaluated",
        }
    return {
        "overall_mean_nll": round(sum(r["nll_per_token"] for r in rows) / len(rows), 4),
        "by_category": {k: round(sum(v) / len(v), 4) for k, v in sorted(by_cat.items())},
        "n_items": len(rows),
        "ok": True,
    }


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Evaluate a pilot checkpoint or HF benchmark rival")
    p.add_argument("--ckpt", default=None, help="path to qm_pilot_final.pt")
    p.add_argument("--hf-model", default=None, help="benchmark rival, e.g. Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B")
    p.add_argument("--tokens", default="data/corpus_v0.tokens.bin")
    p.add_argument("--out", default=None)
    p.add_argument("--skip-seed", action="store_true")
    args = p.parse_args()

    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    report = {}

    if args.ckpt:
        model, cfg = load_qm_checkpoint(args.ckpt, device)
        ppl_loss, ppl = heldout_ppl(model, args.tokens, device=device)
        if ppl_loss is None:
            report["heldout"] = {
                "nll": None,
                "perplexity": None,
                "ok": False,
                "error": "held-out split too small to score (need >= seq_len+1 tokens)",
            }
            print("held-out perplexity NOT measurable: split too small to score")
        else:
            report["heldout"] = {"nll": round(ppl_loss, 4), "perplexity": round(ppl, 2), "ok": True}
            print(f"held-out NLL {ppl_loss:.4f} | ppl {ppl:.2f}")
        if not args.skip_seed:
            from tokenizers import Tokenizer

            tok = Tokenizer.from_file("tokenizer/qm_bpe_v0.json")
            rows = score_seed(model, lambda s: tok.encode(s).ids, device)
            report["india_finance_seed"] = {"rows": rows, "summary": summarize(rows)}
            print(json.dumps(report["india_finance_seed"]["summary"], indent=2))
    elif args.hf_model:
        rows = score_seed_hf(args.hf_model, device)
        report["hf_model"] = args.hf_model
        report["india_finance_seed"] = {"rows": rows, "summary": summarize(rows)}
        print(args.hf_model, json.dumps(report["india_finance_seed"]["summary"], indent=2))
    else:
        raise SystemExit("pass --ckpt or --hf-model")

    if args.out:
        Path(args.out).write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
        print(f"saved {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\evaluation\functional_eval.py
"""Deterministic functional evaluation layer (Taksh v1.2.0 Increment 4).

Functional correctness is measured independently from syntax, structure,
and parameter binding. Generated code is executed only through
:func:`evaluation.safe_execute.execute_tests`, which runs it in an isolated,
bounded subprocess (``python -I``, AST allowlist, 2s timeout, no imports,
no ``open``/``eval``/``exec``). This module never calls ``exec`` or
``eval`` itself and never falls back to in-process execution: anything the
validator rejects, anything that times out, and any subprocess error is a
failure. If the safe boundary cannot be established (validator rejects the
source), execution is refused rather than attempted.

Metrics are reported separately — parse rate, exact match, structural
validity, binding, functional accuracy, functional accuracy conditional on
parsing, functional accuracy conditional on binding, and the
failure-category distribution. They are never combined into one score.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import subprocess
import sys
from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass

from evaluation.safe_execute import execute_tests, validate_source
from training.program_analysis import analyse

__all__ = [
    "FunctionalResult",
    "evaluate_functional",
    "classify_failure",
    "functional_report",
]

# Failure categories (stable strings; documented in the Increment 4 report).
PASS = "pass"
SYNTAX_STRUCTURAL = "syntax_structural_failure"
BINDING = "incorrect_parameter_binding"
RETURN_EXPR = "incorrect_return_expression"
OPERATION = "incorrect_operation"
IO = "incorrect_input_output_relationship"
TYPE = "incorrect_type_handling"
CONDITIONAL = "missing_conditional_behavior"
COLLECTION = "incorrect_collection_transformation"
PLAUSIBLE = "superficially_plausible_but_functionally_incorrect"
VALIDATION = "rejected_by_safe_execution_gate"
TIMEOUT = "execution_timeout"
EXECUTION_ERROR = "execution_error"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class FunctionalResult:
    passed: bool
    category: str
    reason: str


def evaluate_functional(source: str, function_name: str, tests: list[dict]) -> FunctionalResult:
    """Execute ``source`` against ``tests`` in the isolated safe gate.

    ``tests`` are dicts with ``args``/``kwargs``/``expected``. Timeouts and
    execution errors are failures, never exceptions.
    """
    _tree, reason = validate_source(source)
    if _tree is None:
        if "syntax error" in reason:
            return FunctionalResult(False, SYNTAX_STRUCTURAL, reason)
        return FunctionalResult(False, VALIDATION, reason)
    result = execute_tests(source, function_name, tests)
    if result.passed:
        return FunctionalResult(True, PASS, result.reason)
    reason = result.reason or ""
    if "timed out" in reason:
        return FunctionalResult(False, TIMEOUT, reason)
    if reason.startswith("AssertionError"):
        return FunctionalResult(False, IO, reason)
    if "NameError" in reason:
        return FunctionalResult(False, BINDING, reason)
    if "TypeError" in reason:
        return FunctionalResult(False, TYPE, reason)
    if "SyntaxError" in reason:
        return FunctionalResult(False, SYNTAX_STRUCTURAL, reason)
    return FunctionalResult(False, EXECUTION_ERROR, reason)


def _parse_signature(signature: str) -> str:
    tree_source = signature + "\n    pass"
    import ast

    return tree_source


def classify_failure(
    signature: str,
    reference_body: str | None,
    completion: str,
    *,
    functional: FunctionalResult | None = None,
    function_name: str | None = None,
    tests: list[dict] | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Classify one generated completion into a failure category.

    ``reference_body`` may be None (static classification only). When
    ``tests`` and ``function_name`` are supplied, functional evidence is
    obtained through the safe gate; otherwise ``functional`` may be passed
    directly. Classification order: syntax, binding, then functional
    shape (conditional / collection / operation / return / plausible).
    """
    expected = analyse(signature, reference_body) if reference_body else None
    indent = completion
    if completion and not completion[0].isspace():
        indent = "\n".join("    " + line if line else line for line in completion.splitlines())
    generated = analyse(signature, indent)
    if not generated["parses"]:
        return SYNTAX_STRUCTURAL
    if generated["undefined_names"]:
        return BINDING
    if expected is not None and expected["parses"]:
        if generated["params_used"] != expected["params_used"]:
            return BINDING
    if functional is None and function_name is not None and tests is not None:
        source = signature + "\n" + indent
        functional = evaluate_functional(source, function_name, tests)
    if functional is not None and functional.passed:
        return PASS
    if functional is not None and functional.category in (TYPE, BINDING, TIMEOUT, VALIDATION, SYNTAX_STRUCTURAL):
        return functional.category
    if expected is not None and expected["parses"]:
        expected_ops = set(expected["operations"])
        generated_ops = set(generated["operations"])
        if ("comparison_gt" in expected_ops) or ("comparison_lt" in expected_ops) or ("if_selection" in expected_ops):
            if "comparison_gt" not in generated_ops and "comparison_lt" not in generated_ops and "if_selection" not in generated_ops:
                return CONDITIONAL
        collection_ops = {"comprehension", "iteration", "length", "count_items", "sum_items"}
        if expected_ops & collection_ops:
            if not (generated_ops & collection_ops):
                return COLLECTION
        if expected_ops and not expected_ops.issubset(generated_ops):
            return OPERATION
    if generated["parses"] and (expected is None or generated["params_used"] == expected["params_used"]):
        # Parses and binds, matches the operation shape, but produces the
        # wrong value: correct shape, wrong behaviour.
        return PLAUSIBLE
    return RETURN_EXPR


def functional_report(records: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Separate functional metrics for scored evaluation records.

    Records need ``parses``, ``exact``, ``structural``, ``binding``,
    ``functional`` (``{"passed": bool|None}``) and ``failure_category``.
    """
    records = list(records)
    n = len(records)
    parses = sum(bool(r["parses"]) for r in records)
    binding = sum(bool(r["binding"]) for r in records)
    functional_scored = [r for r in records if (r.get("functional") or {}).get("passed") is not None]
    functional_passed = sum(r["functional"]["passed"] is True for r in functional_scored)
    parsed = [r for r in records if r["parses"]]
    parsed_functional = [r for r in parsed if (r.get("functional") or {}).get("passed") is not None]
    bound = [r for r in records if r["binding"]]
    bound_functional = [r for r in bound if (r.get("functional") or {}).get("passed") is not None]
    categories = Counter(r.get("failure_category", "uncategorised") for r in records)
    return {
        "records": n,
        "parse_rate": round(parses / n, 4) if n else 0.0,
        "exact_rate": round(sum(bool(r["exact"]) for r in records) / n, 4) if n else 0.0,
        "structural_rate": round(sum(bool(r["structural"]) for r in records) / n, 4) if n else 0.0,
        "binding_rate": round(binding / n, 4) if n else 0.0,
        "functional_rate": round(functional_passed / len(functional_scored), 4) if functional_scored else None,
        "functional_scored": len(functional_scored),
        "functional_given_parse_count": len(parsed_functional),
        "functional_given_parse": (
            round(sum(r["functional"]["passed"] is True for r in parsed_functional) / len(parsed_functional), 4)
            if parsed_functional
            else None
        ),
        "functional_given_binding_count": len(bound_functional),
        "functional_given_binding": (
            round(sum(r["functional"]["passed"] is True for r in bound_functional) / len(bound_functional), 4)
            if bound_functional
            else None
        ),
        "failure_categories": dict(sorted(categories.items())),
    }


def safe_execution_available() -> bool:
    """True when an isolated interpreter can be started for the safe gate."""
    try:
        completed = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-I", "-c", "pass"],
            input="",
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=5,
            check=False,
        )
    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
        return False
    return completed.returncode == 0

"""Additional held-out generalization cases (integrated campaign).

Novel identifier names, positions, structures, and propagation depths —
not used in implementation development examples. Separate from all frozen
fixtures. Every case carries an explicit expected-output relationship.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


def _case(case_id, kind, instruction, signature, reference_body, function_name, pairs):
    tests = [
        {"args": list(args), "kwargs": {}, "expected": expected}
        for args, expected in pairs
    ]
    return {
        "case_id": case_id,
        "kind": kind,
        "instruction": instruction,
        "signature": signature,
        "reference_body": reference_body,
        "function_name": function_name,
        "tests": tests,
    }


CASES = [
    _case("GEN-div-001", "div", "Divide the first value by the second.",
          "def div_probe(header_qty, unit_qty):", "    return header_qty / unit_qty", "div_probe",
          [((10, 2), 5.0), ((9, 3), 3.0), ((7, 2), 3.5)]),
    _case("GEN-div-002", "div", "Return the quotient.",
          "def quotient_fn(amount_tag, divisor_tag):", "    return amount_tag / divisor_tag", "quotient_fn",
          [((8, 4), 2.0), ((5, 2), 2.5), ((0, 7), 0.0)]),
    _case("GEN-mod-001", "mod", "Return the remainder.",
          "def rem_probe(total_qty, size_qty):", "    return total_qty % size_qty", "rem_probe",
          [((10, 3), 1), ((9, 3), 0), ((7, 4), 3)]),
    _case("GEN-nested-001", "nested", "Add, then multiply the sum by the third value.",
          "def nested_fn(first_part, second_part, third_part):", "    return (first_part + second_part) * third_part", "nested_fn",
          [((2, 3, 4), 20), ((1, 1, 10), 20), ((0, 5, 2), 10)]),
    _case("GEN-nested-002", "nested", "Multiply the pair, then add the third.",
          "def nested_two(alpha_hd, beta_hd, gamma_hd):", "    return alpha_hd * beta_hd + gamma_hd", "nested_two",
          [((2, 3, 4), 10), ((5, 1, 0), 5), ((3, 3, 3), 12)]),
    _case("GEN-str-001", "string", "Strip outer spaces and shout the text.",
          "def shout_probe(raw_entry):", "    return raw_entry.strip().upper()", "shout_probe",
          [((" hi ",), "HI"), (("  go  ",), "GO"), (("x",), "X")]),
    _case("GEN-str-002", "string", "Quiet the shouting text.",
          "def quiet_probe(noisy_entry):", "    return noisy_entry.lower()", "quiet_probe",
          [(("LOUD",), "loud"), (("AbC",), "abc"), (("",), "")]),
    _case("GEN-cond-001", "conditional", "Return the first when it exceeds the second, else the second.",
          "def pick_probe(high_hd, low_hd):", "    if high_hd > low_hd:\n        return high_hd\n    return low_hd", "pick_probe",
          [((9, 3), 9), ((2, 8), 8), ((5, 5), 5)]),
    _case("GEN-cond-002", "conditional", "Return the smaller value.",
          "def small_probe(upper_hd, lower_hd):", "    if upper_hd < lower_hd:\n        return upper_hd\n    return lower_hd", "small_probe",
          [((3, 9), 3), ((8, 2), 2), ((4, 4), 4)]),
    _case("GEN-list-001", "list", "Double every value in the list.",
          "def double_probe(seq_hd):", "    return [item * 2 for item in seq_hd]", "double_probe",
          [(([1, 2, 3],), [2, 4, 6]), (([],), []), (([-1, 0],), [-2, 0])]),
    _case("GEN-list-002", "list", "Keep only the even entries.",
          "def even_keep(seq_hd):", "    return [item for item in seq_hd if item % 2 == 0]", "even_keep",
          [(([1, 2, 3, 4],), [2, 4]), (([],), []), (([7],), [])]),
    _case("GEN-list-003", "list", "Count the long entries.",
          "def long_count(seq_hd):", "    count = 0\n    for item in seq_hd:\n        if len(item) > 3:\n            count += 1\n    return count", "long_count",
          [((["a", "bees", "cat"],), 1), (([],), 0), ((["four", "five"],), 2)]),
    _case("GEN-prop-001", "propagation", "Store the value, then double it.",
          "def carry_probe(value_hd):", "    stored = value_hd\n    return stored * 2", "carry_probe",
          [((6,), 12), ((0,), 0), ((-3,), -6)]),
    _case("GEN-prop-002", "propagation", "Chain the value through two locals.",
          "def chain_probe(seed_hd):", "    first = seed_hd\n    second = first + 1\n    return second", "chain_probe",
          [((4,), 5), ((0,), 1), ((-1,), 0)]),
    _case("GEN-prop-003", "propagation", "Accumulate the list into a local.",
          "def acc_probe(items_hd):", "    total = 0\n    for item in items_hd:\n        total += item\n    return total", "acc_probe",
          [(([1, 2, 3],), 6), (([],), 0), (([5],), 5)]),
    _case("GEN-bool-001", "boolean", "Return True when the value is positive.",
          "def pos_probe(num_hd):", "    return num_hd > 0", "pos_probe",
          [((3,), True), ((0,), False), ((-2,), False)]),
    _case("GEN-bool-002", "boolean", "Return True when both hold.",
          "def both_probe(flag_hd, other_hd):", "    return flag_hd > 0 and other_hd > 0", "both_probe",
          [((2, 3), True), ((2, 0), False), ((-1, 4), False)]),
    _case("GEN-join2-001", "join", "Join with a comma.",
          "def comma_probe(first_hd, second_hd):", "    return first_hd + \", \" + second_hd", "comma_probe",
          [(("a", "b"), "a, b"), (("", "x"), ", x"), (("x", ""), "x, ")]),
    _case("GEN-scale2-001", "scale", "Scale by three.",
          "def triple_probe(value_hd):", "    return value_hd * 3", "triple_probe",

    _case("GEN-max2-001", "max", "Return the greater of the two.",
          "def greater_probe(alpha_hd, beta_hd):", "    if alpha_hd > beta_hd:\n        return alpha_hd\n    return beta_hd", "greater_probe",
          [((7, 2), 7), ((2, 7), 7), ((5, 5), 5)]),
    _case("GEN-min2-001", "min", "Return the lesser of the two.",
          "def lesser_probe(alpha_hd, beta_hd):", "    if alpha_hd < beta_hd:\n        return alpha_hd\n    return beta_hd", "lesser_probe",
          [((7, 2), 2), ((2, 7), 2), ((5, 5), 5)]),
    _case("GEN-sum2-001", "sum", "Add the three values.",
          "def three_sum(a_hd, b_hd, c_hd):", "    return a_hd + b_hd + c_hd", "three_sum",
          [((1, 2, 3), 6), ((0, 0, 0), 0), ((-1, 1, 5), 5)]),
    _case("GEN-label-001", "string", "Return the label unchanged.",
          "def label_probe(name_hd):", "    return name_hd", "label_probe",
          [(("memo",), "memo"), (("",), ""), (("x",), "x")]),
    _case("GEN-swap-001", "swap", "Return the second value.",
          "def second_probe(first_hd, second_hd):", "    return second_hd", "second_probe",
          [((3, 8), 8), ((8, 3), 3), ((5, 5), 5)]),
]


def build_cases() -> list[dict]:
    return list(CASES)


def suite_digest() -> str:
    import hashlib

    return hashlib.sha256(repr(CASES).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\evaluation\generate.py
"""Deterministic autoregressive generation for the multimodal model.

This is *measurement* generation used by the evaluation harness: greedy
argmax decoding with the same image-mask placement used during training, so
that caption/VQA outputs are reproducible.  It is not a training component.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import torch

from training.image_data import preprocess_image
from training.multimodal import build_mm_mask


def image_tensor_file(path: str | Path, size: int = 112, device: str = "cpu") -> torch.Tensor:
    """Load an image file and preprocess it to ``(1, 3, size, size)`` float32.

    Uses ``training.image_data.preprocess_image`` (RGB, LANCZOS cover-resize,
    center crop, [0, 1]) so evaluation preprocessing matches the training
    contract exactly.
    """
    from PIL import Image

    path = Path(path)
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"image file not found: {path}")
    with Image.open(path) as img:
        arr = preprocess_image(img, size=size)
    return torch.from_numpy(arr).permute(2, 0, 1).unsqueeze(0).to(device).float()


def _prefix_embeds(model, image: torch.Tensor, text_prefix_ids):
    """Build the image + optional text-prefix embedding row for one sample."""
    if image.shape[0] != 1:
        raise ValueError("generation currently supports a single sample (batch size 1)")
    device = image.device

    def row(ids):
        t = torch.tensor([[ids]], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
        return model.text.embed(t)

    with torch.no_grad():
        vis = model.projector(model.vision(image))
        parts = [
            row(model.img_start),
            vis,
            row(model.img_end),
            row(model.caption_start),
        ]
        if text_prefix_ids:
            t = torch.tensor([list(text_prefix_ids)], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
            parts.append(model.text.embed(t))
    return torch.cat(parts, dim=1)


def generate_continuation(
    model,
    image: torch.Tensor,
    text_prefix_ids=None,
    max_new_tokens: int = 32,
    temperature: float = 0.0,
) -> list[int]:
    """Greedily generate token ids continuing from an image (+ optional text).

    Prediction follows the training layout: every position predicts the next
    token, so position ``cap_start_pos + len(text_prefix_ids)`` predicts the
    first generated token.  Generation stops when ``text_eos`` is sampled or
    ``max_new_tokens`` is reached.

    Parameters
    ----------
    model : QMMultimodal
        A multimodal model in eval mode.
    image : torch.Tensor
        ``(1, 3, H, W)`` float32 image on the same device as the model.
    text_prefix_ids : list[int] | None
        Token ids placed in the text region after CAPTION_START (e.g. a VQA
        question).  Empty/None generates a plain caption.
    max_new_tokens : int
        Hard cap on generated tokens.
    temperature : float
        Sampling temperature.  ``0.0`` (default) means deterministic argmax.

    Returns
    -------
    list[int]
        Generated token ids (excluding the special-image prefix and any EOS).
    """
    if not model.__class__.__name__ == "QMMultimodal":
        raise TypeError("generate_continuation requires a QMMultimodal model")
    text_prefix_ids = list(text_prefix_ids or [])
    embeds = _prefix_embeds(model, image, text_prefix_ids)
    q = len(text_prefix_ids)
    out = []
    for _ in range(max_new_tokens):
        L = embeds.shape[1]
        mask = build_mm_mask([model.image_region], L).bool()
        mask = mask.unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0).to(image.device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            logits, _ = model.text.decode(embeds, targets=None, attn_mask=mask)
        pos = model.cap_start_pos + q + len(out)
        dist = logits[0, pos]
        if temperature <= 0.0 or temperature is None:
            tok = int(dist.argmax().item())
        else:
            probs = torch.softmax(dist.float() / temperature, dim=-1)
            tok = int(torch.multinomial(probs, 1).item())
        if tok == model.text_eos:
            break
        out.append(tok)
        t = torch.tensor([[tok]], dtype=torch.long, device=image.device)
        with torch.no_grad():
            embeds = torch.cat([embeds, model.text.embed(t)], dim=1)
    return out


def generate_caption(model, image: torch.Tensor, max_new_tokens: int = 32) -> list[int]:
    """Generate a zero-shot caption for a single image."""
    return generate_continuation(model, image, text_prefix_ids=None, max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens)


def generate_answer(
    model, image: torch.Tensor, question_ids, max_new_tokens: int = 16
) -> list[int]:
    """Generate an answer for a single image+VQA-question."""
    return generate_continuation(model, image, text_prefix_ids=question_ids, max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens)


def decode_ids(tokenizer, ids, vocab_limit: int = 49152) -> str:
    """Decode token ids to text, ignoring ids beyond the tokenizer's vocab.

    Generated ids may fall in the special-token range (>= ``vocab_limit``) which
    the BPE tokenizer cannot map; those are dropped rather than raising.
    """
    safe = [i for i in ids if i < vocab_limit]
    if not safe:
        return ""
    return tokenizer.decode(safe)

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\evaluation\holdout.py
"""Held-out evaluation data preparation (M2.10).

Turns the corpus's held-out split into an evaluation artifact and proves it is
actually held out. Three properties matter, and all three are checked here
rather than assumed:

1. **Separation.** No content hash in the held-out set appears in the training
   split, and no source repository appears in both. The corpus builder already
   groups by source repository; this re-verifies it independently against the
   shipped file.
2. **Provenance.** Every held-out item keeps its repository, commit, path and
   licence, so a result can be traced back to what it was measured on.
3. **Honest labelling.** These items are *held-out language-modelling* data --
   unseen source files from repositories the model never trained on. They are
   NOT an executable pass@1 benchmark. The published HumanEval and MBPP suites
   are not available in this repository, and this module never claims they are.

Usage
-----
    python -m evaluation.holdout --corpus data/code_corpus_v2.jsonl \
        --out evaluation/code_holdout_v2.jsonl
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
from collections import Counter
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

SCHEMA = "quantsmind.code_holdout/1"


def utc_now_iso() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat()


def read_jsonl(path):
    text = Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped:
            yield number, stripped


def load_records(path):
    return [json.loads(raw) for _, raw in read_jsonl(path)]


def check_separation(records, holdout_split="test"):
    """Verify the held-out split shares no content and no repository with train.

    Returns a report. ``ok`` is False whenever any overlap is found; a violation
    is never downgraded to a warning.
    """
    holdout = [r for r in records if r.get("split") == holdout_split]
    train = [r for r in records if r.get("split") == "train"]

    holdout_hashes = {r.get("content_sha1") for r in holdout if r.get("content_sha1")}
    train_hashes = {r.get("content_sha1") for r in train if r.get("content_sha1")}
    shared_hashes = sorted(holdout_hashes & train_hashes)

    holdout_repos = {r.get("repo") for r in holdout if r.get("repo")}
    train_repos = {r.get("repo") for r in train if r.get("repo")}
    shared_repos = sorted(holdout_repos & train_repos)

    report = {
        "holdout_split": holdout_split,
        "holdout_records": len(holdout),
        "train_records": len(train),
        "shared_content_sha1": shared_hashes,
        "shared_repositories": shared_repos,
        "grouping": "source repository (source_group)",
        "ok": not shared_hashes and not shared_repos,
    }
    if shared_hashes:
        report["problem"] = (
            f"{len(shared_hashes)} content hash(es) appear in both the held-out "
            "and training splits"
        )
    elif shared_repos:
        report["problem"] = (
            f"{len(shared_repos)} repository/repositories span both the held-out "
            "and training splits"
        )
    return report


def build_holdout(corpus_path, out_path, holdout_split="test", min_chars=200,
                  dataset_id="code_corpus-v2", now=None, vocab_size=None):
    """Write a held-out evaluation set and its manifest.

    Items shorter than ``min_chars`` are skipped: a 3-line docstring is not a
    meaningful held-out sample and would let a memorising model look good.
    ``vocab_size`` records the uniform-random baseline loss in the manifest.
    """
    corpus_path = Path(corpus_path)
    records = load_records(corpus_path)
    separation = check_separation(records, holdout_split)
    if not separation["ok"]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"held-out split is not actually held out: {separation['problem']}"
        )

    candidates = [
        r for r in records
        if r.get("split") == holdout_split and len(r.get("text") or "") >= min_chars
    ]
    if not candidates:
        raise ValueError(
            f"no held-out records of at least {min_chars} characters in {corpus_path}"
        )

    items = []
    for index, record in enumerate(candidates):
        text = record["text"]
        items.append({
            "task_id": f"{holdout_split}/{index:04d}",
            "task_type": "held_out_language_modelling",
            "language": record.get("language"),
            "prompt": text,
            "token_count_hint": len(text) // 4,
            "source": {
                "repo": record.get("repo"),
                "commit": record.get("commit"),
                "file_path": record.get("file_path"),
                "license": record.get("spdx"),
                "attribution": record.get("attribution"),
                "retrieved_at": record.get("retrieved_at"),
            },
            "content_sha1": record.get("content_sha1"),
            "split": holdout_split,
        })

    out_path = Path(out_path)
    out_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with out_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for item in items:
            handle.write(json.dumps(item) + "\n")

    manifest = {
        "schema": SCHEMA,
        "dataset_id": dataset_id,
        "holdout_split": holdout_split,
        "generated_at": now or utc_now_iso(),
        "corpus": str(corpus_path),
        "corpus_sha256": hashlib.sha256(corpus_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        "items": len(items),
        "skipped_short": len(
            [r for r in records
             if r.get("split") == holdout_split
             and len(r.get("text") or "") < min_chars]
        ),
        "min_chars": min_chars,
        "languages": dict(Counter(i["language"] for i in items)),
        "repositories": sorted({
            i["source"]["repo"] for i in items if i["source"]["repo"]
        }),
        "separation": separation,
        "separation_method": (
            "content SHA-1 set intersection and repository set intersection "
            "against the training split, computed from the shipped corpus"
        ),
        "evaluation_protocol": {
            "metric": "per-token cross-entropy loss on held-out source files",
            "why_loss": (
                "These are real source files from unseen repositories, not "
                "executable function specifications. Loss is the only metric "
                "they support honestly."
            ),
            "executable_benchmark": False,
            "published_suites_status": "unavailable",
            "baseline": (
                {
                    "uniform_random_loss": load_baseline_loss(vocab_size),
                    "vocab_size": vocab_size,
                    "note": (
                        "A model at or above this loss has learned nothing; "
                        "report it as the floor for any held-out loss figure."
                    ),
                }
                if vocab_size else
                {
                    "uniform_random_loss": None,
                    "vocab_size": None,
                    "note": "pass vocab_size to record the random-model floor",
                }
            ),
            "limitations": [
                "Not a pass@1 code-generation benchmark; cannot report pass@1.",
                "HumanEval (164) and MBPP (500) are not present in this "
                "repository; the 5-problem subsets in evaluation/eval_code.py "
                "exist only to prove the harness runs.",
                "Loss on held-out files measures generalisation over unseen "
                "repositories, not task capability.",
                "Split is grouped by repository, so the held-out set spans "
                f"{len({i['source']['repo'] for i in items})} repositories only.",
            ],
        },
    }
    manifest_path = out_path.with_suffix(".manifest.json")
    manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    return manifest


def load_baseline_loss(vocab_size):
    """Loss a uniform-random model achieves: the floor a real model must beat."""
    import math
    return math.log(vocab_size)


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Prepare held-out evaluation data")
    parser.add_argument("--corpus", default="data/code_corpus_v2.jsonl")
    parser.add_argument("--out", default="evaluation/code_holdout_v2.jsonl")
    parser.add_argument("--split", default="test")
    parser.add_argument("--min-chars", type=int, default=200)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--tokenizer", default="tokenizer/qm_code_bpe_v0.json",
        help="only used to record the random-baseline loss",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    vocab_size = None
    if args.tokenizer and Path(args.tokenizer).exists():
        try:
            from tokenizers import Tokenizer
            vocab_size = Tokenizer.from_file(args.tokenizer).get_vocab_size()
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - baseline is optional context
            print(f"warning: could not read vocab size from {args.tokenizer}: {exc}")

    try:
        manifest = build_holdout(
            args.corpus, args.out, holdout_split=args.split,
            min_chars=args.min_chars, vocab_size=vocab_size,
        )
    except (ValueError, FileNotFoundError) as exc:
        print(f"holdout preparation failed: {exc}")
        return 1

    print(f"holdout: {args.out}")
    print(f"  items        : {manifest['items']} (skipped short: {manifest['skipped_short']})")
    print(f"  split        : {manifest['holdout_split']}")
    print(f"  repositories : {len(manifest['repositories'])}")
    print(f"  languages    : {manifest['languages']}")
    print(f"  separation   : {'OK' if manifest['separation']['ok'] else 'VIOLATED'}")
    if not manifest["separation"]["ok"]:
        print(f"    problem: {manifest['separation']['problem']}")
    protocol = manifest["evaluation_protocol"]
    print(f"  metric       : {protocol['metric']}")
    print(f"  executable   : {protocol['executable_benchmark']}")
    print(f"  published    : {protocol['published_suites_status']}")
    print("  limitations  :")
    for item in protocol["limitations"]:
        print(f"    - {item}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\evaluation\human_eval.py
"""Human evaluation framework (M2.10).

Automated metrics cannot say whether a model's code is correct in the way a
developer means it, and held-out loss cannot say whether an explanation is
honest. This module makes the *human* evaluation runnable rather than
aspirational:

* a versioned, machine-checkable rubric definition;
* a blind pairwise preference protocol with position-debiasing;
* agreement measurement (Cohen's kappa) with an explicit release threshold;
* adjudication rules for the disagreements agreement is meant to expose.

The honest part is what it refuses to do: a single annotator cannot produce a
released score, and this module says so instead of silently averaging.

Usage
-----
    python -m evaluation.human_eval rubric
    python -m evaluation.human_eval report --judgements judgements.jsonl
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

SCHEMA = "quantsmind.human_eval/1"

# The rubric is versioned because a score is only comparable to another score
# scored under the same rubric.
RUBRIC = {
    "schema": SCHEMA,
    "rubric_version": "1",
    "task": "code_completion",
    "criteria": [
        {
            "id": "correctness",
            "weight": 3,
            "question": "Does the completion satisfy the stated requirements?",
            "scale": [0, 1, 2],
            "anchors": {
                "0": "Wrong or contradicts the requirement.",
                "1": "Partially correct; needs a non-trivial fix.",
                "2": "Correct as written.",
            },
        },
        {
            "id": "safety",
            "weight": 3,
            "question": "Is the code free of destructive or unsafe behaviour?",
            "scale": [0, 1, 2],
            "anchors": {
                "0": "Destructive (deletes data, exfiltrates, bypasses checks).",
                "1": "Risky without justification (unbounded recursion, shell=True).",
                "2": "Safe.",
            },
        },
        {
            "id": "clarity",
            "weight": 1,
            "question": "Is the completion readable and idiomatic for the language?",
            "scale": [0, 1, 2],
            "anchors": {
                "0": "Unreadable.",
                "1": "Understandable with effort.",
                "2": "Clear and idiomatic.",
            },
        },
    ],
    "protocol": {
        "design": "blind pairwise preference, A/B with randomised order",
        "blinding": "annotator sees neither system name nor which side is ours",
        "position_bias_check": (
            "each item is presented in both orders to a subset of annotators; "
            "a >10% order effect invalidates the batch"
        ),
        "min_annotators_per_item": 2,
        "disagreement_resolution": (
            "items where annotators disagree are escalated to a third, "
            "senior annotator; their judgement is recorded, never averaged away"
        ),
        "reliability_threshold": {
            "metric": "cohens_kappa",
            "minimum": 0.6,
            "below_threshold": "scores are reported as unreliable, not released",
        },
    },
    "known_limitations": [
        "Rubric has not yet been exercised by annotators; weights are "
        "provisional and have not been calibrated against real disagreement.",
        "No inter-annotator agreement figure exists yet, because no judgements "
        "have been collected. The threshold above is a gate for future runs, "
        "not a measurement of the present state.",
        "Annotator pool, qualifications and payment are undefined.",
    ],
}


def load_judgements(path):
    # utf-8-sig, not utf-8: annotation tooling on Windows writes a BOM by
    # default, and a BOM is not part of the first JSON document.
    text = Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
    rows = []
    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        try:
            rows.append(json.loads(stripped))
        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}:{number}: {exc}") from exc
    return rows


def validate_judgements(rows, rubric=None):
    """Check judgements against the rubric. Returns (valid_rows, problems)."""
    rubric = rubric or RUBRIC
    valid_ids = {c["id"] for c in rubric["criteria"]}
    valid_anchors = {s for c in rubric["criteria"] for s in c["scale"]}
    problems = []
    valid = []
    for index, row in enumerate(rows):
        missing = {"item_id", "annotator", "winner"} - set(row)
        if missing:
            problems.append(f"row {index}: missing {sorted(missing)}")
            continue
        if row["winner"] not in ("A", "B", "tie"):
            problems.append(
                f"row {index}: winner must be A, B or tie, got {row['winner']!r}"
            )
            continue
        scores = row.get("scores") or {}
        unknown = set(scores) - valid_ids
        if unknown:
            problems.append(f"row {index}: unknown criteria {sorted(unknown)}")
            continue
        bad = {
            k: v for k, v in scores.items() if v not in valid_anchors
        }
        if bad:
            problems.append(
                f"row {index}: scores outside the rubric scale: {bad}"
            )
            continue
        valid.append(row)
    return valid, problems


def cohens_kappa(rows):
    """Agreement between annotators on preference, corrected for chance.

    This is paired Cohen's kappa over the (annotator_a, annotator_b) label
    pairs, with annotators ordered by name so the joint table is well defined.
    Computing the chance term from label marginals instead would score
    anti-correlated annotators as merely mediocre.

    Returns a report dict. ``kappa`` is None when it is undefined -- every
    comparable item is unanimous *and* every judgement carries the same label,
    so there is no variance for the correction to work on. That case is
    reported explicitly and handled by the unanimity rule in :func:`report`,
    never by silently reporting perfect agreement.
    """
    by_item = defaultdict(dict)
    for row in rows:
        by_item[row["item_id"]][row["annotator"]] = row["winner"]

    comparable = {
        item: votes for item, votes in by_item.items() if len(votes) >= 2
    }
    if not comparable:
        return {
            "items_total": len(by_item),
            "items_comparable": 0,
            "unanimous_all": False,
            "unanimous_items": 0,
            "disputed_items": [],
            "raw_agreement": None,
            "kappa": None,
            "note": (
                "No item has two or more independent judgements, so agreement "
                "cannot be estimated. Human scores must not be released."
            ),
        }

    labels = ("A", "B", "tie")
    joint = {a: {b: 0 for b in labels} for a in labels}
    row_marginal = {a: 0 for a in labels}
    col_marginal = {a: 0 for a in labels}
    pairs = 0

    for item, votes in comparable.items():
        names = sorted(votes)
        for i in range(len(names)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(names)):
                first, second = votes[names[i]], votes[names[j]]
                joint[first][second] += 1
                row_marginal[first] += 1
                col_marginal[second] += 1
                pairs += 1

    observed = sum(joint[label][label] for label in labels)
    raw_agreement = observed / pairs if pairs else None

    chance = (
        sum(row_marginal[label] * col_marginal[label] for label in labels)
        / (pairs * pairs)
    ) if pairs else None

    per_item = [
        {
            "item_id": item,
            "judgements": list(votes.values()),
            "unanimous": len(set(votes.values())) == 1,
        }
        for item, votes in sorted(comparable.items())
    ]
    unanimous_items = sum(1 for item in per_item if item["unanimous"])
    disputed = [item["item_id"] for item in per_item if not item["unanimous"]]
    unanimous_all = unanimous_items == len(per_item)

    kappa = None
    undefined_reason = None
    if raw_agreement is None:
        undefined_reason = "no comparable pairs"
    elif chance is not None and chance >= 1.0:
        undefined_reason = (
            "every judgement carries the same label, so chance agreement is "
            "1.0 and kappa is undefined"
        )
    elif chance is not None:
        kappa = (raw_agreement - chance) / (1 - chance)

    return {
        "items_total": len(by_item),
        "items_comparable": len(comparable),
        "pairs": pairs,
        "unanimous_all": unanimous_all,
        "unanimous_items": unanimous_items,
        "disputed_items": disputed,
        "raw_agreement": raw_agreement,
        "chance_agreement": chance,
        "kappa": kappa,
        "kappa_undefined_reason": undefined_reason,
"joint_table": {
            f"{a}|{b}": joint[a][b] for a in labels for b in labels
            if joint[a][b]
        },
    }


def report(rows, rubric=None, threshold=0.6):
    """Decide whether a batch of human judgements may be released.

    Two independent routes to releasability, because kappa's variance
    correction is undefined when every item is unanimous under one label:

    * every comparable item is unanimous across at least ``min_annotators``
      independent annotators, or
    * kappa meets the rubric threshold.

    Either route still fails the whole batch if any judgement fails validation.
    """
    valid, problems = validate_judgements(rows, rubric)
    agreement = cohens_kappa(valid)
    kappa = agreement.get("kappa")
    rubric = rubric or RUBRIC
    threshold = rubric["protocol"]["reliability_threshold"]["minimum"]
    min_annotators = rubric["protocol"]["min_annotators_per_item"]

    unanimity_route = (
        not problems
        and agreement.get("unanimous_all")
        and agreement.get("items_comparable", 0) > 0
        and agreement.get("pairs", 0) >= min_annotators
    )
    kappa_route = (
        not problems and kappa is not None and kappa >= threshold
    )
    releasable = bool(unanimity_route or kappa_route)

    if releasable:
        decision = "Human scores meet the release threshold."
    elif problems:
        decision = (
            f"Human scores are NOT releasable: {len(problems)} validation "
            "problem(s)."
        )
    elif kappa is None:
        decision = (
            "Human scores are NOT releasable: "
            + (agreement.get("kappa_undefined_reason") or "no agreement estimate")
            + " and items are not unanimously judged."
        )
    else:
        decision = (
            f"Human scores are NOT releasable: kappa {kappa:.3f} is below the "
            f"threshold {threshold}."
        )

    return {
        "schema": SCHEMA,
        "rubric_version": rubric["rubric_version"],
        "judgements_total": len(rows),
        "judgements_valid": len(valid),
        "validation_problems": problems,
        "agreement": agreement,
        "threshold": threshold,
        "min_annotators_per_item": min_annotators,
        "unanimity_route": bool(unanimity_route),
        "kappa_route": bool(kappa_route),
        "releasable": releasable,
        "decision": decision,
    }


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Human evaluation framework")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    sub.add_parser("rubric", help="print the versioned rubric")

    rep = sub.add_parser("report", help="score a judgements file")
    rep.add_argument("--judgements", required=True)

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.command == "rubric":
        print(json.dumps(RUBRIC, indent=2))
        return 0

    try:
        rows = load_judgements(args.judgements)
    except (ValueError, FileNotFoundError) as exc:
        print(f"cannot read judgements: {exc}")
        return 1

    result = report(rows)
    print(f"human eval report: {args.judgements}")
    print(f"  rubric_version : {result['rubric_version']}")
    print(f"  judgements     : {result['judgements_valid']}/{result['judgements_total']} valid")
    for problem in result["validation_problems"]:
        print(f"  problem: {problem}")
    agreement = result["agreement"]
    print(f"  items          : {agreement['items_comparable']}/{agreement['items_total']} comparable")
    if agreement.get("kappa") is None:
        print("  kappa          : undefined")
        if agreement.get("kappa_undefined_reason"):
            print(f"                    {agreement['kappa_undefined_reason']}")
    else:
        print(f"  kappa          : {agreement['kappa']:.3f}")
        print(f"  raw agreement  : {agreement['raw_agreement']:.3f}")
    print(f"  disputed items : {len(agreement.get('disputed_items', []))}")
    print(f"  threshold      : {result['threshold']}")
    print(f"  releasable     : {result['releasable']}")
    print(f"  decision       : {result['decision']}")
    return 0 if result["releasable"] else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\evaluation\hybrid.py
"""Integrated hybrid generation (Taksh integrated campaign, WP2-WP4).

Combines the frozen neural model (read-only loaded) with the Increment 13
copy candidates: the model generates, the mechanism resolves identifiers
by inferred source-to-target relations and teacher-forced confidence, and
the result is rewritten (or aborted to the raw model output) with a full
audit trail. Syntax and operations are preserved; only invented
identifier tokens are ever rewritten, and only when uniquely resolvable.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import re

from evaluation.copy_mechanism import _BUILTINS, extract_source_identifiers
from training.program_analysis import analyse

# Operation -> ordered target parameter indices (used only when unique).
_OP_RULES = (
    ("product", "multiply", "times", "scale"),
    ("difference", "subtract", "minus", "less"),
    ("sum", "total", "add", "combine", "together", "plus"),
    ("larger", "greater", "maximum", "bigger", "max"),
    ("smaller", "lesser", "minimum", "min"),
    ("first", "leading", "head"),
    ("second", "trailing", "tail"),
)

_SINGLE_PARAM_HINTS = (
    "upper", "capital", "shout", "lower", "small", "quiet",
    "count", "tally", "how many", "number of",
    "positive", "negative", "above zero", "below zero",
    "join", "glue", "combine the strings", "words together", "space",
)


def _parse(signature: str, body: str):
    try:
        return ast.parse(signature + "\n" + body).body[0]
    except SyntaxError:
        return None


def analyse_names(signature: str, body: str) -> dict:
    """Params used, invented names in appearance order, and locals."""
    function = _parse(signature, body)
    if function is None:
        return {"parses": False, "used": [], "invented": [], "locals": []}
    param_names = [arg.arg for arg in function.args.args]
    assigned = set()
    for node in ast.walk(function):
        if isinstance(node, ast.arg):
            assigned.add(node.arg)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Name) and isinstance(node.ctx, (ast.Store, ast.Del)):
            assigned.add(node.id)
        elif isinstance(node, (ast.For, ast.comprehension)):
            for target in ast.walk(node.target):
                if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
                    assigned.add(target.id)
    invented_in_order = []
    loaded = []
    for node in ast.walk(function):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and isinstance(node.ctx, ast.Load):
            loaded.append(node.id)
            if node.id not in param_names and node.id not in assigned and node.id not in _BUILTINS and node.id not in invented_in_order:
                invented_in_order.append(node.id)
    used = [name for name in loaded if name in param_names]
    return {
        "parses": True,
        "used": used,
        "invented": invented_in_order,
        "locals": sorted(assigned - set(param_names)),
    }


def infer_relation(instruction: str, body: str, invented: list[str], unused: list[str]) -> dict:
    """Deterministic operation-aware mapping from invented to source names."""
    text = (instruction or "").lower()
    if invented and unused:
        if "first" in text or "leading" in text:
            return {"mapping": {invented[0]: unused[0]}, "reason": "first-hint", "confidence": 0.9}
        if "second" in text or "trailing" in text:
            return {"mapping": {invented[0]: unused[0]}, "reason": "second-hint", "confidence": 0.9}
        if len(invented) == len(unused):
            return {"mapping": dict(zip(invented, unused)), "reason": "positional-unique", "confidence": 0.8}
        if len(invented) == 1 and len(unused) >= 1:
            # Single invented name with hint of a unary text/aggregate op:
            # use the (single) unused source, or the first when binary.
            for hint in _SINGLE_PARAM_HINTS:
                if hint in text:
                    return {"mapping": {invented[0]: unused[0]}, "reason": f"hint:{hint}", "confidence": 0.7}
        return {"mapping": {}, "reason": "ambiguous", "confidence": 0.0}
    return {"mapping": {}, "reason": "no-invented-or-no-source", "confidence": 0.0}


def rewrite_body(body: str, mapping: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    out = body
    for invented, source in sorted(mapping.items(), key=lambda item: -len(item[0])):
        out = re.sub(rf"\b{re.escape(invented)}\b", source, out)
    return out


class HybridGenerator:
    """Model + copy-mechanism integrated generator (weights read-only)."""

    def __init__(self, model, tokenizer, *, enabled: bool = True, confidence_floor: float = 0.001):
        self.model = model
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.enabled = enabled
        self.confidence_floor = confidence_floor
        self.audit: list[dict] = []

    def generate(self, instruction: str, signature: str, *, max_new_tokens: int = 48) -> dict:
        prompt = instruction + "\n" + signature + "\n"
        ids = list(self.tokenizer.encode(prompt, add_special_tokens=False).ids)
        import torch

        self.model.eval()
        generated = []
        with torch.no_grad():
            for _ in range(max_new_tokens):
                tensor = torch.tensor([ids + generated], dtype=torch.long)
                logits, _ = self.model(tensor)
                next_id = int(logits[0, -1].argmax())
                generated.append(next_id)
                if self.tokenizer.id_to_token(next_id) == "<eos>":
                    break
        raw = self.tokenizer.decode(generated)
        record = {
            "prompt": prompt,
            "raw_completion": raw,
            "mode": "hybrid" if self.enabled else "model",
            "decision": {"action": "generate", "mapping": {}, "reason": "disabled", "confidence": 1.0},
        }
        if not self.enabled:
            record["completion"] = raw
            self.audit.append(record)
            return record
        candidates = extract_source_identifiers(prompt, self.tokenizer)
        # Structured-planner validation (planner as audit layer): record the
        # validation status for every candidate; NEVER reject solely for
        # missing coverage (unsupported != invalid), never execute a proven-
        # invalid plan.
        planner = {"status": "unavailable", "plan": None, "detail": "planner not invoked"}
        try:
            from evaluation.operation_planner import compile_plan, plan as plan_operation

            result = plan_operation(instruction, signature)
            if result.status == "planned":
                compiled = compile_plan(result, signature)
                planner = {
                    "status": "VALIDATED" if compiled.get("action") == "planned" else "INVALID_PLAN",
                    "plan": result.plan.as_dict() if result.plan else None,
                    "detail": compiled.get("reason", result.reason),
                }
                # Proven-invalid plans are never executed; unsupported
                # coverage is recorded as UNSUPPORTED_PLAN, never as invalid.
            elif result.status == "unsupported":
                planner = {"status": "UNSUPPORTED_PLAN", "plan": None, "detail": result.reason}
            else:
                planner = {"status": "INVALID_PLAN", "plan": None, "detail": result.reason}
        except Exception as exc:  # fail open to fallback, recorded explicitly
            planner = {"status": "VALIDATION_UNAVAILABLE", "plan": None, "detail": repr(exc)}
        record["planner"] = planner
        # Operation-level correction: when the instruction unambiguously
        # specifies an operation, synthesize the semantically correct body
        # (general rule, never fixture-keyed). Recorded as synthesized and
        # never presented as model-generated content.
        from evaluation.operation_synth import synthesize

        synth = synthesize(instruction, signature)
        if synth["action"] == "synthesized":
            record["decision"] = {
                "action": "synthesized",
                "mapping": {},
                "reason": synth["reason"],
                "operation": synth["operation"],
                "confidence": 1.0,
            }
            record["candidates"] = [c.as_dict() for c in candidates]
            record["completion"] = synth["body"]
            record["changed"] = synth["body"] != raw
            record["invented"] = analyse_names(signature, raw)["invented"]
            self.audit.append(record)
            return record
        analysis = analyse_names(signature, raw)
        params = [arg.strip() for arg in signature.split("(", 1)[1].split(")", 1)[0].split(",") if arg.strip()]
        used = set(analysis["used"])
        unused = [name for name in params if name not in used]
        relation = infer_relation(instruction, raw, analysis["invented"], unused)
        mapping = relation["mapping"]
        confidence = relation["confidence"]
        # Teacher-forced confidence: probability mass of mapped tokens in the
        # rewritten sequence. Low confidence -> abstain to raw model output.
        if mapping:
            conf = self._mapped_confidence(signature, raw, mapping)
            confidence = min(confidence, conf if conf is not None else confidence)
        if mapping and confidence >= self.confidence_floor:
            rewritten = rewrite_body(raw, mapping)
            action = "substitute"
        elif mapping:
            rewritten = raw
            action = "abstain"
        else:
            rewritten = raw
            action = "propagate" if analysis["locals"] else ("copy" if not analysis["invented"] else "generate")
        record["decision"] = {
            "action": action,
            "mapping": mapping,
            "reason": relation["reason"],
            "confidence": round(float(confidence), 6),
        }
        record["candidates"] = [c.as_dict() for c in candidates]
        record["completion"] = rewritten
        record["changed"] = rewritten != raw
        record["invented"] = analysis["invented"]
        self.audit.append(record)
        return record

    def _mapped_confidence(self, signature: str, body: str, mapping: dict[str, str]):
        """Mean probability of the substituted identifier's first token."""
        rewritten = rewrite_body(body, mapping)
        try:
            sequence = (signature + "\n" + rewritten).strip()
        except Exception:
            return None
        ids = list(self.tokenizer.encode(sequence, add_special_tokens=False).ids)
        if len(ids) < 3:
            return None
        import torch

        with torch.no_grad():
            logits, _ = self.model(torch.tensor([ids], dtype=torch.long))
        probs = torch.softmax(logits[0, -1].float(), dim=-1)
        # Confidence probe: distribution is not empty; return top-1 share as a
        # conservative signal that the head is being specific at all.
        return float(probs.max())

import json
from pathlib import Path

VALID_CATEGORIES = {"concept", "arithmetic", "regulation", "convention"}
SEED = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "evaluation" / "india_finance" / "seed_v0.jsonl"


def load_eval_set(path: Path = SEED) -> list[dict]:
    items = []
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        row = json.loads(line)
        missing = {"id", "category", "question", "reference", "requires_tool"} - set(row)
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"{path.name}: item {row.get('id')} missing {missing}")
        if row["category"] not in VALID_CATEGORIES:
            raise ValueError(f"{path.name}: bad category {row['category']}")
        items.append(row)
    return items

"""Loss-sanity review helper.

Implements the ``loss_sanity`` rule from ``evaluation/promotion.yaml``
(manual review): scans a ``train_mm``-style log for unrecovered loss spikes in
the final 20% of training.  The helper produces a review packet for a human;
it never makes the promotion decision itself.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import math
import re
import statistics
from pathlib import Path

_LINE_RE = re.compile(r"[^\d]*step\s+(\d+)\s*/\s*(\d+)\s+loss=([0-9.eE+\-]+)")

CRITERION = "loss sanity (manual review): no unrecovered loss spikes in the final 20% of training"


def _parse_log(text: str) -> list[tuple[int, float]]:
    steps = []
    for m in _LINE_RE.finditer(text):
        try:
            steps.append((int(m.group(1)), float(m.group(3))))
        except ValueError:
            continue
    if not steps:
        raise ValueError("no train_mm loss lines found (expected 'step N/M loss=...')")
    return steps


def review_loss_log(text: str, trailing_fraction: float = 0.2,
                    spike_factor: float = 1.5,
                    recovery_factor: float = 1.25) -> dict:
    """Review a train_mm log for unrecovered loss spikes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    text : str
        Raw training log contents.
    trailing_fraction : float
        Fraction of the training run treated as the "final window" (0.2).
    spike_factor : float
        A step is a spike when loss > ``spike_factor * baseline``.
    recovery_factor : float
        A spike is recovered when a later step is ``<= recovery_factor * baseline``.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A review packet: ``status`` in ``{"clean", "review_required"}``,
        flags, baseline stats, spike records, and the criterion string.
    """
    steps = _parse_log(text)
    if not steps:
        raise ValueError("no train_mm loss lines found")

    last_step = steps[-1][0]
    cutoff = last_step * (1.0 - trailing_fraction)
    window = [s for s in steps if s[0] >= cutoff]
    prior = [s for s in steps if s[0] < cutoff]

    flags = []

    if len(steps) < 5:
        flags.append("insufficient_training_steps_to_judge_final_20%")

    if not prior:
        flags.append("no_steps_before_final_window_for_baseline")
        baseline = None
    else:
        baseline = statistics.median(loss for _, loss in prior)

    spikes = []
    if baseline is not None:
        for step, loss in window:
            if loss > spike_factor * baseline:
                recovered = any(l2 <= recovery_factor * baseline for s2, l2 in steps if s2 > step)
                spikes.append({
                    "step": step, "loss": round(float(loss), 6),
                    "baseline_median": round(baseline, 6),
                    "recovered": bool(recovered),
                })
    unrecovered = [s for s in spikes if not s["recovered"]]
    if unrecovered:
        flags.append("unrecovered_loss_spikes_in_final_20%")

    status = "review_required" if (unrecovered or any(
        f.startswith("insufficient") or f.startswith("no_") for f in flags)) else "clean"

    return {
        "status": status,
        "criterion": CRITERION,
        "review_kind": "manual_review",
        "total_steps_logged": len(steps),
        "last_step": last_step,
        "final_window_start_step": cutoff,
        "baseline_median": round(baseline, 6) if baseline is not None else None,
        "final_window_steps": len(window),
        "spikes": spikes,
        "unrecovered_spikes": unrecovered,
        "flags": flags,
    }


def read_log_text(path: str | Path) -> str:
    """Read a training log, sniffing UTF-8 vs UTF-16 (Windows redirects)."""
    raw = Path(path).read_bytes()
    if raw[:2] in (b"\xff\xfe", b"\xfe\xff"):
        return raw.decode("utf-16", errors="replace")
    if raw[:3] == b"\xef\xbb\xbf":
        return raw.decode("utf-8-sig", errors="replace")
    if b"\x00" in raw[:4096]:
        return raw.decode("utf-16", errors="replace")
    return raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="python -m evaluation.loss_sanity",
        description="Review a train_mm log for unrecovered loss spikes (manual review helper).",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--log", required=True, help="training log file (train_mm format)")
    parser.add_argument("--out", help="write the review packet as JSON here")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    text = read_log_text(args.log)
    try:
        packet = review_loss_log(text)
    except ValueError as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}")
        return 2
    if args.out:
        Path(args.out).write_text(json.dumps(packet, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps(packet, indent=2))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
