# Number of semantically equivalent surface variants per operation.
VARIANT_COUNT = 4


def _body(operation: str, params: tuple[str, ...], variant: int) -> str:
    """Return one of four equivalent surface forms for ``operation``."""
    variant %= VARIANT_COUNT
    if operation == "add":
        a, b = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    return {a} + {b}"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    total = {a} + {b}\n    return total"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    result = {a}\n    result += {b}\n    return result"
        return f"    return {b} + {a}"
    if operation == "subtract":
        a, b = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    return {a} - {b}"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    difference = {a} - {b}\n    return difference"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    result = {a}\n    result -= {b}\n    return result"
        return f"    return {a} + (-{b})"
    if operation == "multiply":
        a, b = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    return {a} * {b}"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    product = {a} * {b}\n    return product"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    result = {a}\n    result *= {b}\n    return result"
        return f"    return {b} * {a}"
    if operation == "maximum":
        a, b = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    if {a} > {b}:\n        return {a}\n    return {b}"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    return {a} if {a} > {b} else {b}"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    chosen = {a}\n    if {b} > chosen:\n        chosen = {b}\n    return chosen"
        return f"    return {a} if {a} >= {b} else {b}"
    if operation == "minimum":
        a, b = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    if {a} < {b}:\n        return {a}\n    return {b}"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    return {a} if {a} < {b} else {b}"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    chosen = {a}\n    if {b} < chosen:\n        chosen = {b}\n    return chosen"
        return f"    return {a} if {a} <= {b} else {b}"
    if operation in ("keep_positive", "keep_negative"):
        (value,) = params
        symbol = ">" if operation == "keep_positive" else "<"
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    return [item for item in {value} if item {symbol} 0]"
        if variant == 1:
            return (
                f"    result = []\n"
                f"    for item in {value}:\n"
                f"        if item {symbol} 0:\n"
                f"            result.append(item)\n"
                f"    return result"
            )
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    result = []\n    result.extend(item for item in {value} if item {symbol} 0)\n    return result"
        return (
            f"    result = []\n"
            f"    index = 0\n"
            f"    while index < len({value}):\n"
            f"        item = {value}[index]\n"
            f"        if item {symbol} 0:\n"
            f"            result.append(item)\n"
            f"        index += 1\n"
            f"    return result"
        )
    if operation in ("upper", "lower"):
        (text,) = params
        method = "upper" if operation == "upper" else "lower"
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    return {text}.{method}()"
        if variant == 1:
            local = "shouted" if operation == "upper" else "quieted"
            return f"    {local} = {text}.{method}()\n    return {local}"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    if {text}:\n        return {text}.{method}()\n    return {text}"
        return f'    return f"{{{text}}}".{method}()'
    if operation == "count_values":
        (items,) = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    count = 0\n    for item in {items}:\n        count += 1\n    return count"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    return len({items})"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    return sum(1 for item in {items})"
        return (
            f"    count = 0\n"
            f"    index = 0\n"
            f"    while index < len({items}):\n"
            f"        count += 1\n"
            f"        index += 1\n"
            f"    return count"
        )
    if operation == "sum_values":
        (items,) = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    total = 0\n    for item in {items}:\n        total += item\n    return total"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    return sum({items})"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    return sum(item for item in {items})"
        return (
            f"    total = 0\n"
            f"    index = 0\n"
            f"    while index < len({items}):\n"
            f"        total += {items}[index]\n"
            f"        index += 1\n"
            f"    return total"
        )
    if operation == "choose_first":
        first, _second = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    return {first}"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    chosen = {first}\n    return chosen"
        if variant == 2:
            return f'    """Return the first value."""\n    return {first}'
        return f"    chosen = {first}\n    if True:\n        return chosen\n    return {first}"
    if operation == "choose_second":
        _first, second = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    return {second}"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    chosen = {second}\n    return chosen"
        if variant == 2:
            return f'    """Return the second value."""\n    return {second}'
        return f"    chosen = {second}\n    if True:\n        return chosen\n    return {second}"
    raise ValueError(f"unknown binding operation: {operation}")


def _signature(operation: str, function_name: str, params: tuple[str, ...]) -> str:
    return f"def {function_name}({', '.join(params)}):"


def _validate(signature: str, body: str) -> None:
    source = signature + "\n" + body
    tree = ast.parse(source)
    if len(tree.body) != 1 or not isinstance(tree.body[0], ast.FunctionDef):
        raise ValueError("example did not parse as one function")
    params = [arg.arg for arg in tree.body[0].args.args]
    assigned: set[str] = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree.body[0]):
        if isinstance(node, ast.arg):
            assigned.add(node.arg)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Name) and isinstance(node.ctx, (ast.Store, ast.Del)):
            assigned.add(node.id)
        elif isinstance(node, (ast.For, ast.comprehension)):
            for target_node in ast.walk(node.target):
                if isinstance(target_node, ast.Name):
                    assigned.add(target_node.id)
    used = {node.id for node in ast.walk(tree.body[0]) if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and isinstance(node.ctx, ast.Load)}
    undefined = used - set(params) - assigned - {"len", "sum", "list", "str", "filter", "enumerate", "range"}
    if undefined:
        raise ValueError(f"example has undefined names: {sorted(undefined)}")


def build_examples(
    *,
    name_offset: int = 0,
    function_offset: int = 0,
    instruction_offset: int = 0,
    per_operation: int = 12,
    seed: int = 20261024,
    split: str = "train",
    id_prefix: str = "B1",
) -> list:
    examples = []
    for operation in TRAINED_OPERATIONS:
        instructions = _INSTRUCTIONS[operation]
        function_names = _FUNCTION_NAMES[operation]
        for index in range(per_operation):
            if operation in _TEXT_OPERATIONS:
                params = (_STRING_NAMES[(name_offset + index) % len(_STRING_NAMES)],)
            elif operation in ("keep_positive", "keep_negative", "count_values", "sum_values"):
                params = (_SEQUENCE_NAMES[(name_offset + index) % len(_SEQUENCE_NAMES)],)
            else:
                params = _NUMERIC_PAIRS[(name_offset + index) % len(_NUMERIC_PAIRS)]
            function_name = function_names[(function_offset + index) % len(function_names)]
            instruction = instructions[(instruction_offset + index) % len(instructions)]
            variant = index % VARIANT_COUNT
            signature = _signature(operation, function_name, params)
            body = _body(operation, params, variant)
            _validate(signature, body)
            example_id = f"{id_prefix}-{operation}-{index:03d}"
            examples.append(
                build_example(
                    example_id=example_id,
                    instruction=instruction,
                    signature=signature,
                    body=body,
                    operation=operation,
                    family=_FAMILIES[operation],
                    split=split,
                    seed=seed + index,
                    metadata={
                        "markers": [operation],
                        "binding_focus": True,
                        "variant": variant,
                        "surface_variant": f"v{variant}",
                    },
                )
            )
    return examples


def build_training_examples(*, seed: int = 20261024) -> list:
    return build_examples(name_offset=0, per_operation=12, seed=seed, split="train")


def build_validation_examples(*, seed: int = 20261025) -> list:
    # Rotated function names and a different name offset guarantee that no
    # (instruction, signature) pair can coincide with a training example.
    return build_examples(
        name_offset=5,
        function_offset=2,
        instruction_offset=1,
        per_operation=4,
        seed=seed,
        split="validation",
        id_prefix="V1",
    )


def curriculum_digest() -> str:
    payload = [
        (example.example_id, example.instruction, example.signature, example.body, example.operation)
        for example in build_training_examples()
    ]
    return hashlib.sha256(repr(payload).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\binding_repair.py
"""Conservative repair of free parameter names in generated completions.

Repairs are applied only when there is exactly one unbound name and exactly
one unused requested parameter. Any other shape is left unchanged. This module
is a deterministic source transform, never executes code, and abstains on
nested scopes, unknown calls, unsafe attributes, or ambiguous mappings.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import io
import re
import tokenize
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass

_SAFE_CALLS = frozenset({
    "len", "max", "min", "sum", "abs", "sorted", "range", "list", "dict",
    "set", "tuple", "str", "int", "float", "bool", "isinstance", "enumerate",
    "zip", "any", "all", "reversed", "round",
})
_SAFE_ATTRIBUTES = frozenset({
    "append", "extend", "get", "keys", "values", "items", "upper", "lower",
    "strip", "startswith", "endswith", "split", "join", "index", "count",
})
_SIGNATURE = re.compile(r"(?m)^(?P<signature>def\s+[A-Za-z_]\w*\([^\n]*\):)\s*$")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RepairInfo:
    completion: str
    status: str
    reason: str
    changed: bool
    mapping: dict[str, str]
    unbound: list[str]
    unused_params: list[str]

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        return asdict(self)


def extract_signature(prompt: str) -> str | None:
    matches = list(_SIGNATURE.finditer(prompt or ""))
    if not matches:
        matches = [item for item in re.finditer(r"def\s+[A-Za-z_]\w*\([^\n]*\):", prompt or "")]
    if not matches:
        return None
    return matches[-1].groupdict().get("signature") or matches[-1].group(0)


def _indent_body(completion: str) -> str:
    lines = [line.rstrip() for line in (completion or "").splitlines()]
    while lines and not lines[-1].strip():
        lines.pop()
    if not lines:
        return ""
    if lines[0] and not lines[0][0].isspace():
        lines = ["    " + line if line else line for line in lines]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _named_arguments(node: ast.FunctionDef) -> list[str]:
    args = node.args
    names = [arg.arg for arg in args.posonlyargs]
    names += [arg.arg for arg in args.args]
    names += [arg.arg for arg in args.kwonlyargs]
    if args.vararg:
        names.append(args.vararg.arg)
    if args.kwarg:
        names.append(args.kwarg.arg)
    return names


def _assigned_names(func: ast.FunctionDef) -> set[str]:
    assigned: set[str] = set()
    for node in ast.walk(func):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and isinstance(node.ctx, (ast.Store, ast.Del)):
            assigned.add(node.id)
        elif isinstance(node, (ast.For, ast.AsyncFor)):
            assigned.update(_target_names(node.target))
        elif isinstance(node, ast.comprehension):
            assigned.update(_target_names(node.target))
        elif isinstance(node, (ast.With, ast.AsyncWith)):
            for item in node.items:
                if item.optional_vars is not None:
                    assigned.update(_target_names(item.optional_vars))
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ExceptHandler) and node.name:
            assigned.add(node.name)
    return assigned


def _target_names(target: ast.AST | None) -> set[str]:
    if target is None:
        return set()
    names = set()
    for node in ast.walk(target):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
            names.add(node.id)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Starred):
            names.update(_target_names(node.value))
    return names


def _loaded_names_by_position(func: ast.FunctionDef) -> list[str]:
    nodes = [node for node in ast.walk(func)
             if isinstance(node, ast.Name) and isinstance(node.ctx, ast.Load)]
    nodes.sort(key=lambda node: (getattr(node, "lineno", 0), getattr(node, "col_offset", 0)))
    seen = set()
    ordered = []
    for node in nodes:
        if node.id not in seen:
            seen.add(node.id)
            ordered.append(node.id)
    return ordered


def _abstain(status: str, reason: str, completion: str,
             unbound: list[str] | None = None,
             unused_params: list[str] | None = None) -> RepairInfo:
    return RepairInfo(
        completion=completion, status=status, reason=reason, changed=False,
        mapping={}, unbound=list(unbound or []), unused_params=list(unused_params or []),
    )


def _unsafe_construct(tree: ast.Module, outer: ast.FunctionDef) -> str | None:
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.Lambda)) and node is not outer:
            return "nested scope or lambda"
        if isinstance(node, (ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom)):
            return "import statement"
        if isinstance(node, (ast.Global, ast.Nonlocal)):
            return "global/nonlocal declaration"
        if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
            if node.attr.startswith("_") or node.attr not in _SAFE_ATTRIBUTES:
                return f"unsafe attribute: {node.attr}"
        if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
            function = node.func
            if isinstance(function, ast.Name):
                if function.id not in _SAFE_CALLS:
                    return f"unsafe call: {function.id}"
            elif isinstance(function, ast.Attribute):
                if function.attr not in _SAFE_ATTRIBUTES:
                    return f"unsafe method: {function.attr}"
            else:
                return "unsafe call form"
    return None


def repair_completion_info(signature: str | None, completion: str) -> RepairInfo:
    if not signature:
        return _abstain("abstained_no_signature", "no signature available", completion)
    if not completion.strip():
        return _abstain("abstained_empty_source", "empty completion", completion)
    signature = signature.rstrip("\n")
    stripped = completion.lstrip()
    if stripped.startswith("def "):
        return _abstain("abstained_full_function", "whole-function completions are left unchanged", completion)

    body = _indent_body(completion)
    source = signature + "\n" + body
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(source)
    except SyntaxError as exc:
        return _abstain("abstained_parse_error", f"syntax error: {exc}", completion)
    functions = [node for node in tree.body if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef)]
    if len(functions) != 1:
        return _abstain("abstained_structure", "expected one function definition", completion)
    func = functions[0]

    unsafe = _unsafe_construct(tree, func)
    if unsafe is not None:
        return _abstain("abstained_unsafe", unsafe, completion)
    if not any(isinstance(node, ast.Return) for node in ast.walk(func)):
        return _abstain("abstained_no_return", "completion has no return statement", completion)

    params = _named_arguments(func)
    assigned = _assigned_names(func)
    loaded = _loaded_names_by_position(func)
    unbound = [name for name in loaded
               if name not in params and name not in assigned and name not in _SAFE_CALLS]
    unused_params = [name for name in params if name not in loaded]

    if not unbound:
        return _abstain("unchanged_no_candidates", "no unbound replacement candidates", completion,
                        [], unused_params)
    if not unused_params:
        return _abstain("abstained_no_unused_params", "no unused requested parameter exists", completion,
                        unbound, unused_params)
    if len(unbound) != 1 or len(unused_params) != 1:
        return _abstain(
            "abstained_ambiguous",
            f"expected one unbound name and one unused parameter; got {len(unbound)} and {len(unused_params)}",
            completion,
            unbound,
            unused_params,
        )

    mapping = {unbound[0]: unused_params[0]}
    repaired = _rename_names(source, mapping)
    lines = repaired.splitlines()
    body_out = "\n".join(lines[1:])
    if completion.endswith("\n"):
        body_out += "\n"
    return RepairInfo(
        completion=body_out, status="repaired", reason="unique one-to-one mapping",
        changed=True, mapping=mapping, unbound=unbound, unused_params=unused_params,
    )


def repair_completion(signature: str | None, completion: str) -> str:
    return repair_completion_info(signature, completion).completion


def repair_from_prompt(prompt: str, completion: str) -> str:
    return repair_completion(extract_signature(prompt), completion)


def repair_from_prompt_info(prompt: str, completion: str) -> RepairInfo:
    return repair_completion_info(extract_signature(prompt), completion)


def _rename_names(source: str, mapping: dict[str, str]) -> str:
    tokens = list(tokenize.generate_tokens(io.StringIO(source).readline))
    for index, token in enumerate(tokens):
        if token.type == tokenize.NAME and token.string in mapping:
            tokens[index] = token._replace(string=mapping[token.string])
    return tokenize.untokenize(tokens)

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\chat_template.py
"""Single source of truth for the chat/response template (C3).

The previous template was::

    "<|system|>{system}\\n<|user|>{instruction}\\n<|assistant|>{response}<|eos|>"

None of ``<|system|>``, ``<|user|>``, ``<|assistant|>`` or ``<|eos|>`` exist in
either shipped tokenizer. Encoding that string shredded the markers into ordinary
byte-level tokens (``['<|', 'system', '|>', 'h', 'i', ...]``), so the model was
never shown a real turn delimiter and could not learn to produce one.

This module fixes that without inventing vocabulary and without touching a
tokenizer:

* The template is expressed with ``<bos>`` and ``<eos>``, the boundary tokens the
  shipped tokenizers actually register (``qm_code_bpe_v0``: ids 1 and 2).
* :func:`validate_chat_template` refuses a tokenizer that does not register every
  marker, so this class of defect cannot be reintroduced silently.
* Training (``training/sft.py``) and inference (``serving/code_chat.py``) both
  render through these functions, so they cannot drift apart.

Known limitation, stated plainly: the vocabulary has **no role tokens**, so this
template does not mark who is speaking. It encodes "system preamble, then request,
then response, terminated by ``<eos>``". Adding real role markers would mean
extending the vocabulary, resizing the embedding matrix and invalidating existing
checkpoints; that is a deliberate, separate decision and is not taken here.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from training.tokenizer_contract import (
    CONTRACT_V1,
    CONTRACT_V2,
    detect_contract,
    require_contract,
)

BOS = "<bos>"
EOS = "<eos>"

#: Contract used for all new training and serving. v1 remains renderable so the
#: historical M7 checkpoint can be reproduced and served through its documented
#: legacy path, but new artifacts must record v2.
CONTRACT_ID = CONTRACT_V2
LEGACY_CONTRACT_ID = CONTRACT_V1

#: Rendered as ``BOS + system + "\\n\\n" + instruction + "\\n\\n" + response + EOS``.
#: Placeholder names are kept as ``system``/``instruction``/``response`` so existing
#: callers that do ``TEMPLATE.format(system=..., instruction=..., response=...)``
#: keep working; only the surrounding markers changed.
CHAT_TEMPLATE = BOS + "{system}\n\n{instruction}\n\n{response}" + EOS


def _render(system: str, user: str, assistant: str | None) -> str:
    """Shared body. ``assistant is None`` omits both the response and the EOS.

    The prompt half must stay a literal prefix of the completion, otherwise
    label masking would supervise or hide the wrong tokens. Emitting the EOS in
    the prompt would both terminate early and break that prefix property.
    """
    text = BOS + system + "\n\n" + user + "\n\n"
    if assistant is not None:
        text += assistant + EOS
    return text

#: Markers that must exist as single tokens in the tokenizer.
REQUIRED_MARKERS = (BOS, EOS)

SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
    "You are Quantsmind Coder, an expert programming assistant specializing in "
    "Python and JavaScript/TypeScript. You help with code generation, debugging, "
    "code review, refactoring, and technical explanations.\n"
    "- Always produce correct, idiomatic code with proper error handling.\n"
    "- Explain your reasoning before providing code solutions.\n"
    "- When reviewing code, identify bugs, security issues, and performance problems.\n"
    "- Follow PEP 8 for Python and standard conventions for JavaScript/TypeScript.\n"
    "- If you are unsure about an API or library version, state your assumptions."
)


class IncompatibleTokenizer(RuntimeError):
    """The tokenizer cannot represent the chat template as single tokens."""


def validate_chat_template(tokenizer) -> dict:
    """Verify every template marker is a registered single token.

    Returns the resolved marker ids. Raises :class:`IncompatibleTokenizer` naming
    the missing markers, rather than letting them be shredded into byte tokens.
    """
    resolved = {}
    missing = []
    for marker in REQUIRED_MARKERS:
        token_id = tokenizer.token_to_id(marker)
        if token_id is None:
            missing.append(marker)
        else:
            resolved[marker] = int(token_id)
    if missing:
        raise IncompatibleTokenizer(
            "chat template markers are not registered as single tokens: "
            + ", ".join(missing)
            + ". They would be split into byte-level fragments, so the model "
            "could never learn a turn boundary. Either extend the tokenizer or "
            "choose markers it registers."
        )
    return resolved


def _render_v2(system: str, user: str, assistant: str | None) -> str:
    """Contract v2: explicit single-token role markers and an explicit end-of-turn.

    The prompt half is still a literal prefix of the completion; the assistant
    marker is emitted by the prompt so the model is conditioned to answer, and
    the completion adds the response plus the end-of-turn token it must learn.
    """
    text = (
        "<|system|>" + system + "<|end_of_turn|>"
        + "<|user|>" + user + "<|end_of_turn|>"
        + "<|assistant|>"
    )
    if assistant is not None:
        text += assistant + "<|end_of_turn|>"
    return text


def render_prompt(
    system: str, user: str, *, contract_id: str = LEGACY_CONTRACT_ID
) -> str:
    """Prompt half of the template: everything the model must not be trained to emit.

    ``contract_id`` defaults to the legacy v1 layout so historical callers keep
    their exact bytes. New code should call :func:`render_for`, which derives the
    contract from the tokenizer instead of assuming one.
    """
    if contract_id == CONTRACT_V2:
        return _render_v2(system, user, None)
    if contract_id == CONTRACT_V1:
        return _render(system, user, None)
    raise ValueError(f"unknown prompt contract: {contract_id!r}")


def render_completion(
    system: str, user: str, assistant: str, *, contract_id: str = LEGACY_CONTRACT_ID
) -> str:
    """Full training example under the requested prompt contract."""
    if contract_id == CONTRACT_V2:
        return _render_v2(system, user, assistant)
    if contract_id == CONTRACT_V1:
        return _render(system, user, assistant)
    raise ValueError(f"unknown prompt contract: {contract_id!r}")


def render_for(
    tokenizer, system: str, user: str, assistant: str | None = None
) -> str:
    """Render using the strongest contract ``tokenizer`` actually supports.

    This is the single entry point training and serving should use: the contract
    is a property of the tokenizer, not a caller opinion, so the two sides cannot
    disagree about which layout is in force.
    """
    contract = detect_contract(tokenizer)
    require_contract(tokenizer, contract)
    if assistant is None:
        return render_prompt(system, user, contract_id=contract)
    return render_completion(system, user, assistant, contract_id=contract)


def prompt_token_length(
    tokenizer, system: str, user: str, *, contract_id: str = LEGACY_CONTRACT_ID
) -> int:
    """Length of the prompt prefix in tokens, using the same renderer as training.

    Returned value is the count of *supervised* tokens to mask, consistent with
    ``input_ids = ids[:-1]`` / ``labels = ids[1:]``.
    """
    prompt = render_prompt(system, user, contract_id=contract_id)
    return len(tokenizer.encode(prompt).ids) - 1


def render_chat(tokenizer, messages, default_system: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Render an ordered role/content list under the tokenizer's contract.

    Serving must not invent a second layout for multi-turn input. v2 renders each
    role as its reserved single token; v1 cannot express roles or turns, so it is
    restricted to a single user turn and refuses rather than emitting delimiters
    the tokenizer would shred.
    """
    contract = detect_contract(tokenizer)
    require_contract(tokenizer, contract)

    def role_of(message):
        return message.get("role") if isinstance(message, dict) else getattr(message, "role", None)

    def content_of(message):
        return message.get("content") if isinstance(message, dict) else getattr(message, "content", "")

    system_parts = [content_of(m) for m in messages if role_of(m) == "system"]
    turns = [m for m in messages if role_of(m) in ("user", "assistant")]
    if not turns:
        raise ValueError("messages must contain at least one user or assistant turn")
    if role_of(turns[0]) != "user":
        raise ValueError("the first non-system turn must be a user turn")

    system = "\n".join(system_parts) if system_parts else (default_system or "")
    if contract == CONTRACT_V1:
        if len(turns) != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                "the legacy contract qm.plain_instruction/1 supports a single "
                "user turn only; multi-turn requires qm.chat_instruction/2"
            )
        return render_prompt(system, content_of(turns[0]), contract_id=CONTRACT_V1)

    parts = []
    if system:
        parts.append("<|system|>" + system + "<|end_of_turn|>")
    for turn in turns:
        marker = "<|user|>" if role_of(turn) == "user" else "<|assistant|>"
        parts.append(marker + content_of(turn) + "<|end_of_turn|>")
    parts.append("<|assistant|>")
    return "".join(parts)

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\checkpoint.py
"""Checkpoint compatibility checking (A2 / ``OPEN_ISSUES`` B3).

``training/sft.py`` loaded ``--init-ckpt`` with ``strict=False`` and then printed
"initialized from ..." regardless of what actually happened. That is how
``runs/code_sft`` ended up as a 495,808-parameter ``code_tiny`` model while the
operator believed it was continuing from the 16.3M pretrain: every parameter
failed to load, every parameter stayed random, and the run reported success.

This module makes the outcome explicit and checked:

* missing / unexpected / shape-mismatched parameters are all reported by name;
* shape mismatches are **never** tolerated, even in partial mode, because a
  mismatched tensor means the architecture differs;
* missing parameters are fatal by default;
* partial initialization exists, but only as an explicit opt-in that reports
  exactly what stayed random;
* there is no silent fallback to random weights: if loading fails, the caller is
  expected to raise.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import torch
import torch.nn as nn


class CheckpointIncompatible(RuntimeError):
    """The checkpoint does not match the target model."""


class LoadReport:
    """Outcome of a weight load: what matched, what did not."""

    def __init__(self, loaded, missing, unexpected, mismatched, partial=False):
        self.loaded = list(loaded)
        self.missing = list(missing)
        self.unexpected = list(unexpected)
        self.mismatched = list(mismatched)  # list of (name, ckpt_shape, model_shape)
        self.partial = partial

    @property
    def ok(self) -> bool:
        return not self.missing and not self.unexpected and not self.mismatched

    def describe(self) -> str:
        lines = [
            f"loaded parameters   : {len(self.loaded)}",
            f"missing parameters  : {len(self.missing)}",
            f"unexpected          : {len(self.unexpected)}",
            f"shape mismatches    : {len(self.mismatched)}",
            f"partial load        : {self.partial}",
        ]
        for name in self.missing[:10]:
            lines.append(f"  MISSING    {name}")
        for name in self.unexpected[:10]:
            lines.append(f"  UNEXPECTED {name}")
        for name, ck, mk in self.mismatched[:10]:
            lines.append(f"  MISMATCH   {name}: checkpoint {tuple(ck)} vs model {tuple(mk)}")
        if len(self.missing) > 10 or len(self.unexpected) > 10 or len(self.mismatched) > 10:
            lines.append("  ... (truncated)")
        return "\n".join(lines)

    def as_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "loaded": len(self.loaded),
            "missing": list(self.missing),
            "unexpected": list(self.unexpected),
            "mismatched": [
                {"name": n, "checkpoint_shape": list(c), "model_shape": list(m)}
                for n, c, m in self.mismatched
            ],
            "partial": self.partial,
            "ok": self.ok,
        }


def load_model_weights(
    model: nn.Module,
    state_dict: dict,
    *,
    allow_partial: bool = False,
    source: str = "checkpoint",
) -> LoadReport:
    """Load ``state_dict`` into ``model``, refusing silent partial results.

    ``allow_partial=True`` permits *missing* parameters only. Shape mismatches and
    unexpected keys remain fatal: both indicate the checkpoint was produced for a
    different architecture, which is exactly the mistake this exists to prevent.
    """
    model_state = model.state_dict()
    ckpt_state = dict(state_dict)

    missing = [k for k in model_state if k not in ckpt_state]
    unexpected = [k for k in ckpt_state if k not in model_state]
    mismatched = []
    compatible = {}
    for name, tensor in ckpt_state.items():
        if name not in model_state:
            continue
        target = model_state[name]
        if tuple(tensor.shape) != tuple(target.shape):
            mismatched.append((name, tuple(tensor.shape), tuple(target.shape)))
        else:
            compatible[name] = tensor

    report = LoadReport(
        loaded=sorted(compatible),
        missing=sorted(missing),
        unexpected=sorted(unexpected),
        mismatched=sorted(mismatched),
        partial=allow_partial,
    )

    if mismatched:
        raise CheckpointIncompatible(
            f"{source} does not match the model architecture.\n{report.describe()}\n"
            "Shape mismatches are never tolerated: the checkpoint was produced "
            "for a different model. Refusing to continue."
        )
    if unexpected:
        raise CheckpointIncompatible(
            f"{source} contains parameters the model does not define.\n"
            f"{report.describe()}\n"
            "Refusing to continue: this checkpoint is for a different "
            "architecture."
        )
    if missing and not allow_partial:
        raise CheckpointIncompatible(
            f"{source} is missing {len(missing)} required parameter(s).\n"
            f"{report.describe()}\n"
            "Refusing to silently start from random weights. If partial "
            "initialization is intended, pass allow_partial=True and treat the "
            "listed parameters as untrained."
        )

    model.load_state_dict(compatible, strict=False)
    return report


def init_from_checkpoint(
    model: nn.Module,
    path: str,
    *,
    allow_partial: bool = False,
    source_label: str | None = None,
) -> LoadReport:
    """Load a checkpoint file and validate it against ``model``."""
    label = source_label or path
    try:
        ckpt = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        raise CheckpointIncompatible(f"checkpoint not found: {path}") from exc

    if not isinstance(ckpt, dict):
        raise CheckpointIncompatible(
            f"{label} is not a checkpoint dictionary (got {type(ckpt).__name__}); "
            "expected a dict with a 'model' entry"
        )
    state = ckpt.get("model")
    if state is None:
        # Tolerate a bare state_dict, but say so.
        if all(hasattr(v, "shape") for v in ckpt.values()):
            state = ckpt
        else:
            raise CheckpointIncompatible(
                f"{label} has no 'model' entry and is not a bare state_dict"
            )
    return load_model_weights(model, state, allow_partial=allow_partial, source=label)

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\checkpoint_schema.py
"""``quantsmind.checkpoint/2`` provenance contract (v1.1.0).

A checkpoint is only trustworthy if it answers, from the file alone: which model,
which tokenizer, which prompt contract, which data and which code produced it.
Schema ``/1`` recorded weights, optimizer, step and the resolved config, which is
not enough: the M7 incident was a checkpoint served under a prompt contract it
never trained on, and nothing in the file made that visible.

Schema ``/2`` adds a ``provenance`` block with eleven fields:

1. model geometry          2. parameter count        3. tokenizer identity
4. config hash             5. prompt contract id     6. code revision
7. corpus identity         8. command                 9. seed
10. library versions       11. creation time

Loading is strict for ``/2``. Legacy ``/1`` files remain loadable through an
explicit legacy branch (they carry no contract, so they are treated as
``qm.plain_instruction/1``), never silently as if they were ``/2``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

SCHEMA_V1 = "quantsmind.checkpoint/1"
SCHEMA_V2 = "quantsmind.checkpoint/2"

PROVENANCE_FIELDS = (
    "model_geometry",
    "parameter_count",
    "tokenizer",
    "config_sha256",
    "contract_id",
    "code_revision",
    "corpus",
    "command",
    "seed",
    "libraries",
    "created_at",
)


class ContractMismatch(RuntimeError):
    """A checkpoint's recorded prompt/tokenizer contract does not match the loader."""


def _sha256_text(text: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def config_sha256(model_cfg: dict) -> str:
    """Stable hash of the model geometry (key order and whitespace invariant)."""
    return _sha256_text(json.dumps(model_cfg, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")))


def code_revision(cwd: str | Path | None = None) -> str:
    """Best-effort code revision; never raises, never blocks a save."""
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
            cwd=str(cwd) if cwd else None,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=5,
        )
        rev = out.stdout.strip()
        return rev if out.returncode == 0 and rev else "unknown"
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - provenance must never break training
        return "unknown"


def library_versions() -> dict:
    versions = {"python": sys.version.split()[0]}
    for name in ("torch", "tokenizers", "numpy", "pyyaml"):
        try:
            versions[name] = importlib.metadata.version(name)
        except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
            versions[name] = None
    return versions


def tokenizer_identity(tokenizer=None, tokenizer_path: str | None = None,
                       tokenizer_sha256: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """Record path, digest and vocabulary so a loader can prove the pairing."""
    from training.tokenizer_contract import (
        contract_ids,
        tokenizer_fingerprint,
        tokenizer_file_fingerprint,
    )

    digest = tokenizer_sha256
    if digest is None and tokenizer_path and Path(tokenizer_path).is_file():
        digest = tokenizer_file_fingerprint(tokenizer_path)
    if digest is None and tokenizer is not None:
        digest = tokenizer_fingerprint(tokenizer)
    return {
        "path": str(tokenizer_path) if tokenizer_path else None,
        "sha256": digest,
        "vocab_size": tokenizer.get_vocab_size() if tokenizer is not None else None,
        "control_ids": contract_ids(tokenizer) if tokenizer is not None else None,
    }


def build_provenance(*, model_cfg: dict, parameter_count: int, contract_id: str,
                     config: dict, seed: int | None, tokenizer=None,
                     tokenizer_path: str | None = None,
                     tokenizer_sha256: str | None = None,
                     corpus_manifest: str | None = None,
                     corpus_sha256: str | None = None,
                     command: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """Assemble the eleven required fields. Missing identity is ``None``, never invented."""
    return {
        "model_geometry": dict(model_cfg),
        "parameter_count": int(parameter_count),
        "tokenizer": tokenizer_identity(tokenizer, tokenizer_path, tokenizer_sha256),
        "config_sha256": config_sha256(model_cfg),
        "contract_id": contract_id,
        "code_revision": code_revision(),
        "corpus": {"manifest": corpus_manifest, "sha256": corpus_sha256},
        "command": command if command is not None else " ".join(sys.argv),
        "seed": seed,
        "libraries": library_versions(),
        "created_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat(),
    }


def validate_provenance(provenance: dict | None) -> list[str]:
    """Return every missing/invalid field. An empty list means complete."""
    if not isinstance(provenance, dict):
        return ["provenance block is missing"]
    problems = [f"missing field: {f}" for f in PROVENANCE_FIELDS if f not in provenance]
    tok = provenance.get("tokenizer")
    if not isinstance(tok, dict) or not tok.get("sha256"):
        problems.append("tokenizer identity has no sha256")
    if not provenance.get("contract_id"):
        problems.append("contract_id is empty")
    if not provenance.get("config_sha256"):
        problems.append("config_sha256 is empty")
    if not isinstance(provenance.get("parameter_count"), int):
        problems.append("parameter_count is not an integer")
    if not isinstance(provenance.get("seed"), int):
        problems.append("seed is not an integer")
    return problems


def verify_against(provenance: dict, *, tokenizer=None, tokenizer_sha256: str | None = None,
                   contract_id: str | None = None, model_cfg: dict | None = None) -> None:
    """Refuse a checkpoint whose recorded identity disagrees with the loader.

    Only identities the caller can actually check are compared; an unrecorded
    field is a refusal for ``/2`` because the point of the schema is that the
    answer is present.
    """
    problems = validate_provenance(provenance)
    if problems:
        raise ContractMismatch("checkpoint provenance incomplete: " + "; ".join(problems))

    if contract_id is not None and provenance["contract_id"] != contract_id:
        raise ContractMismatch(
            f"checkpoint was trained under contract {provenance['contract_id']!r}, "
            f"but the loader requires {contract_id!r}"
        )
    if model_cfg is not None and provenance["config_sha256"] != config_sha256(model_cfg):
        raise ContractMismatch(
            "checkpoint model geometry hash does not match the loader's config"
        )

    recorded = provenance["tokenizer"].get("sha256")
    if tokenizer is not None and recorded:
        from training.tokenizer_contract import tokenizer_fingerprint

        if tokenizer_fingerprint(tokenizer) != recorded:
            raise ContractMismatch(
                "checkpoint tokenizer hash does not match the tokenizer being loaded"
            )
    if tokenizer_sha256 is not None and recorded and tokenizer_sha256 != recorded:
        raise ContractMismatch(
            "checkpoint tokenizer file hash does not match the tokenizer file supplied"
        )


def schema_of(ckpt: dict) -> str | None:
    return ckpt.get("schema") if isinstance(ckpt, dict) else None

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\continued_training.py
"""Continued training from the frozen v2.1.0 checkpoint for v2.2.0 cells."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import time

import torch

from training.determinism import set_determinism
from training.objective import accumulation_weights, token_mean_loss
from training.schedules import WarmupCosineSchedule
from training.supervised_train import (_batch_tensor, _validation_loss,
                                       build_batches, weighted_mean_loss)

DEFAULT_SEED = 20261022


def save_checkpoint(path, model, model_config, **metadata):
    payload = {"config": {"model": dict(model_config)},
               "model": model.state_dict()}
    payload.update(metadata)
    torch.save(payload, path)
    return path


def train_from_checkpoint(
    *,
    checkpoint_path,
    checkpoint_hash,
    tokenizer,
    examples,
    val_examples,
    lr: float,
    steps: int,
    max_length: int = 256,
    grad_accum: int = 2,
    seed: int = DEFAULT_SEED,
    identifier_config=None,
    warmup: int = 2,
    weight_decay: float = 0.1,
    grad_clip: float = 1.0,
    artifacts=None,
    device: str = "cpu",
):
    """Fine-tune the frozen checkpoint and return metrics plus the model."""
    from serving.local_inference import load_model

    set_determinism(seed)
    model, model_config = load_model(checkpoint_path, device)
    model.train()
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        model.parameters(), lr=lr, betas=(0.9, 0.95),
        weight_decay=weight_decay)
    schedule = WarmupCosineSchedule(
        peak_lr=lr, warmup_steps=warmup, total_steps=steps, min_ratio=0.1)
    train_batches = build_batches(tokenizer, examples, max_length=max_length, identifier_config=identifier_config)
    val_batches = build_batches(tokenizer, val_examples, max_length=max_length, identifier_config=identifier_config)
    if not train_batches:
        raise ValueError("no trainable examples were produced")

    generator = torch.Generator()
    generator.manual_seed(seed)
    order = torch.randperm(len(train_batches), generator=generator).tolist()
    history = []
    consumed = 0
    started = time.time()
    for step in range(steps):
        window = []
        for micro in range(grad_accum):
            index = order[(step * grad_accum + micro) % len(order)]
            window.append(train_batches[index])
        counts = [item["supervised"] for item in window]
        weights = accumulation_weights(counts)
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        loss_value = 0.0
        for item, weight in zip(window, weights):
            batch = _batch_tensor([item])
            logits, _ = model(batch.input_ids.to(device))
            micro_mean, supervised = weighted_mean_loss(
                logits, batch.labels.to(device), item.get("weights"))
            if supervised == 0 or micro_mean is None:
                continue
            (micro_mean * weight).backward()
            loss_value += float(micro_mean.item()) * weight
        grad_norm = float(torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(
            model.parameters(), grad_clip, error_if_nonfinite=False))
        learning_rate = schedule.lr_at(step)
        for group in optimizer.param_groups:
            group["lr"] = learning_rate
        optimizer.step()
        consumed += sum(counts)
        finite = math.isfinite(loss_value)
        history.append({
            "step": step + 1, "loss": loss_value, "lr": learning_rate,
            "grad_norm_before_clip": grad_norm,
            "supervised_tokens": sum(counts), "finite_loss": finite,
        })
        if not finite:
            break

    validation_loss = _validation_loss(model, val_batches, device)
    model.eval()
    result = {
        "base_checkpoint": str(checkpoint_path),
        "base_checkpoint_sha256": checkpoint_hash,
        "lr": lr, "steps": len(history), "requested_steps": steps,
        "grad_accum": grad_accum, "max_length": max_length,
        "tokens_consumed": consumed,
        "supervised_tokens_per_example": round(
            consumed / max(len(history), 1), 2),
        "initial_loss": history[0]["loss"] if history else None,
        "final_loss": history[-1]["loss"] if history else None,
        "validation_loss": validation_loss,
        "elapsed_seconds": round(time.time() - started, 2),
        "history": history, "train_examples": len(examples),
        "val_examples": len(val_examples), "seed": seed,
        "parameters": int(model.num_params()),
    }
    if artifacts is not None:
        artifacts.write_metric("training.json", result)
        payload = {"config": {"model": dict(model_config)},
                   "model": model.state_dict(), "step": len(history),
                   "seed": seed, "base_checkpoint_sha256": checkpoint_hash}
        path = artifacts.write_checkpoint("trained.pt", payload)
        from training.experiment_artifacts import file_sha256
        result["checkpoint_sha256"] = file_sha256(path)
    return result, model, model_config

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\contrastive_tasks.py
"""Contrastive task pairs for Taksh v2.0.0.

Each pair is two tasks that differ by exactly one meaningful requirement, so
the only way to answer both correctly is to read the instruction. A model
that emits one template for everything fails the pair; a model that changes
only the name fails it as well.

Pairs: arithmetic add/subtract, conditionals max/min, list keep-positive /
keep-negative, string upper/lower, dict lookup/count-keys, loop sum/count.

Partitions: ``train`` (both variants of four families), ``A`` (same templates,
unseen parameters and names), ``B`` (composed tasks), ``C`` (two families
never trained), ``D`` (the contrastive holdout: matched pairs of the trained
families with unseen names and parameters).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import random

from training.synthetic_curriculum import Case, _hash

#: (family, variant) -> (function name, arguments, docstring, body, operation)
TASKS = {
    ("arithmetic", "add"): (
        "combine_values", "left, right", "Return the sum of the two inputs.",
        "    return left + right", "add"),
    ("arithmetic", "subtract"): (
        "separate_values", "left, right", "Return the difference of the two inputs.",
        "    return left - right", "subtract"),
    ("conditionals", "maximum"): (
        "choose_larger", "left, right", "Return the larger of the two values.",
        "    if left > right:\n        return left\n    return right", "maximum"),
    ("conditionals", "minimum"): (
        "choose_smaller", "left, right", "Return the smaller of the two values.",
        "    if left < right:\n        return left\n    return right", "minimum"),
    ("list_ops", "keep_positive"): (
        "select_positive", "values", "Return only the values above zero.",
        "    return [value for value in values if value > 0]", "keep_positive"),
    ("list_ops", "keep_negative"): (
        "select_negative", "values", "Return only the values below zero.",
        "    return [value for value in values if value < 0]", "keep_negative"),
    ("string_ops", "upper"): (
        "shout_text", "text", "Return the text in upper case.",
        "    return text.upper()", "upper"),
    ("string_ops", "lower"): (
        "whisper_text", "text", "Return the text in lower case.",
        "    return text.lower()", "lower"),
    ("dict_ops", "lookup"): (
        "read_value", "mapping, key", "Return the value for a key or a default.",
        "    return mapping.get(key, 0)", "lookup"),
    ("dict_ops", "count_keys"): (
        "count_entries", "mapping, key", "Return how many keys the mapping has.",
        "    return len(mapping)", "count_keys"),
    ("loop_agg", "sum_values"): (
        "total_values", "values", "Accumulate the values with a loop.",
        "    total = 0\n    for value in values:\n        total += value\n    return total",
        "sum_values"),
    ("loop_agg", "count_values"): (
        "count_entries", "values", "Count the values with a loop.",
        "    count = 0\n    for value in values:\n        count += 1\n    return count",
        "count_values"),
}

#: Markers that indicate the requested operation in a generated program.
OPERATION_MARKERS = {
    "add": [" + "],
    "subtract": [" - "],
    "maximum": [">", "max"],
    "minimum": ["<", "min"],
    "keep_positive": ["> 0", ">0"],
    "keep_negative": ["< 0", "<0"],
    "upper": [".upper("],
    "lower": [".lower("],
    "lookup": [".get("],
    "count_keys": ["len("],
    "sum_values": ["+=", "sum"],
    "count_values": ["+= 1", "count"],
}

TRAINED_FAMILIES = ("arithmetic", "conditionals", "list_ops", "string_ops")
WITHHELD_FAMILIES = ("dict_ops", "loop_agg")

#: Unseen function names used by the holdout partitions.
HOLDOUT_NAMES = {
    "arithmetic": ("merge_numbers", "split_numbers"),
    "conditionals": ("pick_bigger", "pick_smaller"),
    "list_ops": ("select_above_zero", "select_below_zero"),
    "string_ops": ("capitalise_text", "lowercase_text"),
    "dict_ops": ("read_entry", "size_of_mapping"),
    "loop_agg": ("running_total", "running_count"),
}

#: Partition D uses different names again, so a matched pair differs in the
#: operation *and* in the requested name.
CONTRASTIVE_NAMES = {
    "arithmetic": ("add_up_numbers", "take_away_numbers"),
    "conditionals": ("bigger_of_two", "smaller_of_two"),
    "list_ops": ("keep_above_zero", "keep_below_zero"),
    "string_ops": ("shout_it", "whisper_it"),
    "dict_ops": ("entry_value", "entry_count"),
    "loop_agg": ("total_it", "count_it"),
}


def _case(case_id, family, variant, name, partition, salt):
    function, arguments, docstring, body, operation = TASKS[(family, variant)]
    prompt = (
        f"def {name}({arguments}):\n"
        f"    \"\"\"{docstring} [case {salt}]\"\"\"\n"
    )
    reference = f"{prompt}{body}\n"
    return Case(
        case_id=case_id,
        family=family,
        partition=partition,
        template_id=f"{family}:{variant}",
        prompt=prompt,
        reference=reference,
        content_sha256=_hash(reference),
        params={
            "operation": operation,
            "variant": variant,
            "pair": family,
            "salt": salt,
        },
    )


def _variants(family):
    return [variant for (fam, variant) in TASKS if fam == family]


def build_contrastive_curriculum(seed: int = 20261021) -> dict:
    """Build the frozen contrastive curriculum (train, A, B, C, D)."""
    partitions = {"train": [], "A": [], "B": [], "C": [], "D": []}
    rng = random.Random(f"{seed}:contrastive")

    for index in range(80):
        family = TRAINED_FAMILIES[index % len(TRAINED_FAMILIES)]
        variants = _variants(family)
        variant = variants[index % len(variants)]
        name = TASKS[(family, variant)][0]
        partitions["train"].append(
            _case(f"train-{family}-{variant}-{index:03d}", family, variant, name,
                  "train", index)
        )

    for index in range(40):
        family = TRAINED_FAMILIES[index % len(TRAINED_FAMILIES)]
        variants = _variants(family)
        variant = variants[index % len(variants)]
        name = HOLDOUT_NAMES[family][0 if variant == variants[0] else 1]
        partitions["A"].append(
            _case(f"A-{family}-{variant}-{index:03d}", family, variant, name, "A", index)
        )

    for index in range(24):
        family = WITHHELD_FAMILIES[index % len(WITHHELD_FAMILIES)]
        variants = _variants(family)
        variant = variants[index % len(variants)]
        name = HOLDOUT_NAMES[family][0 if variant == variants[0] else 1]
        partitions["C"].append(
            _case(f"C-{family}-{variant}-{index:03d}", family, variant, name, "C", index)
        )

    # Partition D: matched pairs of the trained families, both variants, unseen
    # names. A model that ignores the instruction answers both members of a
    # pair the same way; a model that only copies the name still fails it.
    for index in range(24):
        family = TRAINED_FAMILIES[index % len(TRAINED_FAMILIES)]
        variants = _variants(family)
        pair_id = f"{family}-{index // len(TRAINED_FAMILIES):02d}"
        for position, variant in enumerate(variants):
            name = CONTRASTIVE_NAMES[family][position]
            case = _case(
                f"D-{pair_id}-{variant}", family, variant, name, "D", index
            )
            case.params["pair_id"] = pair_id
            partitions["D"].append(case)

    # Partition B: composed tasks (filter then sum) built from trained ops.
    for index in range(16):
        threshold = 1 + index
        prompt = (
            f"def filter_then_total_{index:02d}(values):\n"
            f'    """Keep the values above a threshold, then sum them."""\n'
        )
        reference = (
            f"{prompt}"
            f"    kept = [value for value in values if value > {threshold}]\n"
            f"    total = 0\n"
            f"    for value in kept:\n"
            f"        total += value\n"
            f"    return total\n"
        )
        partitions["B"].append(
            Case(
                case_id=f"B-composed-{index:03d}",
                family="composed",
                partition="B",
                template_id="composed:filter_then_total",
                prompt=prompt,
                reference=reference,
                content_sha256=_hash(reference),
                params={"operation": "filter_then_total", "pair": "composed",
                        "salt": index},
            )
        )
    return partitions


def curriculum_digest(partitions: dict) -> str:
    """A single hash over the whole contrastive curriculum."""
    payload = "\n".join(
        f"{case.partition}:{case.case_id}:{case.content_sha256}"
        for partition in sorted(partitions)
        for case in partitions[partition]
    )
    return _hash(payload)


def contamination_report(partitions: dict) -> dict:
    """Cross-partition contamination for the contrastive curriculum."""
    from training.synthetic_curriculum import _normalized_hash

    violations = []
    exact = {}
    normalized = {}
    for partition in sorted(partitions):
        for case in partitions[partition]:
            exact.setdefault(case.content_sha256, {}).setdefault(partition, []).append(
                case.case_id
            )
            normalized.setdefault(
                _normalized_hash(case.reference), {}
            ).setdefault(partition, []).append(case.case_id)
    for key, group in exact.items():
        if len(group) > 1:
            violations.append(f"identical target across partitions {key[:12]}: {group}")
    # Parameter-erased (template-level) sharing between train, A and D is
    # deliberate in this curriculum: D asks for the *same* operations with
    # unseen names and constants, which is exactly what makes it a test of
    # instruction following rather than of template recall. Only a withheld
    # family (C) appearing in training is a leak.
    train_families = {case.family for case in partitions["train"]}
    for case in partitions["C"]:
        if case.family in train_families:
            violations.append(
                f"{case.case_id}: withheld family {case.family} appears in training"
            )
    return {
        "schema": "quantsmind.synthetic_contamination/1",
        "violations": violations,
        "violation_count": len(violations),
        "contaminated": bool(violations),
        "verdict": "SYNTHETIC_EVALUATION_CONTAMINATED" if violations else "CLEAN",
        "partition_sizes": {
            partition: len(cases) for partition, cases in sorted(partitions.items())
        },
        "note": (
            "Template-level sharing between train, A and D is deliberate: the "
            "contrastive holdout asks for the same operations with unseen names "
            "and constants."
        ),
    }

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\copy_curriculum.py
"""Staged identifier-copying curriculum (Taksh v1.2.0 Increment 9, WP3+WP4).

Seven stages from exact copying to functional generation, all original
synthetic data with novel identifier pools. Stage families use the
Increment 2/4 surface-variant machinery where practical so template
diversity and quality gates carry over. Validation is disjoint in
identifiers and wording (never a shuffle of training examples).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib

from training.binding_curriculum import _validate
from training.functional_curriculum import _INSTRUCTIONS, _SAMPLES, _body
from training.supervised import build_example
from training.targeted_curriculum import novel_pairs, novel_singles

STAGES = (
    "exact_copy",
    "unfamiliar_copy",
    "substitution",
    "propagation",
    "multi_binding",
    "binding_structure",
    "functional",
)

_DIVERSE_INSTRUCTIONS = {
    "exact_copy": ("Return the named value.", "Give back the input.", "Yield the value as-is."),
    "unfamiliar_copy": ("Copy this identifier into the result.", "Pass the named input through."),
    "substitution": ("Rename the input and return it.", "Copy with a new local name."),
    "propagation": ("Keep the value in a local and return it.", "Store then return the input."),
    "multi_binding": ("Combine both values.", "Return the joint result."),
    "binding_structure": ("Choose between the values.", "Pick the larger value."),
    "functional": ("Carry out the described operation.", "Perform the named task."),
}


def _stage_examples(stage: str, *, split: str, id_prefix: str, per_stage: int) -> list:
    is_train = split == "train"
    pool_start = 0 if is_train else 24
    pairs = novel_pairs(48)
    singles = novel_singles(48)
    examples = []
    if stage in ("exact_copy", "unfamiliar_copy"):
        instruction_pool = _DIVERSE_INSTRUCTIONS[stage]
        for index in range(per_stage):
            name = singles[pool_start + (index % 24)]
            signature = f"def copy_{index:02d}({name}):"
            body = f"    return {name}"
            if stage == "unfamiliar_copy":
                body = f"    result = {name}\n    return result"
            instruction = instruction_pool[index % len(instruction_pool)]
            _validate(signature, body)
            examples.append(
                build_example(
                    example_id=f"{id_prefix}-{stage}-{index:03d}",
                    instruction=instruction,
                    signature=signature,
                    body=body,
                    operation=stage,
                    family="copy",
                    split=split,
                    seed=20261109 + index,
                    metadata={"markers": [stage], "stage": stage,
                              "inputs": [[0]], "expected_outputs": [0],
                              "relationship": "output == the named input"},
                )
            )
        return examples
    if stage == "substitution":
        for index in range(per_stage):
            source, target_name = pair_pool = (pairs[pool_start + (index % 24)][0], singles[pool_start + (index % 24)])
            signature = f"def rename_{index:02d}({source}):"
            body = f"    {target_name} = {source}\n    return {target_name}"
            instruction = _DIVERSE_INSTRUCTIONS[stage][index % len(_DIVERSE_INSTRUCTIONS[stage])]
            _validate(signature, body)
            examples.append(
                build_example(
                    example_id=f"{id_prefix}-{stage}-{index:03d}",
                    instruction=instruction,
                    signature=signature,
                    body=body,
                    operation=stage,
                    family="copy",
                    split=split,
                    seed=20261109 + index,
                    metadata={"markers": [stage], "stage": stage,
                              "inputs": [[0]], "expected_outputs": [0],
                              "relationship": "output == input under a new local name"},
                )
            )
        return examples
    if stage == "propagation":
        for index in range(per_stage):
            a = pairs[pool_start + (index % 24)][0]
            local = singles[pool_start + (index % 24)]
            signature = f"def carry_{index:02d}({a}):"
            body = f"    {local} = {a}\n    {local} = {local}\n    return {local}"
            instruction = _DIVERSE_INSTRUCTIONS[stage][index % len(_DIVERSE_INSTRUCTIONS[stage])]
            _validate(signature, body)
            examples.append(
                build_example(
                    example_id=f"{id_prefix}-{stage}-{index:03d}",
                    instruction=instruction,
                    signature=signature,
                    body=body,
                    operation=stage,
                    family="copy",
                    split=split,
                    seed=20261109 + index,
                    metadata={"markers": [stage], "stage": stage,
                              "inputs": [[0]], "expected_outputs": [0],
                              "relationship": "output == input propagated through locals"},
                )
            )
        return examples
    if stage == "multi_binding":
        for index in range(per_stage):
            a, b = pairs[pool_start + (index % 24)]
            signature = f"def both_{index:02d}({a}, {b}):"
            body = f"    return {a} + {b}"
            instruction = _DIVERSE_INSTRUCTIONS[stage][index % len(_DIVERSE_INSTRUCTIONS[stage])]
            _validate(signature, body)
            examples.append(
                build_example(
                    example_id=f"{id_prefix}-{stage}-{index:03d}",
                    instruction=instruction,
                    signature=signature,
                    body=body,
                    operation=stage,
                    family="copy",
                    split=split,
                    seed=20261109 + index,
                    metadata={"markers": [stage], "stage": stage,
                              "inputs": [[1, 2]], "expected_outputs": [3],
                              "relationship": "output == first + second"},
                )
            )
        return examples
    if stage == "binding_structure":
        for index in range(per_stage):
            a, b = pairs[pool_start + (index % 24)]
            signature = f"def choose_{index:02d}({a}, {b}):"
            body = f"    if {a} > {b}:\n        return {a}\n    return {b}"
            instruction = _DIVERSE_INSTRUCTIONS[stage][index % len(_DIVERSE_INSTRUCTIONS[stage])]
            _validate(signature, body)
            examples.append(
                build_example(
                    example_id=f"{id_prefix}-{stage}-{index:03d}",
                    instruction=instruction,
                    signature=signature,
                    body=body,
                    operation=stage,
                    family="copy",
                    split=split,
                    seed=20261109 + index,
                    metadata={"markers": [stage], "stage": stage,
                              "inputs": [[3, 2]], "expected_outputs": [3],
                              "relationship": "output == the larger input"},
                )
            )
        return examples
    # functional stage: the eight established behaviours with novel pools.
    from training.functional_curriculum import OPERATIONS, _FAMILIES, _RELATIONSHIPS

    singles_pool = novel_singles(48)
    pairs_pool = novel_pairs(48)
    for operation in OPERATIONS:
        instructions = list(_INSTRUCTIONS[operation])
        samples = _SAMPLES[operation]
        for index in range(per_stage // len(OPERATIONS)):
            if operation in ("scale_value", "join_text", "add_then_multiply", "multiply_then_add"):
                params = pairs_pool[pool_start + (index % 24)]
            else:
                params = (singles_pool[pool_start + (index % 24)],)
            function_name = f"fn_{operation}_{index:02d}"
            instruction = instructions[(index + (0 if is_train else 2)) % len(instructions)]
            variant = index % 4
            signature = f"def {function_name}({', '.join(params)}):"
            body = _body(operation, params, variant)
            _validate(signature, body)
            args, expected = samples[index % len(samples)]
            examples.append(
                build_example(
                    example_id=f"{id_prefix}-{stage}-{operation}-{index:03d}",
                    instruction=instruction,
                    signature=signature,
                    body=body,
                    operation=operation,
                    family=_FAMILIES[operation],
                    split=split,
                    seed=20261109 + index,
                    metadata={"markers": [operation], "stage": stage,
                              "variant": variant,
                              "inputs": [list(args)], "expected_outputs": [expected],
                              "relationship": _RELATIONSHIPS[operation]},
                )
            )
    return examples


def build_training_examples(*, per_stage: int = 16) -> list:
    examples = []
    for stage in STAGES:
        examples.extend(_stage_examples(stage, split="train", id_prefix="C1", per_stage=per_stage))
    return examples


def build_validation_examples(*, per_stage: int = 4) -> list:
    examples = []
    for stage in STAGES:
        examples.extend(_stage_examples(stage, split="validation", id_prefix="C1V", per_stage=per_stage))
    return examples


def copy_curriculum_digest() -> str:
    payload = [
        (example.example_id, example.instruction, example.signature, example.body, example.operation)
        for example in build_training_examples()
    ]
    return hashlib.sha256(repr(payload).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
