<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\curriculum_quality.py
"""Curriculum diversity and mode-collapse safeguards (Taksh v1.2.0 Increment 2).

These checks are structural (AST based) rather than raw-text matching so
that superficial renamings do not count as diversity. They can be applied
equally to a curriculum (list of supervised examples) and to evaluation
output records (dicts with ``completion`` and ``category``).

Threshold rationale
-------------------
The defaults are deliberately generous: they must reject the Increment 1
failure shape (one template per operation, a dominant comprehension) while
accepting legitimate Python variation.

* ``max_operation_share = 0.12``: with 13 operations the uniform share is
  0.077. 0.12 allows about 55% over-representation but rejects a 2x
  dominance. A single-template corpus still passes this check, so it is
  not sufficient on its own; the per-operation template checks below are
  the decisive ones.
* ``min_templates_per_operation = 3``: Increment 1 §10 recommends 3-4
  surface forms per operation. A corpus with fewer than three distinct
  template families for any operation gives the model a single attractor
  per operation and is rejected.
* ``max_variant_share_within_operation = 0.5``: no single normalised
  shape may exceed half of its operation's examples. Increment 1 scored
  1.0 on every operation.
* ``max_template_share = 0.20``: no single global template family may
  exceed 20% of the corpus. With ~50 templates in a diversified corpus,
  20% is roughly ten times the uniform expectation, so only a strongly
  skewed corpus fails.
* ``max_listcomp_share = 0.10``: list comprehensions are one valid form
  among many. Increment 1 scored 24/156 = 0.154 and collapsed to this
  form on unrelated prompts; a diversified corpus should score well under
  0.10. Legitimate comprehension use is not banned, only dominance.
* ``collapse_threshold = 0.30`` with ``collapse_min_cases = 5`` and
  ``collapse_min_categories = 3`` (evaluation side): one template
  appearing on at least 30% of held-out outputs, at least five cases, and
  at least three different categories is treated as mode collapse. The
  category requirement prevents a single-category legitimation (for
  example, five genuinely list-shaped tasks) from being flagged.
* Degenerate comprehension text (``for item in in ...``) is flagged at a
  count of 3 or more regardless of share: it is never legitimate output.

All thresholds are configurable via :class:`QualityThresholds`; violations
raise :class:`CurriculumQualityError` with a message naming the check and
the observed value.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import copy
import re
from collections import Counter
from dataclasses import dataclass

from training.program_analysis import analyse

__all__ = [
    "CurriculumQualityError",
    "QualityThresholds",
    "template_family",
    "normalised_shape",
    "check_curriculum",
    "diversity_report",
    "detect_mode_collapse",
]

_DEGENERATE_LISTCOMP = re.compile(r"for\s+\w+\s+in\s+in\b")


class CurriculumQualityError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a curriculum or output set violates a quality threshold."""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class QualityThresholds:
    max_operation_share: float = 0.12
    max_template_share: float = 0.20
    max_listcomp_share: float = 0.10
    min_templates_per_operation: int = 3
    max_variant_share_within_operation: float = 0.5
    collapse_threshold: float = 0.30
    collapse_min_cases: int = 5
    collapse_min_categories: int = 3
    degenerate_min_count: int = 3


def _parse_function(signature: str, body: str):
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(signature + "\n" + body)
    except SyntaxError:
        return None
    if not tree.body or not isinstance(tree.body[0], ast.FunctionDef):
        return None
    return tree.body[0]


def _return_kind(node) -> str:
    if node is None:
        return "no_return"
    value = node.value
    if value is None:
        return "bare_return"
    if isinstance(value, ast.Name):
        return "name_return"
    if isinstance(value, ast.BinOp):
        return "binop_return"
    if isinstance(value, ast.UnaryOp):
        return "unary_return"
    if isinstance(value, ast.IfExp):
        return "ternary_return"
    if isinstance(value, ast.ListComp):
        return "listcomp_return"
    if isinstance(value, ast.GeneratorExp):
        return "genexp_return"
    if isinstance(value, ast.JoinedStr):
        return "fstring_return"
    if isinstance(value, ast.Call):
        func = value.func
        if isinstance(func, ast.Name):
            if func.id == "len":
                return "len_call_return"
            if func.id == "sum":
                return "sum_call_return"
            if func.id == "list":
                return "list_call_return"
            return f"{func.id}_call_return"
        if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute):
            return f"method_{func.attr}_return"
        return "call_return"
    if isinstance(value, ast.Attribute):
        return "attribute_return"
    return type(value).__name__.lower() + "_return"


def template_family(signature: str, body: str) -> str:
    """Coarse AST template family of a function body, ignoring identifiers."""
    function = _parse_function(signature, body)
    if function is None:
        return "unparseable"
    statements = function.body
    prefix = ""
    if (
        statements
        and isinstance(statements[0], ast.Expr)
        and isinstance(statements[0].value, ast.Constant)
        and isinstance(statements[0].value.value, str)
        and len(statements) > 1
    ):
        prefix = "docstring_"
        statements = statements[1:]
    kinds = [type(stmt).__name__ for stmt in statements]
    last_return = None
    for stmt in statements:
        if isinstance(stmt, ast.Return):
            last_return = stmt
    return_kind = _return_kind(last_return)
    if "While" in kinds:
        shape = "while_loop"
    elif "For" in kinds:
        shape = "for_loop"
    elif "If" in kinds and "Assign" in kinds:
        shape = "assign_if"
    elif "If" in kinds:
        shape = "if"
    elif "AugAssign" in kinds:
        shape = "augassign"
    elif "Assign" in kinds:
        shape = "assign"
    else:
        shape = "direct"
    return f"{prefix}{shape}_{return_kind}"


def normalised_shape(signature: str, body: str) -> str:
    """Fine-grained AST shape with all identifiers and constants masked.

    Parameter names become ``p0``, ``p1``, ... by position, local names
    become ``L``, the function name becomes ``f``, string constants become
    ``S`` and numeric constants become ``N``. Two examples that differ
    only in names or literal values share a shape; the Increment 2
    variants of one operation do not.
    """
    tree = ast.parse(signature + "\n" + body)
    function = tree.body[0]
    params = [arg.arg for arg in function.args.args]
    assigned: set[str] = set()
    for node in ast.walk(function):
        if isinstance(node, ast.arg):
            assigned.add(node.arg)
        elif isinstance(node, ast.Name) and isinstance(node.ctx, (ast.Store, ast.Del)):
            assigned.add(node.id)
        elif isinstance(node, (ast.For, ast.comprehension)):
            for target in ast.walk(node.target):
                if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
                    assigned.add(target.id)

    def mask(name: str) -> str:
        if name in params:
            return f"p{params.index(name)}"
        if name in assigned:
            return "L"
        if name in {"len", "sum", "list", "str"}:
            return name
        return "G"

    class Masker(ast.NodeTransformer):
        def visit_Name(self, node):
            node.id = mask(node.id)
            return node

        def visit_arg(self, node):
            node.arg = mask(node.arg)
            return node

        def visit_Constant(self, node):
            if isinstance(node.value, str):
                node.value = "S"
            elif isinstance(node.value, (int, float)):
                node.value = "N"
            return node

    masked = copy.deepcopy(function)
    masked.name = "f"
    Masker().visit(masked)
    return ast.dump(masked)


def _params_of(signature: str) -> list[str]:
    tree = ast.parse(signature + "\n    pass")
    return [arg.arg for arg in tree.body[0].args.args]


def _is_degenerate_text(completion: str) -> bool:
    return bool(_DEGENERATE_LISTCOMP.search(completion or ""))


def check_curriculum(train, val=None, *, thresholds: QualityThresholds = QualityThresholds(), heldout_pairs=None) -> dict:
    """Validate a curriculum and return a statistics report.

    Raises :class:`CurriculumQualityError` on the first violated check.
    ``train`` and ``val`` are sequences of supervised examples with
    ``operation``, ``instruction``, ``signature`` and ``body`` attributes.
    ``heldout_pairs`` is an optional set of ``(instruction, signature)``
    pairs that training data must not overlap.
    """
    thresholds = thresholds or QualityThresholds()
    train = list(train)
    val = list(val) if val is not None else []
    if not train:
        raise CurriculumQualityError("curriculum check failed: training set is empty")
    n = len(train)

    op_counts = Counter(example.operation for example in train)
    template_counts = Counter(template_family(e.signature, e.body) for e in train)
    shape_counts = Counter((e.operation, normalised_shape(e.signature, e.body)) for e in train)
    listcomp_count = sum(count for name, count in template_counts.items() if "listcomp" in name)

    # 1. Operation balance.
    for operation, count in op_counts.items():
        share = count / n
        if share > thresholds.max_operation_share:
            raise CurriculumQualityError(
                f"operation balance check failed: operation {operation!r} is {count}/{n} "
                f"({share:.1%}), above max_operation_share {thresholds.max_operation_share:.0%}"
            )

    # 2. Global template balance.
    dominant_template, dominant_count = template_counts.most_common(1)[0]
    if dominant_count / n > thresholds.max_template_share:
        raise CurriculumQualityError(
            f"template balance check failed: template {dominant_template!r} is "
            f"{dominant_count}/{n} ({dominant_count / n:.1%}), above "
            f"max_template_share {thresholds.max_template_share:.0%}"
        )

    # 3. Per-operation template diversity and 4. variant dominance.
    templates_per_operation: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    for example in train:
        templates_per_operation.setdefault(example.operation, set()).add(
            template_family(example.signature, example.body)
        )
    for operation, templates in templates_per_operation.items():
        if len(templates) < thresholds.min_templates_per_operation:
            raise CurriculumQualityError(
                f"template diversity check failed: operation {operation!r} has "
                f"{len(templates)} template families {sorted(templates)}, fewer than "
                f"min_templates_per_operation {thresholds.min_templates_per_operation}"
            )
    for (operation, shape), count in shape_counts.items():
        share = count / op_counts[operation]
        if share > thresholds.max_variant_share_within_operation:
            raise CurriculumQualityError(
                f"variant dominance check failed: one normalised shape for operation "
                f"{operation!r} covers {count}/{op_counts[operation]} ({share:.1%}) of "
                f"that operation, above max_variant_share_within_operation "
                f"{thresholds.max_variant_share_within_operation:.0%}"
            )

    # 5. List-comprehension dominance.
    if listcomp_count / n > thresholds.max_listcomp_share:
        raise CurriculumQualityError(
            f"list-comprehension dominance check failed: list-comprehension templates are "
            f"{listcomp_count}/{n} ({listcomp_count / n:.1%}), above "
            f"max_listcomp_share {thresholds.max_listcomp_share:.0%}"
        )

    # 6. Exact duplicates.
    seen: dict[tuple, str] = {}
    for example in train:
        key = (example.instruction, example.signature, example.body)
        if key in seen:
            raise CurriculumQualityError(
                f"duplicate check failed: {example.example_id!r} duplicates {seen[key]!r} "
                "(identical instruction, signature and body)"
            )
        seen[key] = example.example_id
    ids = [example.example_id for example in train]
    if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
        raise CurriculumQualityError("duplicate check failed: example_id values are not unique in the training set")

    # 7. Invalid Python and binding (undefined names, parameter coverage).
    for example in train + val:
        result = analyse(example.signature, example.body)
        if not result["parses"]:
            raise CurriculumQualityError(
                f"AST validity check failed: {example.example_id!r} does not parse: {result['error']}"
            )
        if result["undefined_names"]:
            raise CurriculumQualityError(
                f"binding check failed: {example.example_id!r} uses undefined names "
                f"{result['undefined_names']} (parameter names were replaced or invented)"
            )
        params = _params_of(example.signature)
        # analyse() reports params_used positionally ("p0", "p1", ...).
        used = set(result["params_used"])
        expected_all = {f"p{index}" for index in range(len(params))}
        if example.operation == "choose_first":
            if used != {"p0"}:
                raise CurriculumQualityError(
                    f"binding check failed: {example.example_id!r} must use only the first "
                    f"parameter {params[0]!r}, used {sorted(used)}"
                )
        elif example.operation == "choose_second":
            if used != {"p1"}:
                raise CurriculumQualityError(
                    f"binding check failed: {example.example_id!r} must use only the second "
                    f"parameter {params[1]!r}, used {sorted(used)}"
                )
        elif used != expected_all:
            raise CurriculumQualityError(
                f"binding check failed: {example.example_id!r} must use every parameter "
                f"{params}, used {sorted(used)}"
            )

    # 8. Train/validation leakage.
    if val:
        train_pairs = {(e.instruction, e.signature) for e in train}
        val_pairs = {(e.instruction, e.signature) for e in val}
        overlap = train_pairs & val_pairs
        if overlap:
            raise CurriculumQualityError(
                f"leakage check failed: {len(overlap)} (instruction, signature) pairs appear "
                f"in both train and validation, first: {sorted(overlap)[:1]}"
            )
        train_bodies = {(e.signature, e.body) for e in train}
        val_bodies = {(e.signature, e.body) for e in val}
        body_overlap = train_bodies & val_bodies
        if body_overlap:
            raise CurriculumQualityError(
                f"leakage check failed: {len(body_overlap)} (signature, body) pairs appear "
                f"in both train and validation, first: {sorted(body_overlap)[:1]}"
            )

    # 9. Held-out overlap.
    if heldout_pairs:
        overlap = [
            e.example_id for e in train
            if (e.instruction, e.signature) in heldout_pairs
        ]
        if overlap:
            raise CurriculumQualityError(
                f"held-out leakage check failed: training examples {overlap[:5]} overlap "
                "frozen evaluation cases"
            )

    family_counts = Counter(example.family for example in train)
    return {
        "train_examples": n,
        "validation_examples": len(val),
        "operations": dict(sorted(op_counts.items())),
        "families": dict(sorted(family_counts.items())),
        "template_families": dict(sorted(template_counts.items())),
        "distinct_template_families": len(template_counts),
        "distinct_normalised_shapes": len(shape_counts),
        "templates_per_operation": {op: sorted(t) for op, t in sorted(templates_per_operation.items())},
        "listcomp_examples": listcomp_count,
        "listcomp_share": round(listcomp_count / n, 4),
        "max_template_share": round(dominant_count / n, 4),
        "exact_duplicates": 0,
        "invalid_examples": 0,
        "train_validation_leakage": 0,
        "heldout_overlap": 0,
    }


def _record_template(record: dict) -> str:
    completion = record.get("completion") or ""
    signature = record.get("signature") or "def probe(value):"
    family = template_family(signature, completion)
    if _is_degenerate_text(completion):
        return "degenerate_listcomp_text"
    if family == "unparseable" and "[" in completion and "for " in completion:
        return "degenerate_listcomp_text"
    return family


def diversity_report(records) -> dict:
    """Template-diversity statistics for a set of evaluation records."""
    records = list(records)
    templates = Counter(_record_template(r) for r in records)
    completions = Counter((r.get("completion") or "").strip() for r in records)
    degenerate = sum(1 for r in records if _is_degenerate_text(r.get("completion") or ""))
    n = len(records)
    top_template, top_count = templates.most_common(1)[0] if templates else (None, 0)
    return {
        "records": n,
        "distinct_templates": len(templates),
        "template_counts": dict(sorted(templates.items())),
        "dominant_template": top_template,
        "dominant_count": top_count,
        "dominant_share": round(top_count / n, 4) if n else 0.0,
        "exact_repeated_completions": sum(1 for text, count in completions.items() if text and count > 1),
        "degenerate_listcomp_text": degenerate,
    }


def detect_mode_collapse(records, *, thresholds: QualityThresholds = QualityThresholds()) -> dict:
    """Detect the Increment 1 failure mode in evaluation output records.

    Collapsed when one template family covers at least
    ``collapse_threshold`` of the records, at least
    ``collapse_min_cases`` records, and at least
    ``collapse_min_categories`` distinct categories; or when degenerate
    comprehension text (``for item in in ...``) appears at least
    ``degenerate_min_count`` times.
    """
    thresholds = thresholds or QualityThresholds()
    records = list(records)
    report = diversity_report(records)
    n = report["records"]
    dominant = report["dominant_template"]
    dominant_count = report["dominant_count"]
    dominant_categories = sorted({
        r.get("category") for r in records
        if _record_template(r) == dominant
    }) if dominant else []
    degenerate = report["degenerate_listcomp_text"]
    share = report["dominant_share"]
    collapsed = bool(
        n
        and dominant_count >= thresholds.collapse_min_cases
        and share >= thresholds.collapse_threshold
        and len(dominant_categories) >= thresholds.collapse_min_categories
    )
    degenerate_collapsed = degenerate >= thresholds.degenerate_min_count
    reasons = []
    if collapsed:
        reasons.append(
            f"template {dominant!r} on {dominant_count}/{n} ({share:.1%}) across "
            f"{len(dominant_categories)} categories {dominant_categories}"
        )
    if degenerate_collapsed:
        reasons.append(f"degenerate comprehension text on {degenerate} records")
    return {
        "collapsed": collapsed or degenerate_collapsed,
        "dominant_template": dominant,
        "dominant_count": dominant_count,
        "dominant_share": share,
        "dominant_categories": dominant_categories,
        "degenerate_listcomp_text": degenerate,
        "template_counts": report["template_counts"],
        "reasons": reasons,
    }

import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch

_DTYPE_MAP = {"uint16": np.uint16, "uint32": np.uint32}


class TokenArtifactIncompatible(RuntimeError):
    """The token artifact does not match the model it would train."""


class TokenDataset:
    def __init__(self, tokens_path: str, meta_path: str | None = None, seed: int = 42):
        p = Path(tokens_path)
        meta_file = Path(meta_path) if meta_path else p.with_suffix(".meta.json")
        self.vocab_size = None
        self.meta = {}
        self.tokens_path = p
        if meta_file.exists():
            self.meta = json.loads(meta_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            if self.meta.get("dtype") not in _DTYPE_MAP:
                raise TokenArtifactIncompatible(
                    f"{meta_file}: unknown dtype {self.meta.get('dtype')!r}. "
                    "Refusing to guess how to read this artifact."
                )
            dtype = _DTYPE_MAP[self.meta["dtype"]]
            self.vocab_size = int(self.meta.get("vocab_size", 0)) or None
        else:
            dtype = np.uint16
        self.data = np.memmap(p, dtype=dtype, mode="r")
        self.rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        if len(self.data) < 2:
            raise ValueError(f"token file too small: {p} ({len(self.data)} tokens)")

    def validate_for_model(self, model_vocab: int, tokenizer_vocab: int | None = None):
        """Check the artifact against the model/tokenizer it will be used with.

        Returns a list of human-readable problems; empty means compatible.
        Artifacts predating ``schema: quantsmind.token_stream/1`` carry no
        provenance, so only the vocabulary cross-check is possible for them and
        that limitation is reported rather than hidden.
        """
        problems = []
        if not self.meta:
            return [
                "token artifact has no metadata file; provenance (tokenizer, source "
                "corpus, separator policy) cannot be verified"
            ]
        if self.meta.get("schema") != "quantsmind.token_stream/1":
            problems.append(
                f"token artifact schema is {self.meta.get('schema')!r}, not "
                "'quantsmind.token_stream/1'; it carries no tokenizer or "
                "separator provenance and cannot be verified"
            )
            problems.append(
                "LEGACY ARTIFACT: produced before document separators existed, so "
                "its documents run together with no boundary (OPEN_ISSUES B6). "
                "Regenerate with data.encode_dataset to restore boundaries before "
                "training on it."
            )
        artifact_vocab = self.vocab_size
        if artifact_vocab and artifact_vocab > model_vocab:
            problems.append(
                f"artifact vocab_size {artifact_vocab} exceeds model vocab_size "
                f"{model_vocab}; ids would index outside the embedding matrix"
            )
        if tokenizer_vocab and artifact_vocab and artifact_vocab != tokenizer_vocab:
            problems.append(
                f"artifact vocab_size {artifact_vocab} does not match the "
                f"tokenizer's {tokenizer_vocab}; the artifact was produced by a "
                "different tokenizer"
            )
        return problems

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.data)

    def batch(self, batch_size: int, seq_len: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
        hi = len(self.data) - seq_len - 1
        if hi < 0:
            raise ValueError(
                f"cannot draw a window of {seq_len} tokens from "
                f"{self.tokens_path}: the stream holds {len(self.data)} tokens, "
                f"so at least {seq_len + 1} are required. Either lower "
                "data.seq_len or encode a larger corpus."
            )
        offsets = self.rng.integers(0, hi + 1, size=batch_size)
        x = np.stack([self.data[o : o + seq_len] for o in offsets])
        y = np.stack([self.data[o + 1 : o + 1 + seq_len] for o in offsets])
        return (
            torch.from_numpy(x.astype(np.int64)),
            torch.from_numpy(y.astype(np.int64)),
        )

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\data_loader.py
"""Deterministic dataset streaming for Taksh v1.3.0.

The reader is the v1.2.0 interface (``data.python_v1.interface``): artifacts
are read in manifest order, their checksums are verified, and every record's
content hash is re-checked while streaming. No other corpus path exists, so
a run cannot silently fall back to a historical token stream.

Sampling is deterministic and resume-aware. For a given ``(seed, epoch)`` the
window order is a pure function, produced by a seeded ``torch.Generator``;
the sampler state records the epoch and the position inside it, so a resumed
run replays exactly the order the interrupted run would have used.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import torch

from data.python_v1.interface import PythonDataset


class ManifestDataset:
    """Ordered view of one prepared split."""

    def __init__(self, manifest_path, split: str = "train", *, require_ready: bool = True):
        self.split = split
        self._dataset = PythonDataset(
            manifest_path, split, verify=True, require_ready=require_ready
        )

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._dataset)

    def __iter__(self):
        for sample in self._dataset:
            yield {
                "source_id": sample.source_id,
                "file_path": sample.file_path,
                "text": sample.text,
                "content_sha256": sample.content_sha256,
            }

    @property
    def manifest(self) -> dict:
        return self._dataset.manifest


class DeterministicSampler:
    """Seeded permutation of window indices, stable per epoch."""

    def __init__(self, count: int, seed: int, shuffle: bool = True):
        self.count = int(count)
        self.seed = int(seed)
        self.shuffle = bool(shuffle)

    def order(self, epoch: int) -> list:
        """Window indices for one epoch. Pure function of (seed, epoch)."""
        if self.count == 0:
            return []
        if not self.shuffle:
            return list(range(self.count))
        generator = torch.Generator()
        generator.manual_seed(self.seed * 1_000_003 + int(epoch))
        return torch.randperm(self.count, generator=generator).tolist()

    def state_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "seed": self.seed,
            "shuffle": self.shuffle,
            "count": self.count,
            "type": "deterministic_epoch_permutation",
        }

    def load_state_dict(self, state: dict) -> None:
        if not state:
            return
        if state.get("type") not in (None, "deterministic_epoch_permutation"):
            raise ValueError(f"unsupported sampler type: {state.get('type')!r}")
        self.seed = int(state.get("seed", self.seed))
        self.shuffle = bool(state.get("shuffle", self.shuffle))
        self.count = int(state.get("count", self.count))


class WindowStream:
    """Turns windows into microbatches and accumulation windows."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        windows,
        *,
        sampler: DeterministicSampler,
        batch_builder,
        micro_batch_size: int = 1,
        grad_accum_steps: int = 1,
        drop_last: bool = True,
    ):
        if micro_batch_size < 1 or grad_accum_steps < 1:
            raise ValueError("micro_batch_size and grad_accum_steps must be >= 1")
        self.windows = list(windows)
        self.sampler = sampler
        self.batch_builder = batch_builder
        self.micro_batch_size = int(micro_batch_size)
        self.grad_accum_steps = int(grad_accum_steps)
        self.drop_last = bool(drop_last)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.windows)

    def microbatches(self, epoch: int, start_position: int = 0):
        """Yield ``(position, batch)`` pairs for one epoch.

        ``position`` is the index of the microbatch inside the epoch, which
        is what a resumed run needs in order to continue exactly where it
        stopped.
        """
        order = self.sampler.order(epoch)
        position = 0
        for start in range(0, len(order), self.micro_batch_size):
            chunk = order[start : start + self.micro_batch_size]
            if self.drop_last and len(chunk) < self.micro_batch_size:
                break
            if position < start_position:
                position += 1
                continue
            batch = self.batch_builder([self.windows[index] for index in chunk])
            yield position, batch
            position += 1

    def accumulation_windows(self, epoch: int, start_position: int = 0):
        """Yield lists of microbatches that form one optimizer step."""
        window: list = []
        for position, batch in self.microbatches(epoch, start_position):
            window.append(batch)
            if len(window) == self.grad_accum_steps:
                yield window
                window = []
        if window:
            yield window

    def state_dict(self, epoch: int, position: int) -> dict:
        state = self.sampler.state_dict()
        state.update({"epoch": int(epoch), "position": int(position)})
        return state

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\determinism.py
"""Deterministic execution helpers (v1.1.0).

The M7 run could not answer "would this command produce the same run again?"
because seeds were not plumbed into torch or numpy, and deterministic kernels were
not requested. This module is the single place that answers the question.

Limits are stated rather than hidden: deterministic algorithms are requested, not
guaranteed. Some CUDA kernels have no deterministic variant; when that happens
PyTorch raises, the caller records the deviation in the run manifest, and the run
is reported as "nondeterministic operation: <name>" instead of silently varying.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import random


def set_determinism(seed: int, *, strict: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Seed every RNG the training loop touches and request deterministic kernels.

    Returns the settings applied so a caller can record them. ``strict=True``
    turns a missing deterministic kernel into an error instead of a warning.
    """
    import numpy as np
    import torch

    os.environ.setdefault("PYTHONHASHSEED", str(seed))
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)

    torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(bool(strict), warn_only=not strict)
    if hasattr(torch.backends, "cudnn"):
        torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
        torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False

    return {
        "seed": int(seed),
        "torch_deterministic": bool(strict),
        "cudnn_deterministic": True,
        "cudnn_benchmark": False,
        "pythonhashseed": os.environ.get("PYTHONHASHSEED"),
    }

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\document_separator.py
"""Document boundary semantics for packed token streams (A3 / B6).

``data/encode_dataset.py`` used to concatenate every corpus record with no
separator at all, while ``TokenDataset.batch`` samples random offsets across the
whole stream. A training window therefore routinely contained the tail of one
unrelated file followed by the head of another, with nothing marking the join.
The model was trained to believe any file continues into any other.

Separator choice
----------------
The shipped code tokenizer (``tokenizer/qm_code_bpe_v0.json``) defines exactly
four specials: ``<pad> <bos> <eos> <unk>``. There is no ``<sep>``, and inventing
one would require adding vocabulary and retraining the tokenizer, so this module
uses **``<eos>``** as the document separator:

* it already exists in the vocabulary, so no token id can be out of range;
* it already carries "this sequence ends here" meaning, and the serving stack
  already stops generation on it, so preprocessing, training and inference agree;
* using it means the model learns to emit it at document boundaries, which is
  exactly what inference needs.

A blank line or ``\\n\\n`` was rejected because the BPE vocabulary contains no
token for it (``token_to_id("\\n\\n")`` is ``None``); it would be shredded into
ordinary byte tokens and would not be distinguishable from content.

Oversized documents
-------------------
A record longer than ``seq_len`` is **not** truncated and **not** split. It is
written whole into the stream and simply spans consecutive training windows. This
is the documented behaviour: the encoder never destroys content, and the reader
windows across boundaries only where a document genuinely continues.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

DOC_SEPARATOR_NAME = "<eos>"
DOC_SEPARATOR_ID = 2  # <eos> in the shipped code tokenizer; always re-resolved


class SeparatorUnavailable(RuntimeError):
    """The tokenizer does not define the document separator token."""


def resolve_separator_id(tokenizer) -> int:
    """Return the token id used to mark a document boundary.

    Raises ``SeparatorUnavailable`` with an actionable message rather than
    silently falling back to a byte sequence that the vocabulary cannot represent.
    """
    token_id = tokenizer.token_to_id(DOC_SEPARATOR_NAME)
    if token_id is None:
        raise SeparatorUnavailable(
            f"tokenizer has no {DOC_SEPARATOR_NAME!r} token, so document "
            "boundaries cannot be marked. Refusing to write a stream whose "
            "documents run into each other. Either use a tokenizer that defines "
            f"{DOC_SEPARATOR_NAME!r} or add it via tokenizer/train_tokenizer.py."
        )
    return int(token_id)


def encode_records(
    tokenizer,
    records,
    max_tokens: int | None = None,
    skip_empty: bool = True,
) -> tuple[list[int], int]:
    """Encode records into one flat id stream, separated by the separator token.

    Returns ``(ids, records_emitted)``.

    ``skip_empty`` drops records that encode to nothing. A dropped record does
    *not* contribute a separator either, so the stream never contains two
    separators in a row and never begins or ends with one.

    ``max_tokens`` truncates **at document granularity**. A document is never cut
    in half: if the next document would exceed the budget, encoding stops at the
    last whole document. The single exception is a document that is larger than
    the entire budget on its own -- there is nothing whole to fall back to, so it
    is truncated and reported via the returned count. Cutting mid-document would
    leave a window that opens with the tail of a document and closes with nothing,
    which is the exact corruption the separator exists to prevent.
    """
    sep = resolve_separator_id(tokenizer)
    ids: list[int] = []
    emitted = 0
    truncated = False

    for record in records:
        chunk = tokenizer.encode(record).ids
        if skip_empty and not chunk:
            continue

        if max_tokens is not None:
            needed = len(chunk) + (1 if ids else 0)
            if len(ids) + needed > max_tokens:
                if not ids:
                    # Nothing emitted yet and this document cannot fit: emit as
                    # much as the budget allows rather than returning nothing.
                    ids.extend(chunk[:max_tokens])
                    emitted += 1
                    truncated = True
                break

        if ids:
            ids.append(sep)
        ids.extend(chunk)
        emitted += 1

    return ids, emitted

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\exec_filter.py
"""Execution-backed filtering helpers for code-training candidates.

C# candidates are compiled locally. Execution is always opt-in and is disabled
by default. This module does not make generated code safe to run.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
from typing import Any

from evaluation.csharp.runner import compile_csharp


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ExecutionFilterResult:
    language: str
    outcome: str
    passed: bool
    execution_authorized: bool
    diagnostics: list[dict[str, Any]]
    detail: str

    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)


def _normalize_language(language: str | None) -> str:
    normalized = (language or "").strip().lower()
    aliases = {"cs": "csharp", "c#": "csharp", "dotnet": "csharp", ".net": "csharp"}
    return aliases.get(normalized, normalized)


def evaluate_candidate(
    language: str | None,
    source: str,
    *,
    allow_execution: bool = False,
    target_framework: str = "net10.0",
    timeout: int = 90,
) -> ExecutionFilterResult:
    normalized = _normalize_language(language)
    if normalized != "csharp":
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported execution language: {language!r}; supported: csharp")
    result = compile_csharp(
        source,
        target_framework=target_framework,
        timeout=timeout,
        allow_execution=allow_execution,
    )
    passed = result.outcome == ("executed" if allow_execution else "compiled")
    if allow_execution:
        passed = passed and result.exit_code == 0
    diagnostics = [*result.diagnostics, *result.source_diagnostics]
    detail = (
        f"outcome={result.outcome}; exit_code={result.exit_code}; "
        f"diagnostics={len(diagnostics)}"
    )
    return ExecutionFilterResult(
        language=normalized,
        outcome=result.outcome,
        passed=passed,
        execution_authorized=allow_execution,
        diagnostics=diagnostics,
        detail=detail,
    )


def filter_candidates(
    candidates,
    *,
    allow_execution: bool = False,
    target_framework: str = "net10.0",
    timeout: int = 90,
) -> list[ExecutionFilterResult]:
    results = []
    for candidate in candidates:
        if not isinstance(candidate, dict):
            raise TypeError("each candidate must be a dict with language and source")
        results.append(
            evaluate_candidate(
                candidate.get("language"),
                candidate.get("source", ""),
                allow_execution=allow_execution,
                target_framework=target_framework,
                timeout=timeout,
            )
        )
    return results

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\experiment_artifacts.py
"""Immutable experiment artifacts (Taksh v2.0.0).

v1.9.0 lost its trained checkpoint to a later diagnostic probe that wrote
into the same run directory. This module removes that failure mode: run
directories are **exclusive** and finalized artifacts are **immutable**.

Rules enforced here:

* A run identifier may be used once; creating it again fails.
* A checkpoint destination may be written once; writing it again fails.
* Writes are atomic: the payload goes to a temporary file and is renamed only
  after it is complete, so an interrupted write never leaves a plausible
  looking artifact behind.
* Finalization writes a manifest and a hash inventory, then makes the
  finalized files read-only.
* Verification recomputes the hashes and fails on any mismatch.
* Nothing identifies an artifact by filename alone: every evaluation record
  carries the checkpoint hash it was produced from.

The output root is outside the Git repository by construction: the caller
supplies it, and this module refuses a root inside the working tree unless
``allow_repository_root`` is set explicitly.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import stat
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

MANIFEST_NAME = "manifest.json"
SUBDIRECTORIES = ("checkpoints", "evaluations", "metrics", "integrity")


class ArtifactError(RuntimeError):
    """An artifact operation was refused."""


def file_sha256(path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(65536), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def canonical_digest(payload) -> str:
    blob = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), default=str)
    return hashlib.sha256(blob.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


class RunArtifacts:
    """One immutable experiment run directory."""

    def __init__(self, root, run_id: str, *, create: bool = True,
                 allow_repository_root: bool = False):
        if not run_id or "/" in run_id or "\\" in run_id or run_id in (".", ".."):
            raise ArtifactError(f"invalid run id: {run_id!r}")
        self.root = Path(root).resolve()
        self.run_id = run_id
        self.files = {}
        self.created = False
        self.finalized = False
        if not allow_repository_root:
            repo = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
            if self.root == repo or repo in self.root.parents:
                raise ArtifactError(
                    f"the experiment root {self.root} is inside the repository; "
                    "experiments must not write into the source tree"
                )
        self.directory = self.root / run_id
        if create:
            if self.directory.exists():
                raise ArtifactError(
                    f"run directory already exists: {self.directory}; a run "
                    "identifier may be used only once"
                )
            self.directory.mkdir(parents=True)
            for name in SUBDIRECTORIES:
                (self.directory / name).mkdir()
            self.created = True
        elif not self.directory.is_dir():
            raise ArtifactError(f"run directory does not exist: {self.directory}")

    def path(self, *parts) -> Path:
        return self.directory.joinpath(*parts)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ writes
    def _write_atomic(self, path: Path, data: bytes) -> Path:
        if self.finalized:
            raise ArtifactError(
                f"run {self.run_id} is finalized; no artifact may be added to it"
            )
        if path.exists():
            raise ArtifactError(
                f"refusing to overwrite an existing artifact: {path}"
            )
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        temporary = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".partial")
        with open(temporary, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(data)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        temporary.replace(path)
        return path

    def write_checkpoint(self, name: str, payload: dict) -> Path:
        """Write a checkpoint exactly once, atomically."""
        if not name.endswith(".pt"):
            name = f"{name}.pt"
        path = self.path("checkpoints", name)
        import torch

        self._write_atomic(path, _torch_bytes(payload))
        digest = file_sha256(path)
        self.files[f"checkpoints/{name}"] = digest
        return path

    def write_json(self, kind: str, name: str, payload: dict) -> Path:
        """Write a JSON artifact exactly once, atomically."""
        if kind not in ("evaluations", "metrics", "integrity"):
            raise ArtifactError(f"unknown artifact kind: {kind!r}")
        path = self.path(kind, name if name.endswith(".json") else f"{name}.json")
        data = (json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True, default=str) + "\n").encode(
            "utf-8"
        )
        self._write_atomic(path, data)
        self.files[f"{kind}/{path.name}"] = file_sha256(path)
        return path

    def write_evaluation(self, name: str, payload: dict) -> Path:
        """Write an evaluation record, which must name its checkpoint hash."""
        checkpoint_hash = payload.get("checkpoint_sha256")
        if not checkpoint_hash:
            raise ArtifactError(
                "an evaluation record must carry the checkpoint hash it was "
                "produced from"
            )
        return self.write_json("evaluations", name, payload)

    def write_metric(self, name: str, payload: dict) -> Path:
        return self.write_json("metrics", name, payload)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- finalisation
    def finalize(self, manifest: dict) -> Path:
        """Finalize the run: write the manifest and the hash inventory.

        A finalized run cannot be finalized again, and its files are made
        read-only at the application level.
        """
        if self.finalized:
            raise ArtifactError(
                f"run {self.run_id} is already finalized and cannot be changed"
            )
        manifest = dict(manifest)
        manifest.setdefault("run_id", self.run_id)
        manifest.setdefault(
            "finalized_at", datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat()
        )
        manifest["files"] = dict(sorted(self.files.items()))
        manifest["manifest_sha256"] = canonical_digest(manifest)
        path = self.path(MANIFEST_NAME)
        data = (json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, sort_keys=True, default=str) + "\n").encode(
            "utf-8"
        )
        self._write_atomic(path, data)
        self.files[MANIFEST_NAME] = file_sha256(path)
        self.write_json("integrity", "hashes.json", {"files": dict(sorted(self.files.items()))})
        for relative in list(self.files):
            target = self.path(relative)
            if target.exists():
                target.chmod(stat.S_IREAD)
        self.finalized = True
        return path

    def verify(self) -> dict:
        """Recompute every recorded hash and report any mismatch."""
        inventory_path = self.path("integrity", "hashes.json")
        if not inventory_path.is_file():
            raise ArtifactError(
                f"run {self.run_id} has no hash inventory; it was never finalized"
            )
        inventory = json.loads(inventory_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        mismatches = []
        missing = []
        for relative, expected in sorted(inventory.get("files", {}).items()):
            target = self.path(relative)
            if not target.is_file():
                missing.append(relative)
                continue
            actual = file_sha256(target)
            if actual != expected:
                mismatches.append(
                    {"file": relative, "expected": expected, "actual": actual}
                )
        return {
            "run_id": self.run_id,
            "files_checked": len(inventory.get("files", {})),
            "mismatches": mismatches,
            "missing": missing,
            "intact": not mismatches and not missing,
        }


def _torch_bytes(payload: dict) -> bytes:
    import io

    import torch

    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    torch.save(payload, buffer)
    return buffer.getvalue()

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\experiment_plan.py
"""The first authorized Python learning experiment, specified but not run.

This module produces the *plan* for the first real-data experiment. It does
not authorize it: the plan's status is ``NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_EXECUTION`` until
every prerequisite is satisfied and the owner explicitly authorizes a run.

Parameters that cannot be established from evidence are written as
placeholders with the reason, rather than invented numbers.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

EXPERIMENT_STATUS = "NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_EXECUTION"

HYPOTHESIS = (
    "Training an S2-compatible Taksh checkpoint on a provenance-verified, "
    "owner-approved Python corpus improves held-out Python completion "
    "quality under identical evaluation conditions: same cases, same prompt "
    "surface, same generation settings, same tokenizer and model geometry."
)

#: Every prerequisite, with what satisfies it. ``status`` is filled from
#: evidence, never assumed.
PREREQUISITES = (
    ("approved_source_allowlist", "one or more source manifests in state 'approved'"),
    ("verified_licensing_evidence", "licence evidence present and hashed for each source"),
    ("immutable_source_revisions", "a pinned revision per approved source"),
    ("completed_provenance_checks", "provenance established for each source"),
    ("completed_contamination_checks", "the corpus screened against the frozen suites"),
    ("frozen_data_splits", "train/validation/test splits with recorded hashes"),
    ("compatible_tokenizer", "the frozen tokenizer the corpus was prepared with"),
    ("compatible_model_geometry", "the S2 rung the checkpoint uses"),
    ("reproducible_training_configuration", "a versioned configuration with a recorded digest"),
    ("sufficient_disk_and_memory", "measured headroom for the run and its artifacts"),
    ("defined_compute_budget", "an agreed step, token and wall-clock budget"),
    ("defined_evaluation_plan", "the frozen evaluation suite and its budgets"),
    ("safe_execution_isolation", "a mechanism that can execute generated code safely"),
)

#: Stop or review conditions. A lower training loss alone is never a success
#: signal.
STOP_CONDITIONS = (
    ("validation_loss_divergence", "validation loss rises for 3 consecutive evaluations"),
    ("train_validation_gap", "the gap exceeds 0.5 nats for 3 consecutive evaluations"),
    ("output_collapse", "more than half the completions are degenerate repetition"),
    ("no_held_out_improvement", "held-out completion quality does not improve over the baseline"),
    ("memorisation", "training families are reproduced but held-out families are not"),
    ("contamination_detected", "a held-out or benchmark record appears in training"),
    ("resource_exhaustion", "the wall-clock or disk budget is reached"),
    ("checkpoint_corruption", "a checkpoint fails its integrity check"),
)

EVALUATION_CRITERIA = (
    "training loss",
    "validation loss",
    "next-token accuracy on the validation split",
    "syntax-valid completion rate on Track A",
    "complete-program rate on Track A",
    "degenerate repetition rate on Track A",
    "truncation rate at a pre-registered budget",
    "held-out family completion quality",
    "instruction-following rate (only on an instruction-qualified checkpoint)",
    "functional correctness (only when a safe isolation mechanism exists)",
)


def prerequisite_status(registry_path=None, *, isolation_available: bool = False,
                        compute_ok: bool = True) -> list:
    """Evaluate each prerequisite from evidence. No assumption is made."""
    statuses = []
    approved = 0
    if registry_path:
        from data.python_v1.readiness import assess

        report = assess(registry_path)
        approved = report["sources"]["approved"]
    for name, requirement in PREREQUISITES:
        if name == "approved_source_allowlist":
            status = "met" if approved else "missing"
        elif name in ("verified_licensing_evidence", "immutable_source_revisions",
                      "completed_provenance_checks"):
            status = "met" if approved else "missing"
        elif name == "completed_contamination_checks":
            status = "missing"
        elif name == "frozen_data_splits":
            status = "missing"
        elif name in ("compatible_tokenizer", "compatible_model_geometry"):
            status = "available"
        elif name == "reproducible_training_configuration":
            status = "available"
        elif name == "sufficient_disk_and_memory":
            status = "available" if compute_ok else "unknown"
        elif name == "defined_compute_budget":
            status = "pending_owner_decision"
        elif name == "defined_evaluation_plan":
            status = "available"
        elif name == "safe_execution_isolation":
            status = "available" if isolation_available else "missing"
        else:
            status = "unknown"
        statuses.append(
            {
                "prerequisite": name,
                "requirement": requirement,
                "status": status,
                "blocking": status in ("missing", "unknown"),
            }
        )
    return statuses


def build_plan(*, registry_path=None, isolation_available: bool = False,
               compute_ok: bool = True, measured_tokens_per_second=None) -> dict:
    """Assemble the experiment plan, with its authorization status."""

"""Functional synthetic curriculum (Taksh v1.2.0 Increment 4).

Original QuantsMind-generated examples with explicit input/output
behavioural relationships. Every example carries the sample inputs and
expected outputs in its metadata (``inputs``, ``expected_outputs``,
``relationship``) so functional correctness can be verified through the
isolated safe-execution gate without touching frozen AD-1/C3 suites.

Eight behaviours, four structurally distinct implementations each,
deterministic seeds, and a disjoint validation split (rotated names,
function names, and instructions). Combined with the Increment 2 binding
curriculum the corpus must still pass the Increment 2 quality checks.

# Deterministic sample inputs/outputs per operation (boundary cases first).

    "scale_value": [((6, 7), 42), ((0, 5), 0), ((-3, 4), -12), ((5, 0), 0)],
    "join_text": [(("blue", "sky"), "blue sky"), (("", "x"), " x"), (("x", ""), "x "), (("a", "b"), "a b")],

# Relationship statement stored in metadata (the I/O contract).
_RELATIONSHIPS = {
    "scale_value": "output == first * second",
    "join_text": "output == first + ' ' + second",
    "add_then_multiply": "output == (first + second) * 2",
    "multiply_then_add": "output == first * second + 2",
    "filter_and_count": "output == number of elements > 0",
    "keep_long_words": "output == [word for word in input if len(word) > 3]",
    "is_even": "output == (input % 2 == 0)",
    "sum_positive": "output == sum of elements > 0",
}


def _body(operation: str, params: tuple[str, ...], variant: int) -> str:
    variant %= 4
    if operation == "scale_value":
        (a, b) = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    return {a} * {b}"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    scaled = {a} * {b}\n    return scaled"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    result = {a}\n    result *= {b}\n    return result"
        return f"    return {b} * {a}"
    if operation == "join_text":
        (a, b) = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f'    return {a} + " " + {b}'
        if variant == 1:
            return f'    joined = {a} + " " + {b}\n    return joined'
        if variant == 2:
            return f'    return f"{{{a}}} {{{b}}}"'
        return f'    return " ".join([{a}, {b}])'
    if operation == "add_then_multiply":
        (a, b) = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    return ({a} + {b}) * 2"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    total = {a} + {b}\n    return total * 2"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    result = {a}\n    result += {b}\n    result *= 2\n    return result"
        return f"    return 2 * ({a} + {b})"
    if operation == "multiply_then_add":
        (a, b) = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    return {a} * {b} + 2"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    product = {a} * {b}\n    return product + 2"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    result = {a}\n    result *= {b}\n    result += 2\n    return result"
        return f"    return 2 + {a} * {b}"
    if operation == "filter_and_count":
        (v,) = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    count = 0\n    for item in {v}:\n        if item > 0:\n            count += 1\n    return count"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    return len([item for item in {v} if item > 0])"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    return sum(1 for item in {v} if item > 0)"
        return (
            f"    count = 0\n    for index, item in enumerate({v}):\n"
            f"        if item > 0:\n            count += 1\n    return count"
        )
    if operation == "keep_long_words":
        (v,) = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    return [word for word in {v} if len(word) > 3]"
        if variant == 1:
            return (
                f"    result = []\n    for word in {v}:\n"
                f"        if len(word) > 3:\n            result.append(word)\n    return result"
            )
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    result = []\n    result.extend(word for word in {v} if len(word) > 3)\n    return result"
        return (
            f"    result = []\n    for index, word in enumerate({v}):\n"
            f"        if len(word) > 3:\n            result.append(word)\n    return result"
        )
    if operation == "is_even":
        (n,) = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    return {n} % 2 == 0"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    if {n} % 2 == 0:\n        return True\n    return False"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    even = {n} % 2 == 0\n    return even"
        return f"    return True if {n} % 2 == 0 else False"
    if operation == "sum_positive":
        (v,) = params
        if variant == 0:
            return f"    total = 0\n    for item in {v}:\n        if item > 0:\n            total += item\n    return total"
        if variant == 1:
            return f"    return sum(item for item in {v} if item > 0)"
        if variant == 2:
            return f"    return sum(item for item in {v} if item > 0) if {v} else 0"
        return (
            f"    total = 0\n    for index, item in enumerate({v}):\n"
            f"        if item > 0:\n            total += item\n    return total"
        )
    raise ValueError(f"unknown functional operation: {operation}")


def build_examples(
    *,
    name_offset: int = 0,
    function_offset: int = 0,
    instruction_offset: int = 0,
    per_operation: int = 12,
    seed: int = 20261107,
    split: str = "train",
    id_prefix: str = "F1",
) -> list:
    examples = []
    for operation in OPERATIONS:
        instructions = _INSTRUCTIONS[operation]
        function_names = _FUNCTION_NAMES[operation]
        samples = _SAMPLES[operation]
        for index in range(per_operation):
            if operation == "join_text":
                params = _TEXT_PAIRS[(name_offset + index) % len(_TEXT_PAIRS)]
            elif operation in ("filter_and_count", "keep_long_words", "sum_positive", "is_even"):
                params = (_SINGLES[(name_offset + index) % len(_SINGLES)],)
            else:
                params = _PAIRS[(name_offset + index) % len(_PAIRS)]
            function_name = function_names[(function_offset + index) % len(function_names)]
            instruction = instructions[(instruction_offset + index) % len(instructions)]
            variant = index % 4
            signature = f"def {function_name}({', '.join(params)}):"
            body = _body(operation, params, variant)
            _validate(signature, body)
            args, expected = samples[index % len(samples)]
            example_id = f"{id_prefix}-{operation}-{index:03d}"
            examples.append(
                build_example(
                    example_id=example_id,
                    instruction=instruction,
                    signature=signature,
                    body=body,
                    operation=operation,
                    family=_FAMILIES[operation],
                    split=split,
                    seed=seed + index,
                    metadata={
                        "markers": [operation],
                        "functional_focus": True,
                        "variant": variant,
                        "surface_variant": f"v{variant}",
                        "inputs": [list(args)],
                        "expected_outputs": [expected],
                        "relationship": _RELATIONSHIPS[operation],
                    },
                )
            )
    return examples


def build_training_examples(*, seed: int = 20261107) -> list:
    return build_examples(per_operation=12, seed=seed, split="train")


def build_validation_examples(*, seed: int = 20261108) -> list:
    return build_examples(
        name_offset=5,
        function_offset=2,
        instruction_offset=1,
        per_operation=4,
        seed=seed,
        split="validation",
        id_prefix="F1V",
    )


def functional_digest() -> str:
    payload = [
        (example.example_id, example.instruction, example.signature, example.body, example.operation)
        for example in build_training_examples()
    ]
    return hashlib.sha256(repr(payload).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def _unused_ast_check() -> None:  # pragma: no cover - import guard
    ast.parse("pass")

"""Evaluation of frozen v2.2.0 cases without executing generated code."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict

from training.program_analysis import analyse
from training.supervised import build_example
from training.supervised_train import reconstruct_program

KNOWN_OPERATIONS = frozenset({
    "add", "subtract", "multiply", "max_builtin", "min_builtin",
    "comparison_gt", "comparison_lt", "if_selection", "filter_positive",
    "filter_negative", "comprehension", "length", "upper", "lower",
    "mapping_get", "mapping_keys", "mapping_contains", "iteration",
    "count_items", "sum_items", "attr_get",
})


def _indent(body: str) -> str:
    lines = [line.rstrip() for line in (body or "").splitlines()]
    while lines and not lines[-1].strip():
        lines.pop()
    if not lines:
        return ""
    if lines[0] and not lines[0][0].isspace():
        lines = ["    " + line if line else line for line in lines]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def score_case(case: dict, continuation: str, finish_reason=None,
               tokens=0) -> dict:
    expected = analyse(case["signature"], case["body"])
    generated = analyse(case["signature"], _indent(continuation))
    reference_ops = set(expected["operations"])
    generated_ops = set(generated["operations"])
    structural = bool(generated["parses"] and reference_ops
                      and reference_ops.issubset(generated_ops))
    exact = bool(generated["parses"] and expected["parses"]
                 and generated["body_dump"] == expected["body_dump"])
    binding = bool(generated["parses"]
                   and generated["params_used"] == expected["params_used"]
                   and not generated["undefined_names"])
    control_flow = bool(generated["parses"]
                        and generated["shape"] == expected["shape"])
    composition = bool(generated["parses"] and generated["key"] == expected["key"])
    template_hit = bool(generated["parses"]
                        and generated_ops.intersection(KNOWN_OPERATIONS))
    if case.get("negative"):
        structural = False
        exact = False
        composition = False
    return {
        "case_id": case["case_id"],
        "partition": case["partition"],
        "operation": case["operation"],
        "family": case["family"],
        "composition": case.get("composition"),
        "seen_in_training": (case.get("metadata") or {}).get("seen_in_training"),
        "negative": case.get("negative"),
        "instruction": case["instruction"],
        "signature": case["signature"],
        "reference_body": case["body"],
        "continuation": continuation,
        "generated_body": _indent(continuation),
        "parses": bool(generated["parses"]),
        "error": generated["error"],
        "exact": exact,
        "structural": structural,
        "binding": binding,
        "control_flow": control_flow,
        "composition_match": composition,
        "template_hit": template_hit,
        "reference_operations": sorted(reference_ops),
        "generated_operations": sorted(generated_ops),
        "params_used": generated["params_used"],
        "undefined_names": generated["undefined_names"],
        "eos_terminated": finish_reason == "stop",
        "truncated": finish_reason == "length",
        "tokens": tokens,
    }

def _summarize(records):
    total = len(records)

    def count(name):
        return sum(1 for record in records if record.get(name))

    summary = {
        "cases": total,
        "parses": count("parses"),
        "exact": count("exact"),
        "structural": count("structural"),
        "binding": count("binding"),
        "control_flow": count("control_flow"),
        "composition_match": count("composition_match"),
        "eos_terminated": count("eos_terminated"),
        "truncated": count("truncated"),
        "template_hit": count("template_hit"),
    }
    for key in ("parses", "exact", "structural", "binding", "control_flow",
                "composition_match", "eos_terminated", "truncated"):
        summary[key + "_rate"] = round(summary[key] / total, 4) if total else 0.0
    return summary


def summarize(records) -> dict:
    by_partition = defaultdict(list)
    by_operation = defaultdict(list)
    for record in records:
        by_partition[record["partition"]].append(record)
        by_operation[record["operation"]].append(record)
    result = {"overall": _summarize(records),
              "by_partition": {key: _summarize(value)
                               for key, value in sorted(by_partition.items())},
              "by_operation": {key: _summarize(value)
                               for key, value in sorted(by_operation.items())}}
    negatives = [r for r in records if r["partition"] == "E6"]
    if negatives:
        unsafe = [r for r in negatives if r["exact"] or r["structural"]]
        result["negative_controls"] = {
            "cases": len(negatives),
            "template_hits": sum(1 for r in negatives if r["template_hit"]),
            "unsafe_credits": len(unsafe),
            "safe": len(negatives) - len(unsafe),
            "safe_rate": round((len(negatives) - len(unsafe)) / len(negatives), 4),
        }
    compositions = [r for r in records if r["partition"] == "E4"]
    if compositions:
        seen = [r for r in compositions if r["seen_in_training"]]
        unseen = [r for r in compositions if not r["seen_in_training"]]
        result["composition_transfer"] = {
            "seen": _summarize(seen), "unseen": _summarize(unseen),
        }
    return result


def paired_delta(baseline_records, candidate_records) -> dict:
    baseline = {r["case_id"]: r for r in baseline_records}
    candidate = {r["case_id"]: r for r in candidate_records}
    shared = sorted(set(baseline) & set(candidate))
    result = {"cases": len(shared)}
    for metric in ("parses", "exact", "structural", "binding", "control_flow",
                   "composition_match"):
        before = sum(1 for key in shared if baseline[key].get(metric))
        after = sum(1 for key in shared if candidate[key].get(metric))
        gained = sum(1 for key in shared
                     if candidate[key].get(metric) and not baseline[key].get(metric))
        lost = sum(1 for key in shared
                   if baseline[key].get(metric) and not candidate[key].get(metric))
        result[metric] = {
            "baseline": before, "candidate": after, "delta": after - before,
            "gained": gained, "lost": lost,
        }
    return result


def compare_partitions(baseline: dict, candidate: dict) -> dict:
    return {"overall": paired_delta(baseline["records"], candidate["records"]),
            "by_partition": {
                key: paired_delta(baseline["by_partition_records"][key],
                                  candidate["by_partition_records"][key])
                for key in sorted(set(baseline["by_partition_records"])
                                  & set(candidate["by_partition_records"]))
            }}

def evaluate_cases(model, tokenizer, cases, *, budget: int = 64,
                   device: str = "cpu", progress=None) -> dict:
    from serving.local_inference import generate_ids

    records = []
    for index, case in enumerate(cases, 1):
        example = build_example(
            example_id=case["case_id"], instruction=case["instruction"],
            signature=case["signature"], body=case["body"],
            operation=case["operation"], family=case["family"],
            split=case["partition"], seed=20261022,
            metadata=case.get("metadata") or {},
        )
        result = generate_ids(
            model, tokenizer, example.prompt_text, max_new_tokens=budget,
            temperature=0.0, device=device, seed=20261022,
        )
        continuation = result.get("text", "")
        record = score_case(
            case, continuation, finish_reason=result.get("finish_reason"),
            tokens=len(result.get("token_ids") or []),
        )
        record["prompt"] = example.prompt_text
        records.append(record)
        if progress is not None:
            progress(index, len(cases), record)
    by_partition = defaultdict(list)
    for record in records:
        by_partition[record["partition"]].append(record)
    return {"version": "2.2.0", "records": records,
            "by_partition_records": dict(by_partition),
            "metrics": summarize(records)}

def _rename(signature, body, function_name, parameter_names):
    match = re.match(r"def\s+([A-Za-z_]\w*)\(([^)]*)\):", signature)
    if not match:
        raise ValueError("invalid signature: " + signature)
    old_params = [part.strip() for part in match.group(2).split(",") if part.strip()]
    if len(old_params) != len(parameter_names):
        raise ValueError("parameter count mismatch for " + signature)
    mapping = dict(zip(old_params, parameter_names))
    new_signature = "def " + function_name + "(" + ", ".join(parameter_names) + "):"
    new_body = body
    for old, new in mapping.items():
        new_body = re.sub(r"\b" + re.escape(old) + r"\b", new, new_body)
    return new_signature, new_body


def _base(op):
    family, instruction, signature, body, _markers = OPERATIONS[op]
    return family, instruction, signature, body


def _case(case_id, partition, operation, instruction, signature, body,
          family, *, composition=None, negative=None, metadata=None):
    return {
        "case_id": case_id,
        "partition": partition,
        "operation": operation,
        "instruction": instruction,
        "signature": signature,
        "body": body,
        "family": family,
        "composition": composition,
        "negative": negative,
        "metadata": dict(metadata or {}),
    }


def e1_cases():
    cases = []
    for op in TRAINED_OPS:
        family, instruction, signature, body = _base(op)
        kind = E1_KIND[op]

            sig, bod = _rename(signature, body, name, params)
            cases.append(_case(f"E1-{op}-{index:03d}", "E1", op, instruction,
                               sig, bod, family, metadata={"variant": "name"}))
    return cases
