# Re-exported for existing callers/tests. TEMPLATE is now rendered from tokens the
# tokenizer actually registers (C3); the old "<|system|>..." form shredded into
# byte tokens because none of those markers existed in the vocabulary.
TEMPLATE = CHAT_TEMPLATE

QUARANTINE_SUFFIX = ".quarantine.json"


def find_quarantine(sft_data_path: str) -> Path | None:
    """Return the quarantine marker sitting beside an SFT dataset, if any.

    A dataset is quarantined when ``<stem>.quarantine.json`` exists next to it, e.g.
    ``data/code_sft_v0.jsonl`` -> ``data/code_sft_v0.quarantine.json``.
    """
    marker = Path(sft_data_path).with_suffix(QUARANTINE_SUFFIX)
    return marker if marker.exists() else None


class SFTPairDataset:
    def __init__(self, jsonl_path: str, tokenizer, max_length: int = 2048):
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.max_length = max_length
        self.pairs = []
        with open(jsonl_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for line in f:
                line = line.strip()
                if line:
                    self.pairs.append(json.loads(line))
        if not self.pairs:
            raise ValueError(f"No SFT pairs found in {jsonl_path}")
        # C3: refuse a tokenizer that cannot represent the template as single
        # tokens, rather than training on shredded byte fragments. The contract
        # itself is a property of the tokenizer (v1: bos/eos, v2: role markers).
        self.markers = validate_chat_template(tokenizer)
        self.contract = detect_contract(tokenizer)

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.pairs)

    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        pair = self.pairs[idx]
        instruction = pair.get("instruction", pair.get("input", ""))
        response = pair.get("response", pair.get("output", ""))
        text = render_completion(
            SYSTEM_PROMPT, instruction, response, contract_id=self.contract
        )
        ids = self.tokenizer.encode(text).ids
        truncated = len(ids) > self.max_length
        ids = ids[: self.max_length]
        input_ids = torch.tensor(ids[:-1], dtype=torch.long)
        labels = torch.tensor(ids[1:], dtype=torch.long)
        # Mask everything up to and including the prompt: supervision starts at
        # the response, and the final <eos> is what the model must learn to emit.
        prompt_ids = prompt_token_length(
            self.tokenizer, SYSTEM_PROMPT, instruction, contract_id=self.contract
        )
        prompt_ids = min(prompt_ids, labels.numel())
        labels[:prompt_ids] = -100
        return input_ids, labels


class SFTBatcher:
    """Shuffled, epoch-cycling index stream for SFT micro-batches.

    The training loop previously built each batch as
    ``[dataset[i % len(dataset)] for i in range(micro_bs)]``, where ``i`` only
    ever ranged over ``0..micro_bs-1``. Every step therefore saw the same first
    ``micro_bs`` pairs and the rest of the dataset was never trained on. This
    yields a fresh shuffle each epoch and refills mid-epoch.
    """

    def __init__(self, n_items: int, batch_size: int, seed: int = 42):
        if n_items <= 0:
            raise ValueError("cannot build batches from an empty dataset")
        self.n_items = n_items
        self.batch_size = batch_size
        self.rng = random.Random(seed)
        self._order: list[int] = []
        self._pos = 0
        # Coverage accounting (A1): the defect this class exists to fix was
        # invisible, so consumption is tracked explicitly.
        self.consumed = 0
        self.seen: set[int] = set()
        self.epochs_completed = 0
        self.refills = 0

    def _refill(self) -> None:
        self._order = list(range(self.n_items))
        self.rng.shuffle(self._order)
        if self._pos >= self.n_items:
            self.epochs_completed += 1
        self._pos = 0
        self.refills += 1

    def next_indices(self) -> list[int]:
        if not self._order:
            self._refill()
        out: list[int] = []
        while len(out) < self.batch_size:
            if self._pos >= self.n_items:
                self._refill()
            out.append(self._order[self._pos])
            self._pos += 1
        self.consumed += len(out)
        self.seen.update(out)
        return out

    @property
    def unique_coverage(self) -> float:
        """Fraction of the dataset that has been seen at least once."""
        return len(self.seen) / self.n_items if self.n_items else 0.0

    @property
    def epoch_float(self) -> float:
        return self.consumed / self.n_items if self.n_items else 0.0

    def coverage_report(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "dataset_size": self.n_items,
            "consumed_examples": self.consumed,
            "unique_examples_seen": len(self.seen),
            "unique_coverage": round(self.unique_coverage, 6),
            "epochs_completed": self.epochs_completed,
            "epochs_consumed": round(self.epoch_float, 6),
            "shuffle_refills": self.refills,
        }


def collate_sft(batch, pad_id=0):
    max_len = max(len(x[0]) for x in batch)
    input_ids = torch.full((len(batch), max_len), pad_id, dtype=torch.long)
    labels = torch.full((len(batch), max_len), -100, dtype=torch.long)
    for i, (x, y) in enumerate(batch):
        input_ids[i, : len(x)] = x
        labels[i, : len(y)] = y
    return input_ids, labels


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Quantsmind SFT training loop")
    p.add_argument("--config", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--sft-data", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--out-dir", default="runs/sft")
    p.add_argument("--init-ckpt", default=None)
    p.add_argument(
        "--init-ckpt-partial",
        action="store_true",
        help="allow --init-ckpt to initialise only the parameters it provides; "
        "the rest stay random and are reported. Shape mismatches still abort.",
    )
    p.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--resume", action="store_true")
    p.add_argument(
        "--ignore-sft-quarantine",
        action="store_true",
        help="train on a quarantined SFT dataset; diagnostics only, no capability claim",
    )
    args = p.parse_args()

    marker = find_quarantine(args.sft_data)
    if marker and not args.ignore_sft_quarantine:
        try:
            reason = json.loads(marker.read_text(encoding="utf-8")).get("reason", "see marker file")
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):
            reason = "see marker file"
        raise SystemExit(
            f"SFT dataset is quarantined: {args.sft_data}\n"
            f"  {reason}\n"
            f"  marker: {marker}\n"
            "Refusing to train. Pass --ignore-sft-quarantine to override for "
            "diagnostics only; a checkpoint trained on it supports no capability claim."
        )

    cfg = load_yaml(args.config)
    seed = cfg.get("run", {}).get("seed", 42)
    determinism = set_determinism(seed)
    print(f"determinism: {determinism}")
    out_dir = Path(args.out_dir)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    device = (
        "cuda"
        if torch.cuda.is_available()
        else ("mps" if getattr(torch.backends, "mps", None) and torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu")
    )
    print(f"device={device}")

    from tokenizers import Tokenizer

    tokenizer = Tokenizer.from_file("tokenizer/qm_code_bpe_v0.json")
    dataset = SFTPairDataset(args.sft_data, tokenizer, cfg["data"]["seq_len"])
    print(f"SFT pairs: {len(dataset)}")

    model_cfg = load_yaml(cfg["run"]["model_config"])["model"]
    model = QMModel(model_cfg).to(device)

    provenance = build_provenance(
        model_cfg=model_cfg,
        parameter_count=sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()),
        contract_id=dataset.contract,
        config=cfg,
        seed=seed,
        tokenizer=tokenizer,
        tokenizer_path="tokenizer/qm_code_bpe_v0.json",
        corpus_manifest=args.sft_data,
    )

    if args.init_ckpt:
        # B3: this used to load with strict=False and print "initialized from ..."
        # regardless of the outcome, which is how runs/code_sft silently became a
        # randomly-initialised 495,808-parameter model. Compatibility is now
        # checked, and partial loading must be asked for explicitly.
        report = init_from_checkpoint(
            model, args.init_ckpt, allow_partial=args.init_ckpt_partial
        )
        print(f"initialized from {args.init_ckpt}")
        print(report.describe())
        if report.partial and report.missing:
            print(
                f"WARNING: {len(report.missing)} parameter(s) were NOT "
                "initialised from the checkpoint and remain random."
            )

    opt_cfg = cfg["optimizer"]
    optim = torch.optim.AdamW(
        model.parameters(),
        lr=opt_cfg["lr_peak"],
        betas=(opt_cfg.get("beta1", 0.9), opt_cfg.get("beta2", 0.95)),
        weight_decay=opt_cfg.get("weight_decay", 0.1),
    )

    train_cfg = cfg["training"]
    total_steps = args.max_steps or train_cfg["max_steps"]
    start_step = 0
    last_ckpt = out_dir / "checkpoint_last.pt"
    if args.resume and last_ckpt.exists():
        start_step = load_checkpoint(last_ckpt, model, optim)
        print(f"resumed from {last_ckpt} at step {start_step}")

    if device == "cuda":
        torch.compile(model)

    batch_cfg = cfg["batch"]
    micro_bs = batch_cfg["micro_batch_size"]
    accum = batch_cfg.get("grad_accum_steps", 1)
    seq_len = cfg["data"]["seq_len"]

    log_every = train_cfg.get("log_every_steps", 10)
    ckpt_every = train_cfg.get("checkpoint_every_steps", 500)

    # A1: the loop used to build every batch as
    # ``[dataset[i % len(dataset)] for i in range(micro_bs)]``, so each step saw
    # the same first ``micro_bs`` pairs and the rest of the corpus was never
    # trained on. An explicit, shuffled, epoch-cycling batcher replaces it.
    batcher = SFTBatcher(len(dataset), micro_bs, seed=seed)
    if args.resume and start_step > 0:
        # Deterministic resume: replay the index stream the interrupted run would
        # have produced, so consumed_examples in the checkpoint matches reality
        # instead of restarting coverage from zero.
        batches_per_step = accum
        for _ in range(start_step * batches_per_step):
            batcher.next_indices()

    examples_per_step = micro_bs * accum
    logger = LossLogger(
        out_dir / "loss_log.jsonl",
        run_kind="sft",
        model_config=cfg["run"].get("model_config"),
        dataset=args.sft_data,
        config=cfg,
    )
    logger.log_header(
        total_steps=total_steps,
        dataset_size=len(dataset),
        examples_per_step=examples_per_step,
        seq_len=seq_len,
        seed=seed,
        init_ckpt=args.init_ckpt,
    )
    print(f"loss log: {out_dir / 'loss_log.jsonl'}")

    ema_loss = None
    model.train()
    t0 = time.time()

    for step in range(start_step, total_steps):
        lr = lr_at(step, total_steps, opt_cfg["lr_peak"], opt_cfg.get("warmup_steps", 0), opt_cfg.get("min_lr_ratio", 0.1))
        for g in optim.param_groups:
            g["lr"] = lr

        loss_val = 0.0
        optim.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        for _ in range(accum):
            indices = batcher.next_indices()
            batch = [dataset[i] for i in indices]
            x, y = collate_sft(batch)
            x, y = x.to(device), y.to(device)
            _, loss = model(x, targets=y)
            (loss / accum).backward()
            loss_val += loss.item() / accum

        grad_clip = opt_cfg.get("grad_clip")
        grad_norm = None
        if grad_clip:
            grad_norm = torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(
                model.parameters(), grad_clip
            )
        optim.step()

        if not math.isfinite(loss_val):
            raise RuntimeError(f"non-finite loss {loss_val} at step {step}")

        ema = 0.05 if ema_loss is None else 0.95
        ema_loss = ema * loss_val + (1 - ema) * (ema_loss or loss_val)

        if step % log_every == 0 or (step + 1) == total_steps:
            logger.log_step(
                step,
                loss_val,
                epoch=batcher.epoch_float,
                lr=lr,
                ema_loss=ema_loss,
                grad_norm=float(grad_norm) if grad_norm is not None else None,
                consumed_examples=batcher.consumed,
            )
            print(
                f"step {step}/{total_steps} loss={loss_val:.4f} "
                f"ema={ema_loss:.4f} lr={lr:.2e} "
                f"consumed={batcher.consumed} unique={len(batcher.seen)}/{len(dataset)}"
            )

        if (step + 1) % ckpt_every == 0 or (step + 1) == total_steps:
            save_checkpoint(
                last_ckpt,
                model,
                optim,
                step + 1,
                cfg,
                extra={
                    "consumed_examples": batcher.consumed,
                    "epochs_consumed": batcher.epoch_float,
                    "dataset_size": len(dataset),
                    "coverage": batcher.coverage_report(),
                },
                provenance=provenance,
            )
            print(f"checkpoint saved: {last_ckpt} (step {step + 1})")

    coverage = batcher.coverage_report()
    coverage["total_steps"] = total_steps
    coverage["optimizer_steps_completed"] = total_steps - start_step
    coverage["examples_per_step"] = examples_per_step
    coverage["eligible_examples"] = len(dataset)
    logger.close(status="complete", coverage=coverage)
    (out_dir / "sft_coverage.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(coverage, indent=2), encoding="utf-8"
    )
    print(f"coverage: {json.dumps(coverage)}")
    if coverage["unique_coverage"] < 1.0:
        print(
            f"WARNING: only {coverage['unique_coverage']:.1%} of the SFT dataset "
            "was seen. This schedule does not cover the full dataset; report it "
            "as a subset run rather than full-dataset training."
        )
    print("SFT training complete")


def load_yaml(path: str) -> dict:
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return yaml.safe_load(f)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Instruction-tuning dataset for M4 (M4 training engine input).

Thin wrapper around :func:`training.instruction_format.encode_example` that adds
shuffled epoch cycling, coverage accounting, and an explicit record of every
example that could not be used and why.

Reused from M3 rather than duplicated: ``training/checkpoint.py`` for weight
compatibility, ``training/validation.py`` for validation passes,
``training/manifest.py`` for the run record.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import random
from pathlib import Path

from training.instruction_format import FormattingError, encode_example


class InstructionDataset:
    """Instruction examples encoded with an exact assistant-only loss mask."""

    def __init__(self, jsonl_path, tokenizer, max_length=512,
                 supervise_prompt=False, seed=42):
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.max_length = max_length
        self.supervise_prompt = supervise_prompt
        self.seed = seed
        self.path = Path(jsonl_path)

        self.records = []
        malformed = []
        text = self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
        for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
            stripped = line.strip()
            if not stripped:
                continue
            try:
                self.records.append(json.loads(stripped))
            except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
                malformed.append({"line": number, "reason": str(exc)})

        self.rejected = []
        self.encoded = []
        for record in self.records:
            try:
                encoded = encode_example(
                    tokenizer,
                    record.get("instruction", ""),
                    record.get("response", ""),
                    record.get("input", "") or "",
                    max_length=max_length,
                    supervise_prompt=supervise_prompt,
                )
            except FormattingError as exc:
                self.rejected.append({
                    "id": record.get("id"), "reason": str(exc),
                })
                continue
            encoded["id"] = record.get("id")
            encoded["task"] = record.get("task")
            self.encoded.append(encoded)

        if not self.encoded:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{self.path}: no example could be encoded. "
                f"{len(self.rejected)} rejected; first: "
                + (self.rejected[0]["reason"] if self.rejected else "none")
            )

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.encoded)

    def __getitem__(self, index):
        return self.encoded[index]

    def report(self) -> dict:
        supervised = sum(item["supervised_tokens"] for item in self.encoded)
        total = sum(item["total_tokens"] for item in self.encoded)
        truncated = sum(1 for item in self.encoded if item.get("truncated"))
        return {
            "path": str(self.path),
            "records_read": len(self.records),
            "records_encoded": len(self.encoded),
            "records_rejected": len(self.rejected),
            "rejected_examples": self.rejected[:10],
            "truncated": truncated,
            "total_tokens": total,
            "supervised_tokens": supervised,
            "masked_tokens": total - supervised,
            "supervised_fraction": (supervised / total) if total else 0.0,
            "mean_tokens_per_example": (total / len(self.encoded))
            if self.encoded else 0.0,
            "max_length": self.max_length,
            "supervise_prompt": self.supervise_prompt,
        }


class EpochShuffler:
    """Shuffled, epoch-cycling index stream with coverage accounting.

    The earlier SFT loop indexed ``dataset[i % len(dataset)]`` for
    ``i`` in ``range(micro_batch_size)``, so every step saw the same first batch
    and most of the dataset was never trained on. This class fixes that and
    reports coverage explicitly.
    """

    def __init__(self, n_items: int, batch_size: int, seed: int = 42):
        if n_items <= 0:
            raise ValueError("cannot build batches from an empty dataset")
        self.n_items = n_items
        self.batch_size = batch_size
        self.rng = random.Random(seed)
        self._order: list[int] = []
        self._pos = 0
        self.consumed = 0
        self.seen: set[int] = set()
        self.epochs_completed = 0
        self.refills = 0

    def _refill(self) -> None:
        self._order = list(range(self.n_items))
        self.rng.shuffle(self._order)
        if self._pos >= self.n_items:
            self.epochs_completed += 1
        self._pos = 0
        self.refills += 1

    def next_indices(self) -> list[int]:
        if not self._order:
            self._refill()
        out: list[int] = []
        while len(out) < self.batch_size:
            if self._pos >= self.n_items:
                self._refill()
            out.append(self._order[self._pos])
            self._pos += 1
        self.consumed += len(out)
        self.seen.update(out)
        return out

    @property
    def unique_coverage(self) -> float:
        return len(self.seen) / self.n_items if self.n_items else 0.0

    def coverage_report(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "dataset_size": self.n_items,
            "consumed_examples": self.consumed,
            "unique_examples_seen": len(self.seen),
            "unique_coverage": round(self.unique_coverage, 6),
            "epochs_completed": self.epochs_completed,
            "shuffle_refills": self.refills,
        }

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\sft_train.py
"""M4 instruction-tuning engine.

Reuses the M3 engine rather than duplicating it:

* ``training.checkpoint.load_model_weights`` -- base-model compatibility checking
* ``training.pretrain.save_checkpoint`` / ``capture_rng_state`` /
  ``restore_rng_state`` / ``lr_at``
* ``training.manifest.build_run_manifest`` -- the run record
* ``training.instruction_format`` -- formatting and loss masking
* ``training.sft_dataset`` -- the encoded instruction dataset

What is M4-specific: loading the M3 base checkpoint rather than random init,
recording the base-checkpoint identity in every artifact, and the freeze policy.

The base checkpoint is opened read-only and never written back.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import math
import time
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import yaml

from training.checkpoint import CheckpointIncompatible, load_model_weights
from training.instruction_format import IGNORE_INDEX, collate
from training.manifest import build_run_manifest, write_run_manifest
from training.pretrain import (
    capture_rng_state,
    lr_at,
    restore_rng_state,
    save_checkpoint,
)
from training.sft_dataset import EpochShuffler, InstructionDataset

FORMAT_NAME = "qm.plain_instruction/1"


def load_base_model(base_checkpoint, model_config_path, device="cpu"):
    """Load the M3 base. Raises rather than silently starting from random weights."""
    from training.model import QMModel

    path = Path(base_checkpoint)
    if not path.exists():
        raise CheckpointIncompatible(f"base checkpoint not found: {path}")

    cfg = yaml.safe_load(Path(model_config_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["model"]
    model = QMModel(cfg)
    payload = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    state = payload.get("model") if isinstance(payload, dict) else None
    if state is None:
        raise CheckpointIncompatible(
            f"{path} has no 'model' entry; refusing to fine-tune it"
        )
    report = load_model_weights(model, state, source=str(path))
    if not report.ok:
        raise CheckpointIncompatible(
            f"{path} did not fully load:\n{report.describe()}"
        )
    return model.to(device), cfg, {
        "path": str(path),
        "step": payload.get("step"),
        "tokens_processed": payload.get("tokens_processed"),
        "val_loss": payload.get("val_loss"),
        "parameters_loaded": len(report.loaded),
        "dataset_identity": payload.get("dataset_identity"),
        "tokenizer_identity": payload.get("tokenizer_identity"),
    }


def apply_freeze_policy(model, policy):
    """``none`` (full fine-tune) or a parameter-name substring to freeze."""
    if policy in (None, "none", "", []):
        frozen = 0
    else:
        terms = [policy] if isinstance(policy, str) else list(policy)
        frozen = 0
        for name, param in model.named_parameters():
            if any(term in name for term in terms):
                param.requires_grad_(False)
                frozen += 1
    trainable = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
    total = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
    return {
        "policy": policy,
        "frozen_tensors": frozen,
        "trainable_parameters": trainable,
        "total_parameters": total,
        "trainable_fraction": trainable / total if total else 0.0,
    }


def masked_loss(logits, labels):
    """Cross-entropy over supervised positions only.

    Guards the all-``-100`` batch, which would otherwise produce NaN and be
    quietly averaged into the loss.
    """
    flat_logits = logits.reshape(-1, logits.size(-1))
    flat_labels = labels.reshape(-1)
    if int((flat_labels != IGNORE_INDEX).sum()) == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "batch has no supervised tokens; masking left nothing to learn from"
        )
    return torch.nn.functional.cross_entropy(
        flat_logits.float(), flat_labels, ignore_index=IGNORE_INDEX
    )


def _checkpoint_extra(step, dataset_report, base_info, tokens_per_step,
                      resumed_tokens, val_loss, cfg, start_step=0):
    """Everything a resume needs, plus the M4 identity chain (M4 §18)."""
    return {
        "dataset_tokens": dataset_report["total_tokens"],
        "seq_len": cfg["data"]["max_length"],
        "tokens_per_step": tokens_per_step,
        "optimizer_steps_completed": step,
        "tokens_processed": resumed_tokens
        + max(0, step - start_step) * tokens_per_step,
        "rng_state": capture_rng_state(),
        "val_loss": val_loss,
        "instruction_format": FORMAT_NAME,
        "m4": {
            "base_checkpoint": base_info["path"],
            "base_step": base_info["step"],
            "training_strategy": "full fine-tune (assistant-only loss)"
            if (cfg.get("adaptation") or cfg.get("model") or {}).get("freeze_policy") in (None, "none")
            else f"freeze={(cfg.get('adaptation') or cfg.get('model') or {}).get('freeze_policy')}",
            "instruction_format": FORMAT_NAME,
            "dataset": cfg["data"]["train_jsonl"],
            "dataset_manifest": cfg["data"].get("dataset_manifest"),
            "tokenizer": cfg["data"]["tokenizer"],
            "seed": cfg.get("run", {}).get("seed"),
        },
        "created_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat(),
    }


def _validate(model, val_set, micro_bs, batches, seed, max_length, device,
              pad_id):
    """Validation without weight updates, on a fixed window stream."""
    previous = model.training
    model.eval()
    total, counted = 0.0, 0
    try:
        with torch.no_grad():
            stream = EpochShuffler(len(val_set), micro_bs, seed=seed)
            for _ in range(batches):
                items = [val_set[i] for i in stream.next_indices()]
                batch = collate(items, pad_id=pad_id)
                _, loss = model(
                    batch["input_ids"].to(device),
                    targets=batch["labels"].to(device),
                )
                total += float(loss.item())
                counted += 1
    finally:
        if previous:
            model.train()
    return total / counted if counted else None


def run(config_path, out_dir, max_steps=None, resume=False, device=None):
    cfg = yaml.safe_load(Path(config_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    data_cfg, run_cfg = cfg["data"], cfg["run"]
    train_cfg, opt_cfg = cfg["training"], cfg["optimizer"]
    batch_cfg = cfg["batch"]

    if device is None:
        requested = (cfg.get("precision") or {}).get("device", "auto")
        device = ("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu") \
            if requested == "auto" else requested

    from tokenizers import Tokenizer

    tokenizer = Tokenizer.from_file(data_cfg["tokenizer"])
    model, model_cfg, base_info = load_base_model(
        run_cfg["base_checkpoint"], run_cfg["base_model_config"], device
    )
    print(f"base checkpoint : {base_info['path']} "
          f"(step {base_info['step']}, {base_info['parameters_loaded']} tensors)")

    freeze_report = apply_freeze_policy(
        model, (cfg.get("adaptation") or cfg.get("model") or {}).get("freeze_policy")
    )
    print(f"freeze policy   : {freeze_report['policy']} "
          f"({freeze_report['trainable_parameters']:,} trainable / "
          f"{freeze_report['total_parameters']:,} total)")

    supervise_prompt = bool(data_cfg.get("supervise_prompt", False))
    train_set = InstructionDataset(
        data_cfg["train_jsonl"], tokenizer,
        max_length=data_cfg["max_length"],
        supervise_prompt=supervise_prompt, seed=run_cfg.get("seed", 42),
    )
    val_set = InstructionDataset(
        data_cfg["val_jsonl"], tokenizer,
        max_length=data_cfg["max_length"],
        supervise_prompt=supervise_prompt, seed=1234,
    )
    report_train = train_set.report()
    print(f"train examples  : {len(train_set)} encoded, "
          f"{len(train_set.rejected)} rejected, "
          f"{report_train['supervised_tokens']:,} supervised tokens")
    print(f"val examples    : {len(val_set)} encoded")

    micro_bs = batch_cfg["micro_batch_size"]
    accum = batch_cfg.get("grad_accum_steps", 1)
    max_length, pad_id = data_cfg["max_length"], 0
    tokens_per_step = micro_bs * accum * max_length
    shuffle = EpochShuffler(len(train_set), micro_bs, seed=run_cfg.get("seed", 42))
    val_seed = data_cfg.get("val_seed", 1234)

    optim = torch.optim.AdamW(
        [p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad],
        lr=opt_cfg["lr_peak"],
        betas=(opt_cfg.get("beta1", 0.9), opt_cfg.get("beta2", 0.95)),
        weight_decay=opt_cfg.get("weight_decay", 0.01),
    )

    out_path = Path(out_dir)
    out_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    last_ckpt = out_path / "checkpoint_last.pt"
    best_ckpt = out_path / "checkpoint_best.pt"

    total_steps = max_steps or train_cfg["max_steps"]
    start_step, resumed_tokens, warnings = 0, 0, []
    if resume:
        if not last_ckpt.exists():
            raise SystemExit(f"--resume requested but no checkpoint at {last_ckpt}")
        payload = torch.load(last_ckpt, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
        load_model_weights(model, payload["model"], source=str(last_ckpt))
        optim.load_state_dict(payload["optimizer"])
        start_step = int(payload["step"])
        resumed_tokens = int(payload.get("tokens_processed") or 0)
        if restore_rng_state(payload.get("rng_state")):
            print(f"resumed at step {start_step} (RNG state restored)")
        else:
            warnings.append("resumed without RNG state; best-effort continuity")
            print(f"resumed at step {step if False else start_step} (best-effort)")

    eval_every = train_cfg.get("eval_every_steps", 0)
    val_batches = train_cfg.get("val_batches", 8)
    ckpt_every = train_cfg.get("checkpoint_every_steps", 40)
    log_every = train_cfg.get("log_every_steps", 10)
    nan_every = (cfg.get("watchdog") or {}).get("nan_check_every_steps", 10)

    best_val = None
    history: list[dict] = []
    events: list[dict] = []
    model.train()
    started = time.perf_counter()
    start_iso = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat()

    for step in range(start_step, total_steps):
        lr = lr_at(step, total_steps, opt_cfg["lr_peak"],
                   opt_cfg.get("warmup_steps", 0), opt_cfg.get("min_ratio", 0.1))
        for group in optim.param_groups:
            group["lr"] = lr

        optim.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        loss_val = 0.0
        for _ in range(accum):
            items = [train_set[i] for i in shuffle.next_indices()]
            batch = collate(items, pad_id=pad_id)
            _, loss = model(batch["input_ids"].to(device),
                            targets=batch["labels"].to(device))
            (loss / accum).backward()
            loss_val += float(loss.item()) / accum

        if nan_every and step % nan_every == 0:
            bad = [n for n, p in model.named_parameters()
                   if p.grad is not None and not torch.isfinite(p.grad).all()]
            if bad:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"non-finite gradients in {len(bad)} parameter(s) at step "
                    f"{step} (first: {bad[0]}); aborting per watchdog policy"
                )
        if opt_cfg.get("grad_clip"):
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), opt_cfg["grad_clip"])
        optim.step()

        if not math.isfinite(loss_val):
            raise RuntimeError(f"non-finite loss {loss_val} at step {step}")

        val_loss = None
        if eval_every and ((step + 1) % eval_every == 0
                           or (step + 1) == total_steps):
            val_loss = _validate(model, val_set, micro_bs, val_batches,
                                 val_seed, max_length, device, pad_id)
            if best_val is None or val_loss < best_val:
                best_val = val_loss
                save_checkpoint(
                    best_ckpt, model, optim, step + 1, cfg,
                    extra=_checkpoint_extra(
                        step + 1, report_train, base_info, tokens_per_step,
                        resumed_tokens, val_loss, cfg, start_step),
                )
                events.append({"event": "best_validation", "step": step + 1,
                               "val_loss": val_loss, "path": str(best_ckpt)})
                print(f"  val_loss={val_loss:.4f} -> new best")
            else:
                print(f"  val_loss={val_loss:.4f} (best {best_val:.4f})")

        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
        if step % log_every == 0 or (step + 1) == total_steps:
            rate = tokens_per_step * (step - start_step + 1) / (elapsed or 1)
            print(f"step {step}/{total_steps} loss={loss_val:.4f} "
                  f"lr={lr:.2e} tok/s={rate:.0f}")
            history.append({"step": step, "train_loss": loss_val,
                            "val_loss": val_loss, "lr": lr,
                            "tokens_per_second": rate,
                            "elapsed_seconds": elapsed})

        if (step + 1) % ckpt_every == 0 or (step + 1) == total_steps:
            save_checkpoint(
                last_ckpt, model, optim, step + 1, cfg,
                extra=_checkpoint_extra(
                    step + 1, report_train, base_info, tokens_per_step,
                    resumed_tokens, val_loss, cfg, start_step),
            )
            events.append({"event": "periodic", "step": step + 1,
                           "path": str(last_ckpt)})
            print(f"checkpoint saved: {last_ckpt} (step {step + 1})")

    steps_run = total_steps - start_step
    tokens_processed = resumed_tokens + steps_run * tokens_per_step
    finished = start_step + steps_run >= total_steps
    status = "complete" if finished else "stopped_early"
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started

    manifest = build_run_manifest(
        run_id=run_cfg.get("name", "m4-sft"),
        status=status, config=cfg, config_path=config_path,
        model_cfg=model_cfg, model_config_path=run_cfg.get("base_model_config"),
        params=sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()),
        tokenizer_path=data_cfg["tokenizer"],
        tokenizer_vocab=tokenizer.get_vocab_size(),
        dataset_manifest=data_cfg.get("dataset_manifest"),
        dataset_paths=[data_cfg["train_jsonl"], data_cfg["val_jsonl"]],
        seed=run_cfg.get("seed"), checkpoint_path=str(last_ckpt),
        steps_completed=steps_run, planned_steps=total_steps,
        tokens_processed=tokens_processed,
        metrics={
            "final_train_loss": history[-1]["train_loss"] if history else None,
            "best_validation_loss": best_val,
            "uniform_random_baseline_loss": math.log(model_cfg["vocab_size"]),
            "tokens_per_step": tokens_per_step,
        },
        start_time=start_iso,
        end_time=datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat(),
        elapsed_seconds=elapsed, warnings=warnings,
        stopping_criteria={"planned_max_steps": total_steps,
                           "stop_reason": None if finished else "step limit"},
        history=history,
        notes=["Base checkpoint is opened read-only and never modified."],
    )
    manifest["adaptation"] = {
        "base_checkpoint": base_info,
        "freeze_policy": freeze_report,
        "instruction_format": FORMAT_NAME,
        "assistant_only_loss": not supervise_prompt,
        "dataset_report_train": train_set.report(),
        "dataset_report_val": val_set.report(),
        "coverage": shuffle.coverage_report(),
        "checkpoint_events": events,
        "validation": {
            "batches": val_batches, "seed": val_seed,
            "note": ("fixed seed and fixed window order, so validation loss is "
                     "comparable across steps"),
        },
    }
    manifest["holdout_policy"] = (
        "The M2 holdout (test split) was not used for training, validation, or "
        "any threshold choice. It remains unspent."
    )
    manifest_path = write_run_manifest(
        (cfg.get("logging") or {}).get("run_manifest_path")
        or (out_path / "run_manifest.json"),
        manifest,
    )

    print(f"run manifest: {manifest_path}")
    print(f"status={status} steps={start_step + steps_run}/{total_steps} "
          f"tokens={tokens_processed}")
    if best_val is not None:
        print(f"best validation loss: {best_val:.4f}")
    return manifest


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="M4 instruction tuning on the M3 base checkpoint"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--config", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", default="runs/m4_sft")
    parser.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--resume", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--device", default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        run(args.config, args.out_dir, max_steps=args.max_steps,
            resume=args.resume, device=args.device)
    except (CheckpointIncompatible, ValueError) as exc:
        print(f"instruction tuning refused: {exc}")
        return 1
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Instruction-to-code supervision with response-only loss masking (v2.1.0).

The v2.0.0 finding was that the *training text did not contain the
instruction*: the curriculum trained on bare reference code while the
evaluator prompted with an instruction plus a signature. A causal model can
only condition on tokens it has seen, so that setup could never teach
instruction-to-operation mapping, whatever the learning rate.

This module fixes the supervision path for the synthetic training only:

* the **training text** is ``instruction + signature + body`` — the model sees
  the instruction and then continues with the requested implementation;
* the **loss** is masked to the response (body plus the end-of-document
  token), so the objective is "given this instruction and signature, produce
  this body", and prompt tokens are never a learning target;
* the **evaluation prompt** is exactly the prefix the model was trained on,
  so training and inference agree.

Nothing here touches production serving, the tokenizer, or the model.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from training.objective import IGNORE_INDEX

PROMPT_SEPARATOR = "\n"


class SupervisionError(ValueError):
    """A supervised example is not safe to train on."""


@dataclass
class SupervisedExample:
    """One instruction-to-code example with its supervision metadata."""

    example_id: str
    instruction: str
    signature: str
    body: str
    operation: str
    family: str
    split: str
    seed: int
    content_sha256: str = ""
    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def prompt_text(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.instruction}{PROMPT_SEPARATOR}{self.signature}{PROMPT_SEPARATOR}"

    @property
    def target_text(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.body}{PROMPT_SEPARATOR}"

    @property
    def full_text(self) -> str:
        return self.prompt_text + self.target_text

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "example_id": self.example_id,
            "instruction": self.instruction,
            "signature": self.signature,
            "body": self.body,
            "operation": self.operation,
            "family": self.family,
            "split": self.split,
            "seed": self.seed,
            "content_sha256": self.content_sha256,
            "metadata": dict(self.metadata),
        }


def build_example(
    *,
    example_id: str,
    instruction: str,
    signature: str,
    body: str,
    operation: str,
    family: str,
    split: str,
    seed: int,
    metadata: dict | None = None,
) -> SupervisedExample:
    """Build one example and hash its training text."""
    if not instruction.strip():
        raise SupervisionError(f"{example_id}: the instruction is empty")
    if not body.strip():
        raise SupervisionError(f"{example_id}: the target body is empty")
    example = SupervisedExample(
        example_id=example_id,
        instruction=instruction,
        signature=signature,
        body=body,
        operation=operation,
        family=family,
        split=split,
        seed=seed,
        metadata=dict(metadata or {}),
    )
    example.content_sha256 = hashlib.sha256(
        example.full_text.encode("utf-8")
    ).hexdigest()
    return example


def supervise(
    tokenizer,
    example: SupervisedExample,
    *,
    max_length: int = 256,
    eos_token: str = "<eos>",
    required_markers=(),
) -> dict:
    """Tokenise one example and mask the loss to the response only.

    Returns the token ids, the labels, the prompt and target boundaries, the
    supervised and masked positions, the end-of-document position, whether the
    example was truncated, and whether the required operation survived
    truncation.
    """
    prompt_ids = tokenizer.encode(example.prompt_text, add_special_tokens=False).ids
    target_ids = tokenizer.encode(example.target_text, add_special_tokens=False).ids
    eos_id = tokenizer.token_to_id(eos_token)
    if eos_id is None:
        raise SupervisionError(f"the tokenizer has no {eos_token!r} token")
    target_ids = list(target_ids) + [eos_id]

    ids = list(prompt_ids) + list(target_ids)
    truncated = len(ids) > max_length
    if truncated:
        ids = ids[:max_length]
        target_ids = target_ids[: max(0, max_length - len(prompt_ids))]

    prompt_len = min(len(prompt_ids), len(ids))
    labels = list(ids[1:])
    # ``labels[i]`` predicts ``ids[i + 1]``, so the label that predicts the
    # *first target token* sits at index ``prompt_len - 1``. Only the labels
    # that predict prompt tokens (indices 0 .. prompt_len - 2) are masked.
    # Masking one label too many would hide the first target token, and the
    # model would learn to emit the terminator instead of the body.
    for index in range(max(0, min(prompt_len - 1, len(labels)))):
        labels[index] = IGNORE_INDEX
    supervised = [
        index for index, label in enumerate(labels) if label != IGNORE_INDEX
    ]
    masked = [index for index, label in enumerate(labels) if label == IGNORE_INDEX]
    kept_text = tokenizer.decode(ids[prompt_len:]).strip()
    return {
        "ids": ids,
        "labels": labels,
        "prompt_len": prompt_len,
        "target_len": len(ids) - prompt_len,
        "supervised_positions": supervised,
        "masked_positions": masked,
        "eos_position": len(ids) - 1 if eos_id in ids else None,
        "truncated": truncated,
        "operation_preserved": all(marker in kept_text for marker in required_markers),
        "kept_target_text": kept_text,
    }


def verify_supervision(tokenizer, example: SupervisedExample, **kwargs) -> list:
    """Return every supervision defect found for one example.

    An empty list means the example is safe to train on: the instruction
    precedes the target, the response boundary is explicit, the target tokens
    are supervised, the prompt tokens are masked, the end-of-document token is
    supervised, and truncation did not remove the required operation.
    """
    problems: list = []
    supervision = supervise(tokenizer, example, **kwargs)
    ids = supervision["ids"]
    labels = supervision["labels"]
    if not supervision["supervised_positions"]:
        problems.append("no target token contributes to the loss")
    if supervision["prompt_len"] == 0:
        problems.append("the prompt is empty")
    if supervision["target_len"] == 0:
        problems.append("the target is empty")
    if supervision["eos_position"] is None:
        problems.append("the end-of-document token was not produced")
    if supervision["truncated"] and not supervision["operation_preserved"]:
        problems.append("truncation removed the required operation")
    for index in supervision["masked_positions"]:
        if index >= supervision["prompt_len"]:
            problems.append("a prompt token index is inside the target region")
    if supervision["prompt_len"] and len(supervision["masked_positions"]) != (
        supervision["prompt_len"] - 1
    ):
        problems.append(
            "the number of masked labels is not prompt_len - 1: the first "
            "target token would be hidden from the loss"
        )
    if len(ids) != len(labels) + 1:
        problems.append("the label count is not the token count minus one")
    return problems

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\supervised_train.py
"""Aligned supervised training and evaluation (Taksh v2.1.0).

The training loop consumes :class:`training.supervised.SupervisedExample`
objects: the *whole* text (instruction + signature + body) is presented to the
model, and the loss is masked to the response only. Evaluation uses exactly
the prompt prefix the model was trained on, so training and inference agree.

Metrics are static: the generated program is parsed and compared, never
executed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import math
import time

import torch

from training.determinism import set_determinism
from training.objective import IGNORE_INDEX, accumulation_weights, token_mean_loss
from training.schedules import WarmupCosineSchedule
from training.sequence import Batch


def build_batches(tokenizer, examples, *, max_length: int = 256, eos_token: str = "<eos>", identifier_config=None):
    """Tokenise examples into masked training batches.

    With ``identifier_config=None`` (default) batches carry no weights and
    the objective is exactly the previous token-mean objective. With an
    :class:`~training.identifier_supervision.IdentifierSupervisionConfig`,
    each batch carries a mean-1.0 ``weights`` tensor aligned with its
    labels, computed once per example (never re-applied).
    """
    from training.identifier_supervision import classify_identifiers, loss_weights
    from training.supervised import supervise

    batches = []
    for example in examples:
        supervision = supervise(
            tokenizer, example, max_length=max_length, eos_token=eos_token,
            required_markers=example.metadata.get("markers", ()),
        )
        if not supervision["supervised_positions"]:
            continue
        ids = supervision["ids"]
        labels = supervision["labels"]
        inputs = torch.tensor([ids[:-1]], dtype=torch.long)
        target = torch.tensor(labels, dtype=torch.long)
        weights = None
        if identifier_config is not None:
            occurrences = classify_identifiers(example.signature, example.body)
            weights = torch.tensor(
                loss_weights(supervision, occurrences, tokenizer=tokenizer, config=identifier_config)["weights"],
                dtype=torch.float32,
            )
        batches.append(
            {
                "input_ids": inputs,
                "labels": target,
                "weights": weights,
                "supervised": len(supervision["supervised_positions"]),
                "example_id": example.example_id,
                "operation": example.operation,
            }
        )
    return batches


def weighted_mean_loss(logits, labels, item_weights):
    """Mean loss for one batch, weighted if ``item_weights`` is present.

    Returns ``(micro_mean, supervised_count)`` matching the existing
    ``summed / supervised`` contract of :func:`token_mean_loss`.
    """
    if item_weights is None:
        summed, supervised = token_mean_loss(logits, labels)
        if supervised == 0:
            return None, 0
        return summed / supervised, supervised
    from training.identifier_supervision import weighted_token_mean_loss

    return weighted_token_mean_loss(logits, labels, item_weights)


def _batch_tensor(items) -> Batch:
    inputs = torch.cat([item["input_ids"] for item in items], dim=0)
    labels = torch.cat([item["labels"] for item in items], dim=0)
    attention = torch.ones_like(inputs)
    return Batch(
        input_ids=inputs,
        labels=labels,
        attention_mask=attention,
        supervised_tokens=int(sum(item["supervised"] for item in items)),
        document_count=len(items),
    )


def train_supervised(
    *,
    model_config: dict,
    tokenizer,
    examples,
    val_examples,
    lr: float,
    steps: int,
    max_length: int = 256,
    grad_accum: int = 2,
    seed: int = 20261021,
    identifier_config=None,
    warmup: int = 2,
    weight_decay: float = 0.1,
    grad_clip: float = 1.0,
    artifacts=None,
    device: str = "cpu",
):
    """Train on instruction-aligned examples and return metrics plus the model."""
    from training.model import QMModel

    set_determinism(seed)
    model = QMModel(model_config).to(device)
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        model.parameters(), lr=lr, betas=(0.9, 0.95), weight_decay=weight_decay
    )
    schedule = WarmupCosineSchedule(
        peak_lr=lr, warmup_steps=warmup, total_steps=steps, min_ratio=0.1
    )
    train_batches = build_batches(tokenizer, examples, max_length=max_length, identifier_config=identifier_config)
    val_batches = build_batches(tokenizer, val_examples, max_length=max_length, identifier_config=identifier_config)
    if not train_batches:
        raise ValueError("no trainable examples were produced")

    generator = torch.Generator()
    generator.manual_seed(seed)
    order = torch.randperm(len(train_batches), generator=generator).tolist()

    history = []
    consumed = 0
    started = time.time()
    for step in range(steps):
        window = []
        for micro in range(grad_accum):
            index = order[(step * grad_accum + micro) % len(order)]
            window.append(train_batches[index])
        counts = [item["supervised"] for item in window]
        weights = accumulation_weights(counts)
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        loss_value = 0.0
        for item, weight in zip(window, weights):
            batch = _batch_tensor([item])
            logits, _ = model(batch.input_ids.to(device))
            micro_mean, supervised = weighted_mean_loss(logits, batch.labels.to(device), item.get("weights"))
            if supervised == 0 or micro_mean is None:
                continue
            (micro_mean * weight).backward()
            loss_value += float(micro_mean.item()) * weight
        grad_norm = float(
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(
                model.parameters(), grad_clip, error_if_nonfinite=False
            )
        )
        learning_rate = schedule.lr_at(step)
        for group in optimizer.param_groups:
            group["lr"] = learning_rate
        optimizer.step()
        consumed += sum(counts)
        history.append(
            {
                "step": step + 1,
                "loss": loss_value,
                "lr": learning_rate,
                "grad_norm_before_clip": grad_norm,
                "supervised_tokens": sum(counts),
                "finite_loss": math.isfinite(loss_value),
            }
        )
        if not math.isfinite(loss_value):
            break

    val_loss = _validation_loss(model, val_batches, device)
    result = {
        "lr": lr,
        "steps": len(history),
        "requested_steps": steps,
        "tokens_consumed": consumed,
        "initial_loss": history[0]["loss"] if history else None,
        "final_loss": history[-1]["loss"] if history else None,
        "validation_loss": val_loss,
        "elapsed_seconds": round(time.time() - started, 2),
        "history": history,
        "train_examples": len(examples),
        "val_examples": len(val_examples),
        "seed": seed,
    }
    if artifacts is not None:
        artifacts.write_metric("training.json", result)
    return result, model


def _validation_loss(model, batches, device) -> float | None:
    if not batches:
        return None
    total = 0.0
    count = 0
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for item in batches:
            batch = _batch_tensor([item])
            logits, _ = model(batch.input_ids.to(device))
            mean_loss, supervised = weighted_mean_loss(logits, batch.labels.to(device), item.get("weights"))
            if supervised:
                total += float((mean_loss * supervised).item())
            count += supervised
    model.train()
    return (total / count) if count else None


class EvaluationError(ValueError):
    """An evaluation record cannot be assembled safely."""


def reconstruct_program(signature: str, body: str) -> str:
    """Assemble Python source from a signature and a body.

    The natural-language instruction is deliberately excluded: only the
    signature and the generated body are Python source. The same rule is used
    for the reference body and for a generated continuation, so the two are
    compared symmetrically. Indentation carried by the body is preserved; a
    body emitted flush-left is indented once so that it can be parsed as the
    function block.
    """
    if not signature or not signature.strip():
        raise EvaluationError("a signature is required to reconstruct a program")
    signature = signature.rstrip()
    lines = [line.rstrip() for line in (body or "").splitlines()]
    while lines and not lines[-1].strip():
        lines.pop()
    if not lines:
        return signature + "\n"
    if lines[0] and not lines[0][0].isspace():
        lines = [f"    {line}" if line else line for line in lines]
    return signature + "\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def _expression_operations(node) -> set:
    """Operation tags implied by the value an expression computes."""
    operations = set()
    if isinstance(node, ast.BinOp):
        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Add):
            operations.add("add")
        elif isinstance(node.op, ast.Sub):
            operations.add("subtract")
        elif isinstance(node.op, ast.Mult):
            operations.add("multiply")
    elif isinstance(node, ast.ListComp):
        for generator in node.generators:
            for condition in generator.ifs:
                for sub in ast.walk(condition):
                    if not isinstance(sub, ast.Compare):
                        continue
                    for op in sub.ops:
                        if isinstance(op, ast.Gt):
                            operations.add("keep_positive")
                        elif isinstance(op, ast.Lt):
                            operations.add("keep_negative")
    elif isinstance(node, ast.Call):
        function = node.func
        if isinstance(function, ast.Attribute):
            if function.attr == "upper":
                operations.add("upper")
            elif function.attr == "lower":
                operations.add("lower")
            elif function.attr == "get":
                operations.add("mapping_get")
        elif isinstance(function, ast.Name) and function.id == "len":
            operations.add("mapping_len")
    return operations


def _selection_operations(statements) -> set:
    """Operations performed by an if/return selection, e.g. a maximum.

    Credit requires a genuine selection: the branch returns one of the two
    values being compared. Merely comparing two values and returning a boolean
    is not a maximum, and an operator in an unrelated expression earns nothing.
    """
    operations = set()
    for statement in statements:
        if not isinstance(statement, ast.If):
            continue
        test = statement.test
        if not isinstance(test, ast.Compare) or len(test.ops) != 1:
            continue
        direction = None
        if isinstance(test.ops[0], ast.Gt):
            direction = "max_gt"
        elif isinstance(test.ops[0], ast.Lt):
            direction = "min_lt"
        if direction is None:
            continue
        operands = [test.left] + list(test.comparators)
        returned = [
            node.value
            for branch in (statement.body, statement.orelse)
            for node in branch
            if isinstance(node, ast.Return) and node.value is not None
        ]
        if not returned:
            continue
        if all(
            any(ast.dump(value) == ast.dump(operand) for operand in operands)
            for value in returned
        ):
            operations.add(direction)
    return operations


def analyse_program(source: str) -> dict:
    """Static analysis of one reconstructed program. Never executes code."""
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(source)
    except (SyntaxError, ValueError):
        return {"parses": False, "operations": set(), "body_dump": None}
    functions = [
        node for node in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef)
    ]
    if not functions:
        return {"parses": False, "operations": set(), "body_dump": None}
    function = functions[-1]
    returns = [
        node.value
        for node in ast.walk(function)
        if isinstance(node, ast.Return) and node.value is not None
    ]
    returned_names = {node.id for node in returns if isinstance(node, ast.Name)}
    operations = set()
    for value in returns:
        operations |= _expression_operations(value)
    for node in ast.walk(function):
        if not isinstance(node, ast.AugAssign):
            continue
        target = getattr(node.target, "id", "")
        if not isinstance(node.op, ast.Add) or target not in returned_names:
            continue
        if "count" in target:
            operations.add("count_items")
        elif "total" in target:
            operations.add("sum_items")
    operations |= _selection_operations(function.body)
    return {
        "parses": True,
        "operations": operations,
        "body_dump": ast.dump(
            ast.Module(body=function.body, type_ignores=[]), annotate_fields=False
        ),
    }


def evaluate_supervised(model, tokenizer, examples, *, budget: int = 96,
                        device: str = "cpu") -> dict:
    """Evaluate instruction-to-operation behaviour on a partition.

    The model is prompted with exactly the training prompt prefix, and the
    continuation is parsed and compared statically. No program is executed.
    """
    from serving.local_inference import generate_ids

    if isinstance(examples, dict):
        flat = []
        for split in sorted(examples):
            flat.extend(examples[split])
        examples = flat

    records = []
    for example in examples:
        result = generate_ids(
            model, tokenizer, example.prompt_text, max_new_tokens=budget,
            temperature=0.0, device=device,
        )
        continuation = result.get("text", "")
        markers = example.metadata.get("markers", [])
        reference_source = reconstruct_program(example.signature, example.body)
        generated_source = reconstruct_program(example.signature, continuation)
        reference = analyse_program(reference_source)
        generated = analyse_program(generated_source)
        expected = set(reference["operations"])
        structural = bool(
            generated["parses"] and expected
            and expected.issubset(generated["operations"])
        )
        exact = bool(
            generated["parses"] and reference["parses"]
            and generated["body_dump"] == reference["body_dump"]
        )
        # The historical operator-token metric is retained unchanged so that
        # earlier reports remain comparable. It is a *token* check, not a
        # structural check, and is never used for the structural verdict.
        operator_token = bool(markers) and any(
            marker in (example.prompt_text + continuation) for marker in markers
        )
        records.append(
            {
                "example_id": example.example_id,
                "operation": example.operation,
                "family": example.family,
                "split": example.split,
                "syntax_valid": generated["parses"],
                "complete_function": generated["parses"],
                "parses": generated["parses"],
                "operation_agreement": operator_token,
                "structural_operation": structural,
                "expected_operations": sorted(expected),
                "generated_operations": sorted(generated["operations"]),
                "exact_target": exact,
                "ast_equal": exact,
                "status": (
                    "complete_and_exact" if exact else
                    "complete_correct_operation" if structural else
                    "complete_wrong_operation" if generated["parses"] else
                    "incomplete"
                ),
                "tokens": len(result.get("token_ids") or []),
                "finish_reason": result.get("finish_reason"),
                "eos_terminated": result.get("finish_reason") == "stop",
                "truncated": result.get("finish_reason") == "length",
                "degenerate": _degenerate(continuation, result.get("token_ids") or []),
                "text": continuation,
            }
        )
    return {"records": records, "metrics": supervised_metrics(records)}


def _degenerate(text: str, tokens) -> bool:
    if not tokens:
        return True
    longest = 1
    run = 1
    for previous, current in zip(tokens, tokens[1:]):
        run = run + 1 if current == previous else 1
        longest = max(longest, run)
    if longest >= 8:
        return True
    lines = [line.strip() for line in (text or "").splitlines() if line.strip()]
    if len(lines) >= 2 and len(set(lines)) / len(lines) < 0.5:
        return True
    return False


def supervised_metrics(records) -> dict:
    total = len(records)
    if not total:
        return {"cases": 0}
    return {
        "cases": total,
        "syntax_valid": sum(
            1 for r in records if r.get("syntax_valid", r.get("parses"))
        ),
        "complete_function": sum(
            1 for r in records if r.get("complete_function", r.get("parses"))
        ),
        "operation_agreement": sum(
            1 for r in records if r.get("operation_agreement")
        ),
        "structural_operation": sum(
            1 for r in records if r.get("structural_operation")
        ),
        "exact_target": sum(1 for r in records if r.get("exact_target")),
        "complete_and_exact": sum(
            1 for r in records if r.get("status") == "complete_and_exact"
        ),
        "complete_correct_operation": sum(
            1 for r in records if r.get("status") == "complete_correct_operation"
        ),
        "complete_wrong_operation": sum(
            1 for r in records if r.get("status") == "complete_wrong_operation"
        ),
        "incomplete": sum(1 for r in records if r.get("status") == "incomplete"),
        "degenerate": sum(1 for r in records if r.get("degenerate")),
        "eos_terminated": sum(1 for r in records if r.get("eos_terminated")),
        "truncated": sum(1 for r in records if r.get("truncated")),
        "mean_tokens": round(
            sum(r.get("tokens") or 0 for r in records) / total, 2
        ),
    }

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\synthetic_curriculum.py
"""Deterministic synthetic Python curriculum for the v1.9.0 experiment.

The curriculum exists to answer one question: can the S2 model learn
*reusable* Python structure, or only memorised templates? To make that
distinguishable it is generated from explicit grammars, not by paraphrasing a
corpus, and it is partitioned so that three different kinds of generalisation
can be measured separately:

``train``
    Four families. Two families are deliberately withheld.
``A`` (in-distribution holdout)
    The trained families with unseen parameter combinations and unseen
    function names.
``B`` (compositional holdout)
    New compositions of familiar operations, never seen in training.
``C`` (family holdout)
    Two entirely withheld families, with their own structures.

Nothing here derives from a real corpus, a benchmark, or the repository's
historical data. Every sample is generated from the grammars below with a
fixed seed, and every sample carries a content hash, a template id and a
family label so contamination can be measured rather than assumed.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

FAMILIES = (
    "arithmetic",
    "conditionals",
    "list_ops",
    "string_ops",
    "dict_ops",
    "loop_agg",
)

TRAIN_FAMILIES = ("arithmetic", "conditionals", "list_ops", "string_ops")
HELDOUT_FAMILIES = ("dict_ops", "loop_agg")

TRAIN_NAMES = {
    "arithmetic": ("add_pair", "scale_value", "offset_amount"),
    "conditionals": ("choose_sign", "classify_range"),
    "list_ops": ("keep_positive", "double_all", "drop_small"),
    "string_ops": ("reverse_text", "count_letters"),
}
UNSEEN_NAMES = {
    "arithmetic": ("combine_amounts", "shift_value"),
    "conditionals": ("label_value", "bucket_number"),
    "list_ops": ("filter_even", "square_each"),
    "string_ops": ("flip_text", "letter_frequency"),
}
HELDOUT_NAMES = {
    "dict_ops": ("lookup_default", "merge_counts"),
    "loop_agg": ("sum_even_values", "count_long_words"),
}


@dataclass
class Case:
    """One generated task."""

    case_id: str
    family: str
    partition: str
    template_id: str
    prompt: str
    reference: str
    content_sha256: str
    params: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "case_id": self.case_id,
            "family": self.family,
            "partition": self.partition,
            "template_id": self.template_id,
            "prompt": self.prompt,
            "reference": self.reference,
            "content_sha256": self.content_sha256,
            "params": dict(self.params),
        }


def _hash(text: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def _normalized_hash(text: str) -> str:
    """Hash with identifiers and numbers erased, so parameter swaps collide."""
    stripped = re.sub(r"\b[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\b", "ID", text)
    stripped = re.sub(r"\d+", "N", stripped)
    return _hash(stripped)


def _shingles(text: str, size: int = 5) -> set:
    tokens = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*|\d+|[^\sA-Za-z_0-9]", text)
    if len(tokens) < size:
        return {" ".join(tokens)} if tokens else set()
    return {" ".join(tokens[i : i + size]) for i in range(len(tokens) - size + 1)}


def _jaccard(left: set, right: set) -> float:
    if not left or not right:
        return 0.0
    return len(left & right) / len(left | right)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Family grammars. Each returns (prompt, reference, template_id, params).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _arithmetic(name: str, rng) -> tuple:
    salt = _SALT[0]
    left, right = 2 + salt, 3 + salt
    prompt = f'def {name}(left, right):\n    """Return the sum of the two inputs."""\n'
    reference = (
        f'def {name}(left, right):\n'
        f'    """Return the sum of the two inputs."""\n'
        f"    return left + right + {left}\n"
    )
    return prompt, reference, "arithmetic:sum", {"offset": left, "right": right}


def _conditionals(name: str, rng) -> tuple:
    bound = 3 + _SALT[0]
    prompt = f'def {name}(value):\n    """Return a label for the value."""\n'
    reference = (
        f'def {name}(value):\n'
        f'    """Return a label for the value."""\n'
        f"    if value > {bound}:\n"
        f'        return "high"\n'
        f"    if value < -{bound}:\n"
        f'        return "low"\n'
        f'    return "middle"\n'
    )
    return prompt, reference, "conditionals:label", {"bound": bound}


def _list_ops(name: str, rng) -> tuple:
    threshold = 1 + _SALT[0]
    prompt = f'def {name}(values):\n    """Return the values above a threshold."""\n'
    reference = (
        f'def {name}(values):\n'
        f'    """Return the values above a threshold."""\n'
        f"    return [value for value in values if value > {threshold}]\n"
    )
    return prompt, reference, "list_ops:filter", {"threshold": threshold}


def _string_ops(name: str, rng) -> tuple:
    letter = "abcdefghilmnoprstu"[_SALT[0] % len("abcdefghilmnoprstu")]
    salt = _SALT[0]
    prompt = f'def {name}(text):\n    """Work with a text value."""\n'
    reference = (
        f'def {name}(text):\n'
        f'    """Work with a text value."""\n'
        f'    reversed_text = text[::-1]\n'
        f'    return reversed_text.count("{letter}") + {salt}\n'
    )
    return prompt, reference, "string_ops:count", {"letter": letter}


def _dict_ops(name: str, rng) -> tuple:
    default = 1 + _SALT[0]
    prompt = f'def {name}(mapping, key):\n    """Return a mapping value or a default."""\n'
    reference = (
        f'def {name}(mapping, key):\n'
        f'    """Return a mapping value or a default."""\n'
        f"    return mapping.get(key, {default})\n"
    )
    return prompt, reference, "dict_ops:lookup", {"default": default}


def _loop_agg(name: str, rng) -> tuple:
    factor = 2 + (_SALT[0] % 5)
    salt = _SALT[0]
    prompt = f'def {name}(values):\n    """Accumulate values with a loop."""\n'
    reference = (
        f'def {name}(values):\n'
        f'    """Accumulate values with a loop."""\n'
        f"    total = 0\n"
        f"    for value in values:\n"
        f"        total += value * {factor} + {salt}\n"
        f"    return total\n"
    )
    return prompt, reference, "loop_agg:accumulate", {"factor": factor}


def _composed(name: str, rng) -> tuple:
    threshold = 2 + _SALT[0]
    prompt = (
        f'def {name}(values):\n'
        f'    """Keep the large values, then sum them."""\n'
    )
    reference = (
        f'def {name}(values):\n'
        f'    """Keep the large values, then sum them."""\n'
        f"    kept = [value for value in values if value > {threshold}]\n"
        f"    total = 0\n"
        f"    for value in kept:\n"
        f"        total += value\n"
        f"    return total\n"
    )
    return prompt, reference, "composed:filter_then_sum", {"threshold": threshold}


#: A per-case salt that keeps every generated sample textually distinct
#: while preserving the family structure. It is what makes "same
#: template, new parameters" the only difference between training and
#: partition A.
_SALT = [0]


GRAMMARS = {
    "arithmetic": _arithmetic,
    "conditionals": _conditionals,
    "list_ops": _list_ops,
    "string_ops": _string_ops,
    "dict_ops": _dict_ops,
    "loop_agg": _loop_agg,
    "composed": _composed,
}


def _make_case(case_id: str, family: str, partition: str, name: str, rng) -> Case:
    _SALT[0] += 1
    prompt, reference, template_id, params = GRAMMARS[family](name, rng)
    return Case(
        case_id=case_id,
        family=family,
        partition=partition,
        template_id=template_id,
        prompt=prompt,
        reference=reference,
        content_sha256=_hash(reference),
        params=params,
    )


def build_curriculum(seed: int = 20261021) -> dict:
    """Build the frozen curriculum: train plus partitions A, B and C."""
    import random

    # The salt counter is per build, so two builds of the same seed produce
    # byte-identical curricula.
    _SALT[0] = 0
    partitions: dict = {"train": [], "A": [], "B": [], "C": []}

    for index in range(120):
        family = TRAIN_FAMILIES[index % len(TRAIN_FAMILIES)]
        rng = random.Random(f"{seed}:train:{index}")
        name = TRAIN_NAMES[family][index % len(TRAIN_NAMES[family])]
        partitions["train"].append(
            _make_case(f"train-{family}-{index:03d}", family, "train", name, rng)
        )

    for index in range(40):
        family = TRAIN_FAMILIES[index % len(TRAIN_FAMILIES)]
        rng = random.Random(f"{seed}:A:{index}")
        names = UNSEEN_NAMES[family]
        name = names[index % len(names)]
        partitions["A"].append(
            _make_case(f"A-{family}-{index:03d}", family, "A", name, rng)
        )

    for index in range(30):
        rng = random.Random(f"{seed}:B:{index}")
        name = UNSEEN_NAMES["list_ops"][index % len(UNSEEN_NAMES["list_ops"])]
        partitions["B"].append(
            _make_case(f"B-composed-{index:03d}", "composed", "B", name, rng)
        )

    for index in range(40):
        family = HELDOUT_FAMILIES[index % len(HELDOUT_FAMILIES)]
        rng = random.Random(f"{seed}:C:{index}")
        names = HELDOUT_NAMES[family]
        name = names[index % len(names)]
        partitions["C"].append(
            _make_case(f"C-{family}-{index:03d}", family, "C", name, rng)
        )

    return partitions


def curriculum_digest(partitions: dict) -> str:
    """A single hash over the whole frozen curriculum."""
    payload = "\n".join(
        f"{case.partition}:{case.case_id}:{case.content_sha256}"
        for partition in sorted(partitions)
        for case in partitions[partition]
    )
    return _hash(payload)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Contamination controls
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def contamination_report(partitions: dict, *, similarity_threshold: float = 0.9) -> dict:
    """Measure cross-partition contamination.

    A *violation* is a real leak: an identical sample across partitions, an
    identical target solution, a withheld family appearing in training, or a
    near-duplicate structure above the similarity threshold for a partition
    that is supposed to differ structurally (B and C).

    Sharing a template between training and partition A is *by design* -- A
    measures the same families with new parameters and new names -- so it is
    reported as a note, not counted as a leak.
    """
    violations: list = []
    notes: list = []
    train_shingles = [_shingles(case.reference) for case in partitions["train"]]
    train_families = {case.family for case in partitions["train"]}
    structural_partitions = {"B", "C"}
    inherited_partitions = {"train", "A"}

    def spans(group: dict, left: set, right: set) -> bool:
        return bool(
            {p for p, ids in group.items() if ids} & left
        ) and bool({p for p, ids in group.items() if ids} & right)

    exact: dict = {}
    normalized: dict = {}
    for partition in sorted(partitions):
        for case in partitions[partition]:
            exact.setdefault(case.content_sha256, {}).setdefault(partition, []).append(
                case.case_id
            )
            normalized.setdefault(
                _normalized_hash(case.reference), {}
            ).setdefault(partition, []).append(case.case_id)

    for key, group in exact.items():
        if len(group) > 1:
            violations.append(
                f"identical sample across partitions {key[:12]}: {group}"
            )
    for key, group in normalized.items():
        if spans(group, inherited_partitions, structural_partitions):
            violations.append(
                f"parameter-erased duplicate across an inheriting and a "
                f"structural partition {key[:12]}: {group}"
            )
        elif len(group) > 1:
            notes.append(
                f"template-shared samples across {sorted(group)} (expected for "
                "the in-distribution partition)"
            )

    for case in partitions["C"]:
        if case.family in train_families:
            violations.append(
                f"{case.case_id}: withheld family {case.family} appears in training"
            )

    max_similarity = {"A": 0.0, "B": 0.0, "C": 0.0}
    for partition in ("A", "B", "C"):
        for case in partitions[partition]:
            shingles = _shingles(case.reference)
            best = 0.0
            for train_case, train_shingles_set in zip(
                partitions["train"], train_shingles
            ):
                best = max(best, _jaccard(shingles, train_shingles_set))
            max_similarity[partition] = max(max_similarity[partition], best)
            if partition in structural_partitions and best >= similarity_threshold:
                violations.append(
                    f"{case.case_id}: structural similarity {best:.2f} with a "
                    "training sample"
                )

    return {
        "schema": "quantsmind.synthetic_contamination/1",
        "violations": violations,
        "violation_count": len(violations),
        "notes": notes[:10],
        "contaminated": bool(violations),
        "verdict": (
            "SYNTHETIC_EVALUATION_CONTAMINATED" if violations else "CLEAN"
        ),
        "similarity_threshold": similarity_threshold,
        "max_train_similarity": {k: round(v, 4) for k, v in max_similarity.items()},
        "partition_sizes": {
            partition: len(cases) for partition, cases in sorted(partitions.items())
        },
    }
