<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\synthetic_eval.py
"""Evaluation protocol for the v1.9.0 synthetic curriculum.

The protocol is frozen: the same cases, the same prompts, the same token
budget, the same decoding settings and the same validators are used before
and after training. Nothing here executes generated code; every metric is
static.

Metrics
-------
``syntax_valid``          the assembled program parses
``complete_function``     the assembled program defines the requested function
``exact_target``          the assembled program matches the reference
``structural_similarity`` token-shingle similarity against the reference
``degenerate``            the completion collapses into repetition
``eos_terminated``        generation stopped on the end-of-document token
``truncated``             generation stopped on the budget
``tokens``                tokens generated
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import re
import time
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

from training.synthetic_curriculum import _jaccard, _shingles


def requested_function(prompt: str) -> str:
    match = re.search(r"def\s+([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*)", prompt)
    return match.group(1) if match else ""


def _defines_function(program: str, name: str) -> bool:
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(program)
    except (SyntaxError, ValueError):
        return False
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
            if node.name == name:
                return True
    return False


def _exact(program: str, reference: str) -> bool:
    def norm(text: str) -> str:
        text = re.sub(r"#.*", "", text)
        text = re.sub(r'""".*?"""', "", text, flags=re.DOTALL)
        return "\n".join(line.rstrip() for line in text.strip().splitlines() if line.strip())

    return norm(program) == norm(reference)


def evaluate_cases(model, tokenizer, cases, *, budget: int = 96,
                   temperature: float = 0.0, seed: int | None = None,
                   device: str = "cpu") -> dict:
    """Evaluate the frozen cases with one checkpoint."""
    from serving.local_inference import generate_ids

    records = []
    for case in cases:
        started = time.time()
        result = generate_ids(
            model,
            tokenizer,
            case.prompt,
            max_new_tokens=budget,
            temperature=temperature,
            seed=seed if temperature and temperature > 0 else None,
            device=device,
        )
        text = result.get("text", "")
        program = case.prompt + text
        name = requested_function(case.prompt)
        syntax_valid = False
        try:
            ast.parse(program)
            syntax_valid = True
        except (SyntaxError, ValueError):
            syntax_valid = False
        tokens = result.get("token_ids") or []
        shingles = _shingles(text)
        reference_shingles = _shingles(case.reference)
        records.append(
            {
                "case_id": case.case_id,
                "family": case.family,
                "partition": case.partition,
                "syntax_valid": syntax_valid,
                "complete_function": _defines_function(program, name) if name else False,
                "exact_target": _exact(program, case.reference),
                "structural_similarity": round(_jaccard(shingles, reference_shingles), 4),
                "degenerate": _is_degenerate(text, tokens),
                "eos_terminated": result.get("finish_reason") == "stop",
                "truncated": result.get("finish_reason") == "length",
                "tokens": len(tokens),
                "latency_seconds": round(time.time() - started, 3),
            }
        )
    return {"records": records, "aggregate": aggregate_records(records)}


def _is_degenerate(text: str, tokens) -> bool:
    if not tokens:
        return True
    longest = 1
    run = 1
    for previous, current in zip(tokens, tokens[1:]):
        run = run + 1 if current == previous else 1
        longest = max(longest, run)
    if longest >= 8:
        return True
    if len(text.strip().splitlines()) >= 2:
        lines = [line.strip() for line in text.splitlines() if line.strip()]
        if lines and len(set(lines)) / len(lines) < 0.5:
            return True
    return False


def aggregate_records(records) -> dict:
    """Aggregate case records into the reported metrics, with denominators."""
    total = len(records)
    if not total:
        return {"cases": 0}
    syntax = sum(1 for record in records if record["syntax_valid"])
    complete = sum(1 for record in records if record["complete_function"])
    exact = sum(1 for record in records if record["exact_target"])
    degenerate = sum(1 for record in records if record["degenerate"])
    eos = sum(1 for record in records if record["eos_terminated"])
    truncated = sum(1 for record in records if record["truncated"])
    similarity = [record["structural_similarity"] for record in records]
    per_family = defaultdict(lambda: {"total": 0, "syntax_valid": 0, "complete_function": 0})
    for record in records:
        entry = per_family[record["family"]]
        entry["total"] += 1
        entry["syntax_valid"] += int(record["syntax_valid"])
        entry["complete_function"] += int(record["complete_function"])
    return {
        "cases": total,
        "syntax_valid": syntax,
        "syntax_valid_rate": syntax / total,
        "complete_function": complete,
        "complete_function_rate": complete / total,
        "exact_target": exact,
        "exact_target_rate": exact / total,
        "degenerate": degenerate,
        "degenerate_rate": degenerate / total,
        "eos_terminated": eos,
        "truncated": truncated,
        "mean_structural_similarity": round(sum(similarity) / total, 4),
        "mean_tokens": round(
            sum(record["tokens"] for record in records) / total, 2
        ),
        "per_family": {name: dict(counts) for name, counts in sorted(per_family.items())},
    }


#: The outcome vocabulary of the experiment. Only measured evidence selects
#: one of these; a lower training loss never does.
CLASSIFICATIONS = (
    "SYNTHETIC_GENERALIZATION_DEMONSTRATED",
    "SYNTHETIC_PATTERN_LEARNING_ONLY",
    "LOSS_REDUCTION_WITHOUT_CODING_GAIN",
    "NO_MEASURABLE_LEARNING",
    "EXPERIMENT_BLOCKED",
)


def classify(baseline: dict, trained: dict, *, loss_delta: float | None = None) -> dict:
    """Classify the experiment from measured evidence only.

    Syntax validity alone is not a learning signal: a model can emit a
    parseable, function-shaped but degenerate completion. Generalisation is
    therefore only claimed when the held-out syntax rate improves *and* the
    degenerate rate falls *and* the outputs move toward the targets (exact
    agreement or structural similarity). Otherwise the run is reported as
    pattern learning, which is what it is.
    """

    def rate(block, key, partition):
        return block.get(partition, {}).get(key, 0.0)

    def mean(block, key):
        values = [
            block.get(partition, {}).get(key, 0.0)
            for partition in ("A", "B", "C")
            if block.get(partition)
        ]
        return sum(values) / len(values) if values else 0.0

    held_out_gain = 0.0
    for partition in ("B", "C"):
        held_out_gain += rate(trained, "syntax_valid_rate", partition) - rate(
            baseline, "syntax_valid_rate", partition
        )
    in_distribution_gain = rate(
        trained, "syntax_valid_rate", "A"
    ) - rate(baseline, "syntax_valid_rate", "A")
    degenerate_change = rate(trained, "degenerate_rate", "A") - rate(
        baseline, "degenerate_rate", "A"
    )
    exact_gain = mean(trained, "exact_target_rate") - mean(baseline, "exact_target_rate")
    similarity_gain = mean(
        trained, "mean_structural_similarity"
    ) - mean(baseline, "mean_structural_similarity")
    loss_fell = bool(loss_delta is not None and loss_delta < 0)

    if (
        held_out_gain > 0
        and degenerate_change < 0
        and (exact_gain > 0 or similarity_gain > 0.05)
    ):
        verdict = "SYNTHETIC_GENERALIZATION_DEMONSTRATED"
        reason = (
            f"held-out syntax validity improved ({held_out_gain:+.3f}), the "
            f"degenerate rate fell ({degenerate_change:+.3f}) and the outputs "
            f"moved toward the targets (exact {exact_gain:+.3f}, structural "
            f"{similarity_gain:+.3f})"
        )
    elif in_distribution_gain > 0 or held_out_gain > 0:
        verdict = "SYNTHETIC_PATTERN_LEARNING_ONLY"
        reason = (
            f"completion shape improved (in-distribution "
            f"{in_distribution_gain:+.3f}, held-out {held_out_gain:+.3f}) but the "
            f"output did not become semantically correct (exact {exact_gain:+.3f}, "
            f"structural {similarity_gain:+.3f})"
            + (
                f" and degeneracy rose ({degenerate_change:+.3f})"
                if degenerate_change >= 0
                else ""
            )
        )
    elif loss_fell:
        verdict = "LOSS_REDUCTION_WITHOUT_CODING_GAIN"
        reason = "training loss fell but no completion-quality metric improved"
    else:
        verdict = "NO_MEASURABLE_LEARNING"
        reason = "neither loss nor completion quality improved measurably"

    return {
        "verdict": verdict,
        "reason": reason,
        "in_distribution_gain": round(in_distribution_gain, 4),
        "held_out_gain": round(held_out_gain, 4),
        "degenerate_change": round(degenerate_change, 4),
        "exact_target_gain": round(exact_gain, 4),
        "structural_similarity_gain": round(similarity_gain, 4),
        "loss_delta": loss_delta,
        "note": (
            "This classification describes behaviour on a synthetic "
            "curriculum. It is not a claim about Python programming ability, "
            "and the experimental checkpoint is not promoted."
        ),
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# v2.0.0: task-conditioning metrics
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _body_of(program: str) -> str:
    """A normalised representation of the generated function body."""
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(program)
    except (SyntaxError, ValueError):
        return "<unparsable>"
    funcs = [n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef)]
    if not funcs:
        return "<no-function>"
    return ast.dump(funcs[-1], annotate_fields=False)


def evaluate_cases_v2(model, tokenizer, cases, *, budget: int = 64,
                      temperature: float = 0.0, seed: int | None = None,
                      device: str = "cpu") -> dict:
    """Evaluate cases with the v2.0 metrics (task conditioning included)."""
    from serving.local_inference import generate_ids
    from training.contrastive_tasks import OPERATION_MARKERS

    if isinstance(cases, dict):
        case_list = []
        for partition in sorted(cases):
            case_list.extend(cases[partition])
    else:
        case_list = list(cases)

    records = []
    for case in case_list:
        result = generate_ids(
            model, tokenizer, case.prompt, max_new_tokens=budget,
            temperature=temperature, seed=seed if temperature and temperature > 0 else None,
            device=device,
        )
        text = result.get("text", "")
        program = case.prompt + text
        body = _body_of(program)
        body_key = _body_key(program)
        operation = (case.params or {}).get("operation")
        markers = OPERATION_MARKERS.get(operation, [])
        records.append({
            "case_id": case.case_id,
            "family": case.family,
            "partition": case.partition,
            "pair_id": (case.params or {}).get("pair_id"),
            "operation": operation,
            "body": body,
            "body_key": body_key,
            "syntax_valid": body != "<unparsable>",
            "complete_function": body not in ("<unparsable>", "<no-function>"),
            "exact_target": _exact(program, case.reference),
            "operation_agreement": bool(markers) and any(
                marker in program for marker in markers
            ),
            "degenerate": _is_degenerate(text, result.get("token_ids") or []),
            "eos_terminated": result.get("finish_reason") == "stop",
            "truncated": result.get("finish_reason") == "length",
            "tokens": len(result.get("token_ids") or []),
            "text": text,
        })
    return {"records": records, "metrics": task_conditioning_metrics(records)}


def _body_key(program: str) -> str:
    """A body comparison key that ignores literal numbers.

    Numbers are per-case salts, so a digit-stable key measures whether the
    *computation* changed rather than whether the text differs.
    """
    import re

    return re.sub(r"\d+", "N", _body_of(program))


def task_conditioning_metrics(records) -> dict:
    """Metrics that distinguish task-conditioned output from a fixed template."""
    total = len(records)
    if not total:
        return {"cases": 0}
    bodies = [record.get("body_key") or record["body"] for record in records]
    modal = max(set(bodies), key=bodies.count)
    unique_bodies = len(set(bodies))
    unique_texts = len({record["text"] for record in records})
    sensitive = sum(1 for body in bodies if body != modal)
    pairs = {}
    for record in records:
        if record.get("pair_id"):
            pairs.setdefault(record["pair_id"], []).append(record)
    differentiated = 0
    comparable = 0
    for members in pairs.values():
        if len(members) < 2:
            continue
        comparable += 1
        if len({member["body"] for member in members}) > 1:
            differentiated += 1
    return {
        "cases": total,
        "syntax_valid": sum(1 for r in records if r["syntax_valid"]),
        "complete_function": sum(1 for r in records if r["complete_function"]),
        "exact_target": sum(1 for r in records if r["exact_target"]),
        "degenerate": sum(1 for r in records if r["degenerate"]),
        "operation_agreement": sum(1 for r in records if r["operation_agreement"]),
        "unique_completion_ratio": unique_texts / total,
        "unique_body_ratio": unique_bodies / total,
        "prompt_sensitivity": sensitive / total,
        "contrastive_pairs": comparable,
        "contrastive_differentiated": differentiated,
        "contrastive_differentiation_rate": (
            differentiated / comparable if comparable else None
        ),
        "eos_terminated": sum(1 for r in records if r["eos_terminated"]),
        "truncated": sum(1 for r in records if r["truncated"]),
        "mean_tokens": round(sum(r["tokens"] for r in records) / total, 2),
    }


#: Task-conditioning classifications (v2.0.0).
TASK_CONDITIONING_CLASSES = (
    "TASK_CONDITIONED_LEARNING_DEMONSTRATED",
    "SURFACE_CONDITIONED_LEARNING",
    "GENERIC_TEMPLATE_COLLAPSE",
    "LOSS_REDUCTION_WITHOUT_TASK_LEARNING",
    "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE",
)


def classify_task_conditioning(metrics: dict, *, loss_delta=None) -> dict:
    """Classify task conditioning from measured evidence only.

    A model that emits one body for every prompt is a template collapse, no
    matter how well it parses. A model that changes the requested operation
    but is never verified for correctness is reported as task-conditioned
    *with the correctness caveat attached*, because static operator agreement
    is not functional proof.
    """
    if not metrics or not metrics.get("cases"):
        return {"verdict": "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE", "reason": "no cases evaluated"}
    body_ratio = metrics.get("unique_body_ratio", 0.0)
    sensitivity = metrics.get("prompt_sensitivity", 0.0)
    operation = metrics.get("operation_agreement", 0) / metrics["cases"]
    differentiation = metrics.get("contrastive_differentiation_rate")
    loss_fell = bool(loss_delta is not None and loss_delta < 0)

    if body_ratio <= 0.25 or sensitivity <= 0.25:
        verdict = "GENERIC_TEMPLATE_COLLAPSE"
        reason = (
            f"only {body_ratio:.2f} of the completions have a distinct body and "
            f"prompt sensitivity is {sensitivity:.2f}: the output does not depend "
            "on the requested operation"
        )
    elif differentiation is not None and differentiation >= 0.8 and operation >= 0.8:
        verdict = "TASK_CONDITIONED_LEARNING_DEMONSTRATED"
        reason = (
            f"{differentiation:.2f} of the matched contrastive pairs produced "
            f"different bodies and {operation:.2f} of the completions contain the "
            "requested operation"
        )
    elif operation >= 0.4:
        verdict = "SURFACE_CONDITIONED_LEARNING"
        reason = (
            f"the requested operation appears in {operation:.2f} of the "
            "completions, but the matched pairs are not reliably differentiated"
        )
    elif sensitivity > 0.25:
        verdict = "SURFACE_CONDITIONED_LEARNING"
        reason = (
            f"the output varies with the prompt (sensitivity {sensitivity:.2f}) "
            f"but only {operation:.2f} of the completions contain the requested "
            "operation: the response is prompt-dependent without being "
            "task-correct"
        )
    elif loss_fell:
        verdict = "LOSS_REDUCTION_WITHOUT_TASK_LEARNING"
        reason = "training loss fell without measurable task differentiation"
    else:
        verdict = "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE"
        reason = "the evidence does not separate collapse from task conditioning"
    return {
        "verdict": verdict,
        "reason": reason,
        "loss_delta": loss_delta,
        "caveat": (
            "Static operator agreement is not functional correctness: no "
            "generated program was executed, because no verified isolation "
            "mechanism exists on this host."
        ),
    }

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\synthetic_train.py
"""Bounded synthetic training cells with stability instrumentation (v2.0.0).

A cell trains the S2 model on the *contrastive* synthetic curriculum and
records, per optimizer step: the loss, the gradient norm before clipping, the
parameter-update magnitude, and the ratio of the update to the parameter norm.
Artifacts are written through :mod:`training.experiment_artifacts`, so a run
directory can never be reused or overwritten.

This is a diagnostic harness. It trains only on locally generated synthetic
Python, it never touches the production corpus registry, and it never promotes
a checkpoint.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import time

import torch

from training.determinism import set_determinism
from training.objective import accumulation_weights, token_mean_loss
from training.schedules import WarmupCosineSchedule
from training.sequence import SequenceBuilder


def build_corpus(partitions: dict, split: str = "train") -> list:
    """Training records for a partition: the reference solution of each case."""
    return [
        {
            "text": case.reference,
            "case_id": case.case_id,
            "family": case.family,
            "operation": (case.params or {}).get("operation"),
        }
        for case in partitions[split]
    ]


def _windows(builder: SequenceBuilder, records: list) -> list:
    return builder.build_windows(
        [(r["case_id"], r["case_id"], r["text"]) for r in records]
    )


def train_cell(
    *,
    model_config: dict,
    tokenizer,
    train_records: list,
    val_records: list,
    lr: float,
    steps: int,
    context_length: int,
    grad_accum: int = 2,
    seed: int = 20261021,
    warmup: int = 2,
    weight_decay: float = 0.1,
    grad_clip: float = 1.0,
    init_checkpoint: str | None = None,
    artifacts=None,
    device: str = "cpu",
) -> dict:
    """Run one training cell and return its metrics."""
    from training.model import QMModel

    set_determinism(seed)
    model = QMModel(model_config).to(device)
    if init_checkpoint:
        from serving.local_inference import torch_load_checkpoint

        model.load_state_dict(torch_load_checkpoint(init_checkpoint)["model"])

    builder = SequenceBuilder(
        tokenizer,
        context_length=context_length,
        model_vocab=model_config["vocab_size"],
        policy="document",
        append_eos=True,
    )
    train_windows = _windows(builder, train_records)
    val_windows = _windows(builder, val_records)
    if not train_windows:
        raise ValueError("the training partition produced no windows")

    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        model.parameters(), lr=lr, betas=(0.9, 0.95), weight_decay=weight_decay
    )
    schedule = WarmupCosineSchedule(
        peak_lr=lr, warmup_steps=warmup, total_steps=steps, min_ratio=0.1
    )
    generator = torch.Generator()
    generator.manual_seed(seed)
    order = torch.randperm(len(train_windows), generator=generator).tolist()

    history = []
    consumed_tokens = 0
    started = time.time()
    for step in range(steps):
        batches = []
        for micro in range(grad_accum):
            index = order[(step * grad_accum + micro) % len(order)]
            batches.append(builder.to_batch([train_windows[index]]))
        counts = [batch.supervised_tokens for batch in batches]
        weights = accumulation_weights(counts)
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        window_loss = 0.0
        for batch, weight in zip(batches, weights):
            logits, _ = model(batch.input_ids.to(device))
            summed, supervised = token_mean_loss(logits, batch.labels.to(device))
            if supervised == 0:
                continue
            micro_mean = summed / supervised
            (micro_mean * weight).backward()
            window_loss += float(micro_mean.item()) * weight
        grad_norm = float(
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(
                model.parameters(), grad_clip, error_if_nonfinite=False
            )
        )
        param_norm = float(
            torch.sqrt(sum((p.detach() ** 2).sum() for p in model.parameters()))
        )
        before = [p.detach().clone() for p in model.parameters()]
        learning_rate = schedule.lr_at(step)
        for group in optimizer.param_groups:
            group["lr"] = learning_rate
        optimizer.step()
        delta = float(
            torch.sqrt(
                sum(
                    ((p.detach() - b) ** 2).sum()
                    for p, b in zip(model.parameters(), before)
                )
            )
        )
        consumed_tokens += sum(counts)
        history.append(
            {
                "step": step + 1,
                "loss": window_loss,
                "lr": learning_rate,
                "grad_norm_before_clip": grad_norm,
                "param_norm": param_norm,
                "update_norm": delta,
                "update_to_param_ratio": (delta / param_norm) if param_norm else None,
                "supervised_tokens": sum(counts),
                "finite_loss": math.isfinite(window_loss),
            }
        )
        if not math.isfinite(window_loss):
            break

    elapsed = time.time() - started
    val_loss = _validate(model, builder, val_windows, device)
    result = {
        "lr": lr,
        "steps": len(history),
        "requested_steps": steps,
        "tokens_consumed": consumed_tokens,
        "initial_loss": history[0]["loss"] if history else None,
        "final_loss": history[-1]["loss"] if history else None,
        "validation_loss": val_loss,
        "elapsed_seconds": round(elapsed, 2),
        "history": history,
        "train_windows": len(train_windows),
        "val_windows": len(val_windows),
        "init_checkpoint": init_checkpoint,
        "seed": seed,
        "context_length": context_length,
        "grad_accum": grad_accum,
    }
    if artifacts is not None:
        artifacts.write_metric("training.json", result)
    return result, model


def _validate(model, builder, windows, device) -> float | None:
    """Mean token loss over the validation windows (no gradient)."""
    if not windows:
        return None
    total = 0.0
    count = 0
    model.eval()
    with torch.no_grad():
        for window in windows:
            batch = builder.to_batch([window])
            logits, _ = model(batch.input_ids.to(device))
            summed, supervised = token_mean_loss(logits, batch.labels.to(device))
            total += float(summed.item())
            count += supervised
    model.train()
    return (total / count) if count else None


def save_model_checkpoint(model, path) -> None:
    """Write a model state dict for later evaluation."""
    torch.save({"model": model.state_dict()}, path)

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\targeted_curriculum.py
"""Targeted generalization curriculum (Taksh v1.2.0 Increment 7).

Addresses the Increment 6 failure evidence: both checkpoints scored 0/48
on novel-identifier variants of the eight functional behaviours because
training names were fixed pools (`text`, `left`, `right`, `values`,
`items`, ...). This module reuses the Increment 4 behaviours and surface
variants but with:

* **novel identifier pools** — 48 generated names per arity, disjoint from
  every Increment 2/4 pool and from the fixed names above;
* **wider prompt variation** — six paraphrases per behaviour, split so
  training and validation wording sets are disjoint;
* **semantic separation** — validation uses a disjoint identifier half and
  a disjoint paraphrase half (not a shuffle of training examples);
* **retention** — the Increment 2 binding curriculum (arithmetic,
  maximum/minimum, binding probes) is composed alongside this module at
  the experiment level, so AD-1-style operations keep coverage.

All examples are original synthetic data. Every example carries verifiable
input/output metadata and must pass the safe functional gate.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib

from training.binding_curriculum import _validate
from training.functional_curriculum import (
    OPERATIONS,
    _FAMILIES,
    _INSTRUCTIONS,
    _RELATIONSHIPS,
    _SAMPLES,
    _body,
)
from training.supervised import build_example

_STEMS = (
    "probe", "node", "case", "entry", "vertex", "segment",
    "unit", "slot", "cell", "point", "vertex", "node",
)

# Two extra paraphrases per behaviour (six total with the Increment 4 set).
_EXTRA_INSTRUCTIONS = {
    "scale_value": ("Multiply these two quantities and report the product.", "Return value times factor."),
    "join_text": ("Combine the strings with one space between them.", "Return the joined pair of words."),
    "add_then_multiply": ("Double the combined total of the pair.", "Add first, then double the sum."),
    "multiply_then_add": ("Increase the product by two.", "Take the product and add two to it."),
    "filter_and_count": ("How many items sit above zero?", "Give the count of positive entries."),
    "keep_long_words": ("Keep entries whose length exceeds three.", "Return words longer than three characters."),
    "is_even": ("Determine whether the integer is even.", "Even parity check, please."),
    "sum_positive": ("What is the total of the positive entries?", "Add only the values above zero."),
}

_BINARY_OPERATIONS = ("scale_value", "join_text", "add_then_multiply", "multiply_then_add")
_SINGLE_OPERATIONS = ("filter_and_count", "keep_long_words", "is_even", "sum_positive")


def novel_pairs(count: int = 48) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """48 unique novel parameter-name pairs, disjoint from all prior pools."""
    pairs = []
    for index in range(count):
        first = f"{_STEMS[index % len(_STEMS)]}_{index:02d}"
        second = f"{_STEMS[(index + 5) % len(_STEMS)]}_{index:02d}"
        pairs.append((first, second))
    return pairs


def novel_singles(count: int = 48) -> list[str]:
    return [f"{_STEMS[index % len(_STEMS)]}_{index:02d}" for index in range(count)]


def build_examples(
    *,
    per_operation: int = 16,
    seed: int = 20261108,
    split: str = "train",
    id_prefix: str = "T1",
) -> list:
    is_train = split == "train"
    # Semantic separation: train uses identifier half 0 (indices 0..23) and
    # paraphrases 0..3; validation uses half 1 (24..47) and paraphrases 4..5.
    pair_pool = novel_pairs(48)
    single_pool = novel_singles(48)
    name_start = 0 if is_train else 24
    examples = []
    for operation in OPERATIONS:
        instructions = list(_INSTRUCTIONS[operation]) + list(_EXTRA_INSTRUCTIONS[operation])
        active_instructions = instructions[0:4] if is_train else instructions[4:6]
        samples = _SAMPLES[operation]
        for index in range(per_operation):
            pool_index = name_start + index
            if operation in _BINARY_OPERATIONS:
                params = pair_pool[pool_index]
            else:
                params = (single_pool[pool_index],)
            function_name = f"op_{operation}_{index:02d}"
            instruction = active_instructions[index % len(active_instructions)]
            variant = index % 4
            signature = f"def {function_name}({', '.join(params)}):"
            body = _body(operation, params, variant)
            _validate(signature, body)
            sample_index = index % len(samples) if is_train else (index + 2) % len(samples)
            args, expected = samples[sample_index]
            example_id = f"{id_prefix}-{operation}-{index:03d}"
            examples.append(
                build_example(
                    example_id=example_id,
                    instruction=instruction,
                    signature=signature,
                    body=body,
                    operation=operation,
                    family=_FAMILIES[operation],
                    split=split,
                    seed=seed + index,
                    metadata={
                        "markers": [operation],
                        "functional_focus": True,
                        "targeted": True,
                        "variant": variant,
                        "surface_variant": f"v{variant}",
                        "inputs": [list(args)],
                        "expected_outputs": [expected],
                        "relationship": _RELATIONSHIPS[operation],
                    },
                )
            )
    return examples


def build_training_examples(*, seed: int = 20261108) -> list:
    return build_examples(per_operation=16, seed=seed, split="train")


def build_validation_examples(*, seed: int = 20261109) -> list:
    return build_examples(per_operation=4, seed=seed, split="validation", id_prefix="T1V")


def targeted_digest() -> str:
    payload = [
        (example.example_id, example.instruction, example.signature, example.body, example.operation)
        for example in build_training_examples()
    ]
    return hashlib.sha256(repr(payload).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()

<|file|> F:\Codes\Git\Quantsmind-LLM\training\tokenizer_analysis.py
"""Measured Python suitability analysis for the Taksh tokenizer (v1.2.0).

The question this module answers is narrow and answerable: *how does the
tokenizer in this repository actually behave on Python source?* It measures,
on a bounded sample:

* fertility (tokens per source character, per lexical token, per byte),
* identifier fragmentation (how many identifiers cost more than one token),
* keyword and operator representation,
* indentation, newline and string-literal handling,
* Unicode handling and unknown-token incidence,
* encode/decode round-trip correctness,
* context-window efficiency (bytes of source covered by one 4096-token window).

The comparison baseline is documented rather than downloaded: a byte-level
fallback costs one token per UTF-8 byte, so *bytes per token* is the
compression factor against that baseline. The v1.1.0 control-token
derivation is measured separately to show whether the reserved control range
changed fertility (it must not, because no merge is retrained).

The decision rules are engineering defaults with stated thresholds. They are
**not** claimed to be empirically optimal: no sweep was run, and the report
says so. The measured values are the evidence; the thresholds are the policy.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import io
import json
import keyword
import tokenize
from pathlib import Path

from training.tokenizer_contract import CONTRACT_V1, CONTRACT_V2, build_contract_tokenizer

#: Conservative engineering defaults. Documented, not optimised.
ACCEPTED_MIN_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 3.0
MIGRATION_MAX_IDENTIFIER_FRAGMENTATION = 0.50
MIGRATION_MIN_CHARS_PER_TOKEN = 2.5
INSUFFICIENT_MIN_SAMPLES = 20
INSUFFICIENT_MIN_BYTES = 20_000

COMMON_OPERATORS = (
    "+ - * / % // ** == != < > <= >= = += -= *= /= //= **= & | ^ ~ << >> >>="
    " and or not in is if else elif for while return import from as pass "
    "break continue class def try except finally with lambda yield global "
    "nonlocal assert del global raise async await"
).split()

#: Reserved spellings: the v1.0.0 specials and the v1.1.0 control range. A
#: literal of one of these in ordinary text is encoded as the reserved id.
RESERVED_LITERALS = (
    "<bos>",
    "<eos>",
    "<unk>",
    "<pad>",
    "<|system|>",
    "<|user|>",
    "<|assistant|>",
    "<|end_of_turn|>",
    "<|tool|>",
    "<|fim|>",
)


def _lexical_tokens(text: str) -> list:
    """Significant Python tokens (names, numbers, strings, operators)."""
    tokens = []
    try:
        for token in tokenize.generate_tokens(io.StringIO(text).readline):
            if token.type in (
                tokenize.NAME,
                tokenize.NUMBER,
                tokenize.STRING,
                tokenize.OP,
            ):
                tokens.append(token)
    except (tokenize.TokenError, IndentationError, SyntaxError, ValueError):
        return []
    return tokens


def analyse_texts(tokenizer, texts, *, source_label: str = "sample") -> dict:
    """Measure the tokenizer over a list of Python sources."""
    total_chars = 0
    total_bytes = 0
    total_tokens = 0
    total_lexical = 0
    identifiers = 0
    identifiers_split = 0
    identifier_tokens = 0
    string_chars = 0
    string_tokens = 0
    newline_tokens = 0
    newlines = 0
    indent_tokens = 0
    indented_lines = 0
    unicode_chars = 0
    unicode_tokens = 0
    unknown_hits = 0
    lossless_failures = 0
    policy_failures = 0
    reserved_files = 0
    reserved_occurrences = 0
    roundtrip_checked = 0

    reserved = RESERVED_LITERALS
    unk_id = None
    try:
        unk_id = tokenizer.token_to_id("<unk>")
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - optional token
        unk_id = None

    for text in texts:
        total_chars += len(text)
        total_bytes += len(text.encode("utf-8"))
        encoding = tokenizer.encode(text)
        total_tokens += len(encoding.ids)
        if unk_id is not None:
            unknown_hits += sum(1 for i in encoding.ids if i == unk_id)
        roundtrip_checked += 1
        # Two decodes are measured on purpose:
        #   * lossless -- special-token skipping disabled. This is the
        #     artifact's own fidelity: can the tokenizer represent this text?
        #   * policy   -- the library default, which skips special tokens.
        #     A difference here means a reserved spelling was dropped, not
        #     that the artifact lost information.
        if tokenizer.decode(encoding.ids, skip_special_tokens=False) != text:
            lossless_failures += 1
        if tokenizer.decode(encoding.ids) != text:
            policy_failures += 1
        hits = sum(text.count(literal) for literal in reserved)
        if hits:
            reserved_files += 1
            reserved_occurrences += hits

        for token in _lexical_tokens(text):
            total_lexical += 1
            piece = token.string
            cost = len(tokenizer.encode(piece, add_special_tokens=False).ids)
            if token.type == tokenize.NAME:
                identifiers += 1
                identifier_tokens += cost
                if cost > 1:
                    identifiers_split += 1
            elif token.type == tokenize.STRING:
                string_chars += len(piece)
                string_tokens += cost
            elif token.type == tokenize.OP:
                total_lexical += 0
        newlines += text.count("\n")
        newline_tokens += len(
            tokenizer.encode("\n", add_special_tokens=False).ids
        )
        for line in text.splitlines():
            if line[:1] in (" ", "\t") and line.strip():
                indented_lines += 1
                indent_tokens += len(
                    tokenizer.encode(line[: len(line) - len(line.lstrip())], add_special_tokens=False).ids
                )
        unicode_chars += sum(1 for ch in text if ord(ch) > 127)
        unicode_tokens += len(
            tokenizer.encode(
                "".join(ch for ch in text if ord(ch) > 127) or " ", add_special_tokens=False
            ).ids
        )

    keyword_costs = {
        word: len(tokenizer.encode(word, add_special_tokens=False).ids)
        for word in sorted(keyword.kwlist)
    }
    operator_costs = {
        op: len(tokenizer.encode(op, add_special_tokens=False).ids)
        for op in COMMON_OPERATORS
    }

    def ratio(numerator, denominator):
        return (numerator / denominator) if denominator else 0.0

    return {
        "source_label": source_label,
        "samples": len(texts),
        "characters": total_chars,
        "bytes": total_bytes,
        "tokens": total_tokens,
        "tokens_per_character": ratio(total_tokens, total_chars),
        "characters_per_token": ratio(total_chars, total_tokens),
        "bytes_per_token": ratio(total_bytes, total_tokens),
        "tokens_per_lexical_token": ratio(total_tokens, total_lexical),
        "identifiers": identifiers,
        "identifier_fragmentation": ratio(identifiers_split, identifiers),
        "mean_tokens_per_identifier": ratio(identifier_tokens, identifiers),
        "keywords_single_token": ratio(
            sum(1 for c in keyword_costs.values() if c == 1), len(keyword_costs)
        ),
        "operators_single_token": ratio(
            sum(1 for c in operator_costs.values() if c == 1), len(operator_costs)
        ),
        "string_tokens_per_character": ratio(string_tokens, string_chars),
        "newline_tokens": ratio(newline_tokens, newlines),
        "indent_tokens_per_indented_line": ratio(indent_tokens, indented_lines),
        "unicode_characters": unicode_chars,
        "unicode_tokens_per_character": ratio(unicode_tokens, unicode_chars),
        "unknown_token_rate": ratio(unknown_hits, total_tokens),
        "roundtrip_checked": roundtrip_checked,
        "lossless_roundtrip_failures": lossless_failures,
        "lossless_round_trip_failure_rate": ratio(lossless_failures, roundtrip_checked),
        "policy_roundtrip_failures": policy_failures,
        "policy_round_trip_failure_rate": ratio(policy_failures, roundtrip_checked),
        "reserved_literal_files": reserved_files,
        "reserved_literal_occurrences": reserved_occurrences,
        "bytes_per_4096_token_window": ratio(total_bytes * 4096, total_tokens),
    }


def collect_python_sources(root, *, max_files: int = 200, max_bytes: int = 2_000_000) -> list:
    """Collect a bounded sample of Python source files from a local tree."""
    from data.python_v1.ingest import ingest_source, read_source

    report = ingest_source(
        {"id": "sample"},
        root,
        limits={"max_files": max_files, "max_total_bytes": max_bytes,
                "max_file_bytes": max_bytes, "max_path_depth": 40},
        excluded_paths=[],
        allowed_extensions=(".py",),
    )
    texts = []
    for ref in report.files:
        try:
            text, _encoding, _fallback = read_source(ref, max_bytes=max_bytes)
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - undecodable files are simply skipped
            continue
        texts.append(text)
    return texts


def collect_jsonl_texts(path, *, field: str = "text", max_samples: int = 500,
                         max_bytes: int = 2_000_000) -> list:
    """Collect text fields from a JSONL corpus, bounded."""
    texts = []
    total = 0
    with Path(path).open("r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for line in handle:
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            try:
                row = json.loads(line)
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                continue
            text = row.get(field)
            if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
                continue
            texts.append(text)
            total += len(text)
            if len(texts) >= max_samples or total >= max_bytes:
                break
    return texts


def decide(metrics: dict) -> tuple[str, list]:
    """Turn measurements into a decision with stated reasons.

    The artifact verdict is driven by the **lossless** round-trip rate: with
    special-token skipping disabled, a failure means the tokenizer really
    cannot represent the file, which is a migration-level defect.

    The policy rate (the library default, which skips special tokens) is
    reported separately. It is not an artifact defect: it means the text
    contains a reserved spelling, which becomes a reserved id in the token
    stream. That is a corpus-side risk, handled by excluding such samples
    from the training data, and it is not fixed by a larger vocabulary.
    """
    reasons = []
    samples = metrics.get("samples", 0)
    total_bytes = metrics.get("bytes", 0)
    if samples < INSUFFICIENT_MIN_SAMPLES or total_bytes < INSUFFICIENT_MIN_BYTES:
        reasons.append(
            f"insufficient evidence: {samples} samples / {total_bytes} bytes "
            f"(need {INSUFFICIENT_MIN_SAMPLES} samples / {INSUFFICIENT_MIN_BYTES} bytes)"
        )
        return "INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE", reasons

    fragmentation = metrics.get("identifier_fragmentation", 0.0)
    chars_per_token = metrics.get("characters_per_token", 0.0)
    lossless_rate = metrics.get("lossless_round_trip_failure_rate", 0.0)
    policy_rate = metrics.get("policy_round_trip_failure_rate", 0.0)
    migration = []

    if lossless_rate > 0.01:
        migration.append(
            f"lossless round-trip failure rate {lossless_rate:.3f} exceeds 0.01: "
            "the tokenizer cannot reproduce the measured files even with "
            "special-token skipping disabled"
        )
    elif lossless_rate > 0:
        reasons.append(
            f"lossless round-trip failure rate {lossless_rate:.3f} is non-zero: "
            "a small class of files cannot be reproduced losslessly"
        )
    if policy_rate > 0.01:
        reasons.append(
            f"policy round-trip failure rate {policy_rate:.3f}: the sample "
            "contains reserved token spellings, which are encoded as reserved "
            "ids. This is a corpus-side injection risk handled by excluding "
            "such samples, not an artifact defect"
        )
    if fragmentation > MIGRATION_MAX_IDENTIFIER_FRAGMENTATION:
        migration.append(
            f"identifier fragmentation {fragmentation:.2f} exceeds the migration "
            f"threshold {MIGRATION_MAX_IDENTIFIER_FRAGMENTATION:.2f}"
        )
    if chars_per_token < MIGRATION_MIN_CHARS_PER_TOKEN:
        migration.append(
            f"characters per token {chars_per_token:.2f} is below the migration "
            f"threshold {MIGRATION_MIN_CHARS_PER_TOKEN:.2f}"
        )
    if migration:
        reasons.extend(migration)
        reasons.append(
            "the reserved control range is not the cause: no merge was retrained"
        )
        return "TOKENIZER_MIGRATION_RECOMMENDED", reasons

    if chars_per_token < ACCEPTED_MIN_CHARS_PER_TOKEN:
        reasons.append(
            f"characters per token {chars_per_token:.2f} is below the acceptance "
            f"threshold {ACCEPTED_MIN_CHARS_PER_TOKEN:.2f}"
        )
        reasons.append(
            "identifier fragmentation is within bounds, so the corpus is usable "
            "but the vocabulary is small for a Python-first corpus"
        )
        return "TOKENIZER_ACCEPTED_WITH_LIMITATIONS", reasons

    reasons.append(
        f"characters per token {chars_per_token:.2f} meets the acceptance "
        f"threshold {ACCEPTED_MIN_CHARS_PER_TOKEN:.2f}"
    )
    reasons.append(
        f"identifier fragmentation {fragmentation:.2f} is within the migration "
        f"threshold {MIGRATION_MAX_IDENTIFIER_FRAGMENTATION:.2f}"
    )
    reasons.append("lossless round-trip is exact on the measured sample")
    return "TOKENIZER_ACCEPTED", reasons


def classify_roundtrip_failures(tokenizer, texts) -> dict:
    """Separate artifact-level loss from special-token decoding policy.

    A failure under the library default (``skip_special_tokens=True``) that
    disappears when special-token skipping is disabled is a *policy* effect:
    the reserved spelling was decoded away, not lost by the tokenizer. A
    failure that survives with skipping disabled is genuine artifact loss.
    """
    literals = RESERVED_LITERALS
    policy_failures = 0
    lossless_failures = 0
    special_token_drop = 0
    for text in texts:
        ids = tokenizer.encode(text).ids
        policy_ok = tokenizer.decode(ids) == text
        lossless_ok = tokenizer.decode(ids, skip_special_tokens=False) == text
        if not policy_ok:
            policy_failures += 1
        if not lossless_ok:
            lossless_failures += 1
        elif not policy_ok:
            special_token_drop += 1
    return {
        "policy_failures": policy_failures,
        "lossless_failures": lossless_failures,
        "special_token_drop": special_token_drop,
        "genuine_loss": lossless_failures,
        "note": (
            "tokenizers' decode() defaults to skip_special_tokens=True, so a "
            "registered special token present in the text is decoded away. "
            "With skip_special_tokens=False the text is reproduced exactly, "
            "which means the artifact is lossless and the difference is a "
            "decoding policy, not a tokenizer defect."
        ),
    }


def migration_plan(tokenizer, metrics: dict) -> dict:
    """Embedding and checkpoint implications of a larger vocabulary."""
    d_model = 256
    config_path = Path("configs/model/code_m3_9m.yaml")
    if config_path.is_file():
        try:
            import yaml

            d_model = int(
                (yaml.safe_load(config_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) or {})
                .get("model", {})
                .get("d_model", d_model)
            )
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - the default is used
            pass
    current_vocab = tokenizer.get_vocab_size()
    proposed_vocab = 32768
    current_embedding = current_vocab * d_model
    proposed_embedding = proposed_vocab * d_model
    return {
        "current_vocabulary": current_vocab,
        "proposed_vocabulary": proposed_vocab,
        "d_model": d_model,
        "current_embedding_parameters": current_embedding,
        "proposed_embedding_parameters": proposed_embedding,
        "embedding_parameter_delta": proposed_embedding - current_embedding,
        "training_data_requirement": (
            "Train the vocabulary on the pipeline's train split only, with the "
            "v1.1.0 control range reserved and unchanged. The holdouts and "
            "the benchmark screen must not contribute merges."
        ),
        "checkpoint_compatibility": (
            "Existing v1.0.0 and v1.1.0 checkpoints embed the 5,822-row table "
            "and cannot be loaded into a resized model. They stay servable "
            "through the legacy tokenizer artifact; the new tokenizer is a "
            "separate artifact with its own model rung."
        ),
        "migration_plan": [
            "v1.3.0 trains a new tokenizer artifact (for example "
            "qm_code_bpe_v1.json) from the v1.2.0 train split only.",
            "The reserved control range from v1.1.0 is preserved with the same "
            "ids, so the prompt contract does not change.",
            "A new model rung is configured with the larger vocabulary; the "
            "legacy rung and tokenizer remain loadable for existing "
            "checkpoints.",
            "Legacy checkpoints and the legacy tokenizer are never deleted or "
            "silently replaced.",
        ],
    }


def python_fragmentation_report(tokenizer, texts) -> dict:
    """Python-specific fragmentation measurements for the frozen tokenizer.

    Covers keywords, common identifiers, indentation, punctuation and long
    identifiers, plus the prompt-token inflation a Python prompt suffers from.
    The tokenizer is measured, never modified.
    """
    import keyword as _keyword

    keywords = sorted(_keyword.kwlist)
    keyword_costs = {
        word: len(tokenizer.encode(word, add_special_tokens=False).ids)
        for word in keywords
    }
    identifiers = [
        "def", "class", "return", "self", "value", "result", "handler",
        "process", "config", "request", "response", "iterator", "cache",
        "manager", "factory", "builder", "container", "collection",
    ]
    identifier_costs = {
        name: len(tokenizer.encode(name, add_special_tokens=False).ids)
        for name in identifiers
    }
    indentation = {
        "one_space": len(tokenizer.encode(" ", add_special_tokens=False).ids),
        "four_spaces": len(tokenizer.encode("    ", add_special_tokens=False).ids),
        "tab": len(tokenizer.encode("\t", add_special_tokens=False).ids),
        "newline": len(tokenizer.encode("\n", add_special_tokens=False).ids),
    }
    punctuation = {
        symbol: len(tokenizer.encode(symbol, add_special_tokens=False).ids)
        for symbol in ("(", ")", ":", ",", "=", ".", "->", "==", "_")
    }
    long_names = [
        "get_user_by_identifier",
        "compute_sharding_strategy_for_partition",
        "transform_configuration_payload",
    ]
    long_costs = {
        name: len(tokenizer.encode(name, add_special_tokens=False).ids)
        for name in long_names
    }
    characters = sum(len(text) for text in texts)
    tokens = sum(
        len(tokenizer.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False).ids) for text in texts
    )
    return {
        "samples": len(texts),
        "characters": characters,
        "tokens": tokens,
        "characters_per_token": round(characters / tokens, 4) if tokens else None,
        "keywords_total": len(keywords),
        "keywords_single_token": sum(
            1 for cost in keyword_costs.values() if cost == 1
        ),
        "keyword_fragmentation_share": round(
            1 - (sum(1 for cost in keyword_costs.values() if cost == 1) / len(keywords)),
            4,
        ),
        "identifiers_total": len(identifier_costs),
        "identifiers_single_token": sum(
            1 for cost in identifier_costs.values() if cost == 1
        ),
        "identifier_fragmentation_share": round(
            1 - (sum(1 for cost in identifier_costs.values() if cost == 1) / len(identifier_costs)),
            4,
        ),
        "indentation_tokens": indentation,
        "punctuation_tokens": punctuation,
        "long_identifier_tokens": long_costs,
        "unknown_token_id": tokenizer.token_to_id("<unk>"),
    }


def build_report(tokenizer_path, texts, *, label: str = "python source sample") -> dict:
    """Measure the tokenizer and produce the suitability report."""
    from tokenizers import Tokenizer

    from data.python_v1.registry import file_sha256

    path = Path(tokenizer_path)
    tokenizer = Tokenizer.from_file(str(path))
    metrics = analyse_texts(tokenizer, texts, source_label=label)

    derived = build_contract_tokenizer(path)
    control_metrics = analyse_texts(derived, texts, source_label=label + " (control tokens)")

    verdict, reasons = decide(metrics)
    regression = control_metrics["tokens_per_character"] - metrics["tokens_per_character"]
    failures = classify_roundtrip_failures(tokenizer, texts)
    report = {
        "schema": "quantsmind.tokenizer_suitability/1",
        "tokenizer": {
            "path": path.as_posix(),
            "sha256": file_sha256(path),
            "vocab_size": tokenizer.get_vocab_size(),
            "contract_id": CONTRACT_V1,
        },
        "control_token_derivation": {
            "contract_id": CONTRACT_V2,
            "vocab_size": derived.get_vocab_size(),
            "fertility_delta_tokens_per_character": regression,
            "note": (
                "The v1.1.0 control range appends six single-token markers and "
                "retrains no merge, so fertility must not regress."
            ),
        },
        "metrics": metrics,
        "round_trip": failures,
        "corpus_guard": {
            "rule": "reserved token spellings are excluded from the corpus",
            "reserved_literals": list(RESERVED_LITERALS),
            "reason": (
                "A reserved spelling in ordinary text is encoded as the "
                "reserved id. For the v1.1.0 control range that is a role "
                "marker, so such a file would forge a role boundary in the "
                "qm.chat_instruction/2 renderer. The pipeline excludes these "
                "files (reason code reserved_token_literal) rather than "
                "rewriting them."
            ),
            "measured_files_with_reserved_literals": metrics.get(
                "reserved_literal_files", 0
            ),
            "measured_occurrences": metrics.get("reserved_literal_occurrences", 0),
        },
        "baseline": {
            "byte_level_fallback_bytes_per_token": 1.0,
            "note": (
                "A byte-level fallback costs one token per UTF-8 byte. "
                "bytes_per_token is therefore the compression factor against "
                "that baseline. No external tokenizer was downloaded or "
                "compared."
            ),
        },
        "decision": {
            "verdict": verdict,
            "reasons": reasons,
            "thresholds": {
                "accepted_min_characters_per_token": ACCEPTED_MIN_CHARS_PER_TOKEN,
                "migration_max_identifier_fragmentation": (
                    MIGRATION_MAX_IDENTIFIER_FRAGMENTATION
                ),
                "migration_min_characters_per_token": MIGRATION_MIN_CHARS_PER_TOKEN,
                "insufficient_min_samples": INSUFFICIENT_MIN_SAMPLES,
                "insufficient_min_bytes": INSUFFICIENT_MIN_BYTES,
                "status": (
                    "engineering defaults with stated thresholds; not claimed "
                    "to be empirically optimal, because no sweep was run"
                ),
            },
        },
        "limitations": [
            "the sample is a bounded slice of one local corpus; it is not a "
            "representative sample of Python on the public internet",
            "no external or modern tokenizer was downloaded for comparison, so "
            "the report is a self-measurement, not a competitive benchmark",
            "thresholds are engineering defaults, not the result of a sweep",
            "identifier fragmentation counts tokens, not whether the split is "
            "semantically harmful",
            "the reserved-literal rate in this repository is inflated by the "
            "repository's own subject matter: its code contains literal "
            "special-token strings far more often than general Python does",
        ],
    }
    report["migration_plan"] = dict(
        migration_plan(tokenizer, metrics),
        triggered_by_gates=(verdict == "TOKENIZER_MIGRATION_RECOMMENDED"),
        note=(
            "This plan is an input to the owner's vocabulary decision (D6). "
            "v1.2.0 does not retrain, resize or replace any tokenizer, and a "
            "larger vocabulary would not fix the reserved-literal injection "
            "risk, which is handled corpus-side."
        ),
    )
    return report


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Measure Python suitability of the Taksh tokenizer"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--tokenizer", default="tokenizer/qm_code_bpe_v0.json")
    parser.add_argument("--source-dir", default=None, help="local tree of Python files")
    parser.add_argument("--jsonl", default=None, help="JSONL corpus with a text field")
    parser.add_argument("--max-files", type=int, default=200)
    parser.add_argument("--max-bytes", type=int, default=2_000_000)
    parser.add_argument("--out", default=None, help="write the report here (optional)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.jsonl:
        texts = collect_jsonl_texts(
            args.jsonl, max_samples=args.max_files, max_bytes=args.max_bytes
        )
        label = f"{args.jsonl}"
    elif args.source_dir:
        texts = collect_python_sources(
            args.source_dir, max_files=args.max_files, max_bytes=args.max_bytes
        )
        label = f"{args.source_dir} (**.py)"
    else:
        parser.error("one of --source-dir or --jsonl is required")
        return 2

    report = build_report(args.tokenizer, texts, label=label)
    rendered = json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    if args.out:
        Path(args.out).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        Path(args.out).write_text(rendered + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(rendered)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

"""Tokenizer control-token contract for ``qm.chat_instruction/2`` (v1.1.0).

The v1.0.0 tokenizers register only ``<bos>`` and ``<eos>``. A chat contract built
on those two markers cannot say *who* is speaking, so the model is asked to infer
turn structure from prose. Worse, any renderer that writes ``<|system|>`` into the
text gets byte fragments back, because the marker is not a token.

This module makes the reserved range explicit and checkable:

* :data:`CONTROL_TOKENS` is the reserved set (system, user, assistant,
  end-of-turn, tool, fill-in-the-middle). Each must encode to exactly one id.
* :func:`build_contract_tokenizer` derives a v2 tokenizer from an existing
  artifact by **appending** the control tokens. No BPE merges are retrained and
  no existing id changes, so the derivation is deterministic and auditable.
* :func:`detect_contract` reports which contract a tokenizer can serve. It never
  guesses: an unregistered marker means the tokenizer cannot serve v2.
* :func:`tokenizer_fingerprint` hashes the serialized tokenizer, so a checkpoint
  can bind the exact tokenizer it was trained with.

Scope note: v1.1.0 reserves and validates these tokens; shipping a v2 tokenizer
artifact and resizing embeddings for the S2 rung belongs to v1.2.0/v1.3.0.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from pathlib import Path

CONTRACT_V1 = "qm.plain_instruction/1"
CONTRACT_V2 = "qm.chat_instruction/2"

#: Reserved single-token markers, in a fixed order. Appending them in this order
#: is what makes derived tokenizers byte-reproducible.
CONTROL_TOKENS = (
    "<|system|>",
    "<|user|>",
    "<|assistant|>",
    "<|end_of_turn|>",
    "<|tool|>",
    "<|fim|>",
)

BOS = "<bos>"
EOS = "<eos>"


class TokenizerContractError(RuntimeError):
    """The tokenizer cannot represent the requested prompt contract."""


def contract_ids(tokenizer) -> dict[str, int] | None:
    """Return ``{marker: id}`` if every control token is a single registered token.

    ``None`` means this tokenizer does not support contract v2. Partial
    registration is treated as unsupported: a half-marked vocabulary is more
    dangerous than an obviously legacy one.
    """
    resolved: dict[str, int] = {}
    for marker in CONTROL_TOKENS:
        token_id = tokenizer.token_to_id(marker)
        if token_id is None:
            return None
        # A registered token must decode back to itself; otherwise it is an alias
        # that would render as different text than it encodes.
        if tokenizer.id_to_token(int(token_id)) != marker:
            return None
        resolved[marker] = int(token_id)
    return resolved


def detect_contract(tokenizer) -> str:
    """Return the strongest contract this tokenizer can serve, or raise."""
    if contract_ids(tokenizer) is not None:
        return CONTRACT_V2
    if tokenizer.token_to_id(BOS) is not None and tokenizer.token_to_id(EOS) is not None:
        return CONTRACT_V1
    raise TokenizerContractError(
        "tokenizer registers neither the v2 control tokens nor the legacy "
        "<bos>/<eos> pair; no prompt contract can be rendered without shredding "
        "markers into byte fragments"
    )


def require_contract(tokenizer, contract_id: str) -> dict[str, int] | None:
    """Verify that ``tokenizer`` can serve ``contract_id``; return its marker ids."""
    available = detect_contract(tokenizer)
    if contract_id == CONTRACT_V2:
        ids = contract_ids(tokenizer)
        if ids is None:
            raise TokenizerContractError(
                f"contract {contract_id} requires single-token control markers "
                f"{list(CONTROL_TOKENS)}; the tokenizer is only {available}"
            )
        return ids
    if contract_id == CONTRACT_V1:
        if tokenizer.token_to_id(BOS) is None or tokenizer.token_to_id(EOS) is None:
            raise TokenizerContractError(
                f"contract {contract_id} requires <bos>/<eos> single tokens"
            )
        return None
    raise TokenizerContractError(f"unknown prompt contract: {contract_id!r}")


def build_contract_tokenizer(source: str | Path, *, verify: bool = True):
    """Derive a contract-v2 tokenizer from ``source`` without retraining.

    The source artifact is copied, then the control tokens are appended as
    special tokens. Existing ids are untouched. The result is deterministic:
    the same input artifact and tokenizer library version produce the same
    serialized bytes and therefore the same fingerprint.
    """
    from tokenizers import Tokenizer

    tok = Tokenizer.from_file(str(source))
    if contract_ids(tok) is None:
        tok.add_special_tokens(list(CONTROL_TOKENS))
    if verify:
        ids = contract_ids(tok)
        if ids is None:
            raise TokenizerContractError(
                "derived tokenizer still lacks single-token control markers"
            )
        for marker in CONTROL_TOKENS:
            enc = tok.encode(marker, add_special_tokens=False)
            if enc.ids != [ids[marker]]:
                raise TokenizerContractError(
                    f"{marker} does not encode to exactly one id: {enc.ids}"
                )
    return tok


def tokenizer_fingerprint(tokenizer) -> str:
    """SHA-256 of the serialized tokenizer (the artifact serving must match)."""
    return hashlib.sha256(tokenizer.to_str().encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def tokenizer_file_fingerprint(path: str | Path) -> str:
    """SHA-256 of a tokenizer file on disk, byte for byte."""
    return hashlib.sha256(Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
